### Entry 73 — C4: the first reader — the next sight-reading phrase chosen from what the learner's reads have shown, one dimension at a time, never one already played, one in four easy on purpose, and a reason line that says only what was measured (2026-09-26)

**Judgement.** Yes for the eight items, with one behaviour change said up front and nine deviations below. **What a learner now gets tomorrow**, on rung 2.2, from five realistic reads each (the rung's own row generated, played through the real engine at the default 70 %, evidenced with the row's skills, stored as the Score screen stores it):

- **Never read:** *One phrase you have never seen, once, slowly* — the rung's row (`sight-reading-2-right`: right hand, eighths, skips, C4–C5) as it stands. No reason is claimed; there is no evidence.
- **Misread every skip on the last two days** (15/15, 21/21, 15/15, then 14/21, 14/20 right and in time): *This one in C position — 14 of 20 right and in time yesterday* — the same row held inside C4–G4, eighths and skips kept. One dimension (range) down.
- **Read the eighths cleanly every day** (21/21 … 23/23): *Now with both hands — 23 of 23 right and in time yesterday* — the same row with the left hand holding whole-note roots under it. One dimension (hands) up; a key would need 3.1, 6/8 or syncopation 4.5, so neither is offered.

Until today all three got the same thing: the stage rule's level-1 left-hand row (`item.level <= stageNumber`), the same every day for the whole of Stage 2, whatever they read. **What I looked at on the glass** (built app, `vite preview`, 342 × 740, light, desktop Chromium; pictures in the scratch folder `glass/`): Today for the three learners above; and three mornings of the thirty-day learner (days 3, 6 and 22 of `DIARY.md`, their stored rows restored as a backup) — the card (*Now with both hands — 15 of 15 right and in time yesterday*; *This one right hand only — 10 of 14 right and in time yesterday*; *Now in G major — 12 of 12 right and in time yesterday*), the phrase ▶ opened (two hands in C; right hand in C; two hands in G, one sharp), the sheet after a run played in time over the MIDI mock, the row it stored (its recipe, seed, `unseen: true`, and four evidence results), and the card after it (*Read today — tomorrow's phrase is new*). The daily card's reason used to be cut to "…" at this width — the old sentence as well as the new; it takes a second line now. Nothing was heard, and no musical judgement here is more than a reading of the notation.

**The checkpoint's question** — does the app teach reading better than on 2026-09-25, or is it only more careful about what it claims? Better in sequencing, from the diary and the pictures: the phrase is the rung's (eighths on the eighths rung, not two notes in the bass), it gets harder only after two clean days, easier after two bad ones, one read in four is easy on purpose, keys arrive when 3.1 teaches them, and no phrase is ever one already played. **Not** better in diagnosis: the evidence is per skill, so a learner who misreads skips (diary days 3–6) had the left hand taken away — the last thing added — not skips practised; the line can say *14 of 20*, never *the skips*. And the phrases themselves are the same generator's (day 3's opened with four C4s in a row), which is D's.

**Behaviour change, said up front: day one.** The brief says a learner with no evidence "starts where the rung's row starts". The stage rule and the reader part on thirteen of the core rungs (the reader gives the row of the latest rung reached that lists one). Measured on the built content, learner with no reads, core track: 1.3 and 1.4 get `1-left` (the stage rule gave `1`, 1.5's skips, two rungs early — S16's second half); 2.1 gets `1`; 2.2–2.5 get `2-right` (was `1-left`); 3.4–3.6 get `2` (was `2-right`); 4.5–4.7 get `3` (was `2`). 0.x, 1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 3.1–3.3 and 4.1–4.4 are unchanged. Lesson 3.4 described the old rule and was rewritten (deviation 4).

**Deviations, each with its reason.**
1. **`router.ts`** (not named): `?recipe=hands:both,fifths:1,easy:1`, parsed key by key, written in one order, compared by value. The recipe has to ride the route as the seed does: *New phrase*, Blind and a reload must write the same kind of phrase, and the run must store the recipe it was. Recomputing it on the Score screen would disagree with Today the moment the run is stored.
2. **`db.ts`: `recipe` beside `evidence`** (the brief named the evidence field only; its judgement line allows the last recipe "on the observation"): one optional header field, `ReadingMoves` and `ReadingRecipe` beside it; no store, index or version changed.
3. **`style.css`**, one rule: `.list-row__sub.today-reason { white-space: normal }`. The daily card's reason was cut after about thirty characters at 342 px (seen on the glass, the old sentence too); the card's title is one line and it has no Swap, so a two-line reason keeps it inside R2. Every other Today reason is still one line, cut (P3).
4. **`content/lessons/3.4.md`**, one sentence: it said the daily read "at this stage is a right-hand phrase at level 2 … The two-hand phrase becomes the daily read at Stage 4" — the stage rule. Rewritten to what the reader does at 3.4: "starts from this rung's two-hand phrase at level 2 and changes one thing at a time from what your reads show — its key, or how far it ranges — never to something a lesson has not taught yet". The claims row that re-implemented the stage rule is deleted as briefed; the claims file's rule (a sentence about the app has a row) gets a row for the new sentence, calling the real reader. Content rebuilt.
5. **Item 6's code is in `ScoreScreen.fillSidePanel`**: the brief named `tablet.ts`, which holds no panel text. The pure function (`sidePanelProse`) is in `tablet.ts`; the screen calls it.
6. **Titles where the recipe moved the hands** (`readingTitle`, `help.ts`): the Score screen's header and Today's reading row said "…, level 2, right hand" over a two-hand phrase. A row named for one hand whose recipe added the other drops the hand; one named for neither says the hand the recipe took away. Today's reading row's `RH`/`LH` follows the recipe too.
7. **`sightReading.ts`: one generator parameter, `position`** (the brief's "only if a recipe field is needed"): the melody inside the five notes from the key's tonic, whatever the level's range. Without it the range dimension could only be moved by changing the level, which moves rhythms and leaps with it. Default absent, so every golden and every row's phrase is unchanged. `maxFifthsFor(level)` is exported so a key move is one the level writes.
8. **The transposition drills leave the reading slot**: they carry the `sight-reading` tag and open on the Drill screen; the slot is the reader's phrase now.
9. **Before any rung that lists a reading row the slot has none** (as at 0.x–1.2 before) while the daily read keeps the easiest row there (as before): one function, `anchored: false`, and the slot's stated condition on it.

## Done — per item: mechanism, the red line, before → after

**0. The reading state; evidence at record time (S14 in part).** *Mechanism:* C3's `evidenceFor` needs the played model, which exists only while the Score screen holds the phrase (verified by the orchestrator; on the committed tree `evidenceFor` is called in `app/src` only by the Score screen's sheet, for its *Not judged* lines — nothing turned rows into evidence). *Change:* the screen computes the results once, where it builds the run (`evidenceOf`), uses them for the sheet's *Not judged* lines and stores them on the row (`SessionRow.evidence`; a self-reported run's evidence is computed from the answered run); the stamp is the row's own `definitions`. `evidence/readingState.ts`: `storedEvidence(row)` (nothing without a current stamp, nothing re-derived; each record dated by its row) and `readingState(rows, vocabulary, today)` — the reading strand (every skill but the technique `position-shift`), one `ladderState` reading per skill with the evidence behind it. *Red:* `a recorded sight-read kept no evidence: expected undefined to be defined`; `the row kept no refusal for the timing Wait never took: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'sight-reading', 'subdivision' ]`; `Failed to resolve import "../../src/evidence/readingState"`. *After:* the row carries evidence and refusals (on the glass: `sight-reading 16/16, interval-reading 11/11, subdivision 6/6, position-shift refused no-opportunity`); three realistic learners read into three states (below). The evidence call costs a small fraction of what the screen already spends building the phrase's model — about a twenty-fifth for a four-bar right-hand phrase and a sixtieth for an eight-bar two-hand one (jsdom, this machine, medians of twelve) — and the sheet already made it since C3; it is made once now and used twice. Not measured on the phone.

**1. The reading slot and the daily read (S4, L12 reading part).** *Mechanism:* `dailyItemFor` (`TodayScreen`) took the hardest reading row with `item.level <= stageNumber`; the slot (`session.ts`) took `pick(pool, seed + slotIndex)` over rows at or below the stage plus the rung's own. *Change:* one function, `readingOffer` (`session.ts`), for both: the row is the reading row of the latest rung reached on the active tracks (curriculum order, no stage number); the working recipe is the learner's last at that row (`SessionRow.recipe`; an easy read is a detour); its block is the reads at it since arriving. Sight-reading's stored evidence (right notes in time, every step) decides: the last two against → one dimension **down** (undo the newest addition, else range, then hands); proficient over the block by the ladder's rule and the read before not an easy one → one dimension **up** (the demands the rung has taught, earliest taught first, not a skill failing elsewhere); else the same recipe. Dimensions (`READING_DIMENSIONS`): hands, range, rhythm, key, metre, syncopation, each one generator parameter, spelled as `drill.params` so `readingOptions(item, recipe, seed)` is the one writer of a phrase for Today, the Score screen and the tests. Today opens the offer with `?seed=&recipe=&rung=&slot=`; C3's `rungForSlot` and route are kept. *Red:* `TypeError: readingOptions is not a function` (the reader's file, on import); `the never-read learner has no reading row: expected undefined to be defined`; renumbering the stages on the committed slot: `expected 'drill.reading.sight-reading-4' to be 'drill.reading.sight-reading-1'`; the slot at 2.2: `expected 'drill.reading.sight-reading-1' to be 'drill.reading.sight-reading-2-right'`; router `expected undefined to deeply equal { Object (moved, easy) }`; the screen `the screen wrote the row's own phrase over the recipe the route named`, `expected undefined to deeply equal { Object (row) }`. *After:* the three learners above; renumbered stages change nothing; every other slot identical for a failing and a never-read learner.

**2. Unseen is guaranteed (S13).** *Mechanism:* a fresh open and *New phrase* drew `Math.random` seeds, avoiding only the phrase on the screen; nothing checked the record before drawing. *Change:* the Score screen reads the item's stored runs before it draws a seed for itself and never draws one on the record (`freshSeed(avoid)`); *New phrase* avoids those and the current one, and keeps the recipe. The slot's seed is the day's own stream (`dailySeed(day + '#reading')` stepped by Shuffle) past any seed on the row's record; the daily read keeps the day's seed (it ticks the day), and once today's phrase is on the record the card says *Read today — tomorrow's phrase is new* (or *Heard before it was read …*) instead of offering it as never seen. *Red:* `a new phrase was one already on the record: expected [ 111, 222 ] to not include 111`; `a fresh open drew a phrase already on the record: expected 111 not to be 111`. *After:* thirty days, every phrase offered off the record (`firstThirtyDays`).

**3. The easy band (S13).** `EASY_AFTER = 3`: after three reads that were not easy, the next is one dimension below the recipe — the step a failing read would get — flagged `easy` on the recipe and the route, and the line says *An easy one, for fluency: right hand only*. No move up on the read after an easy one, so from one day's phrase to the next never more than one dimension changes. Where nothing sits below (1.3's row; 1.5's before a move) there is none. *After:* within four reads in the twelve-read follow; seven easy reads in the diary's thirty.

**4. The reason line (I1, design §11 item 4).** `READING_TEXT`, `readingReason`, `readingChange` in `help.ts`, printed in `04` §2 (a test holds the two together): what the phrase changes first, then the last read's measurement — *Now with both hands — 23 of 23 right and in time yesterday*. It never names a demand (the evidence is per skill: "you misread two of five skips" is not something it knows), never says "reading" is shown (Entry 72: sight-reading is right notes in time, not reading ahead), and where no evidence chose the phrase it is the rung's old words. Change-first because the session card cuts a reason to one line at 342 px, and what the phrase is must survive the cut. *Red:* the e2e on a build of the committed source, `Expected: "Yesterday: 11 of 16 right and in time — this one in C position" Received: "One phrase you have never seen, once, slowly"` (the words were reordered after that run; the committed build prints the rung's sentence whatever the words); the length on the glass: `the reason is cut off on the glass: Expected: false Received: true` (before the CSS rule).

**5. The old rule's tests.** `lessonClaimsAboutApp` "3.4: the daily read is the right-hand level-2 phrase at Stage 3 and the two-hand one at Stage 4" deleted (it re-implemented the stage rule; class delete); `sightReadingSlot` revised (the stage rule's four Stage 1–2 claims kept as the floor, the evidence rule added). `sightReadingPromises` preserved and green.

**6. The side panel from nowhere (U47).** *Mechanism:* `fillSidePanel` drew the judging rung, else the first rung listing the piece, whole — including its *How you'll know you've got it* paragraph, the rung's pass, beside a run held to the Settings pair (C1). *Change:* whole for the judging rung; from nowhere, the first listing rung's teaching without that one paragraph (every lesson has exactly one, `lessonShape`; a sweep of the other paragraphs finds percentages in four lessons, 0.3's being the Settings default pair and the rest instructions or practice advice). *Red:* `TypeError: sidePanelProse is not a function`; e2e `the panel quotes a pass the run is not held to … Expected substring: not "How you'll know you've got it"`.

**7. Nothing else adapts.** Technique, review, new, repertoire and jam fill as they did (asserted for two learners); Skills, the swap sheet and the stores untouched.

**The brief's hypotheses, answered.**
1. *The evidence call is cheap* — yes, as a relationship: a small fraction of the screen's own model build for the same phrase (item 0). Not timed against the sheet's DOM build, which I did not isolate; not measured on the phone.
2. *Ladder states are distinguishable on a few days* — yes. Five realistic reads each: never read — every reading skill *not introduced*; misread the skips on the last two days — *sight-reading* and *reading by interval* **familiar** (proficient by day 2, down after two full-standard reads against on the same row); clean — *sight-reading* and *subdivision* **proficient** (no transfer: one row). Caveats: the misread learner's state does not say "skips"; subdivision evidence exists only below about nine tenths of 72 bpm (C3's precision rule), so a clean reader at full tempo has none.
3. *Promises and one-dimension moves do not conflict* — two conflicts found by reading twelve phrases each way with the detectors, and resolved by fixing the dimension, not breaking the promise: level 4's promised accidental was missing from one of twelve phrases in G, and one of twelve in 6/8. Per rung, what the reader can move (taught-at applied): 1.3, 1.4 (`1-left`) nothing — the bass clef in C position is the promise, and the reason says *The next step waits for a later lesson*; 1.5–2.1 (`1`) the left hand; 2.2–2.5 (`2-right`) both hands up, C position down; 3.1–3.3 the same and the key (G, F); 3.4–4.4 (`2`) the key up, the range down; 4.5–4.7 (`3`) the key up, hands and range down; technique.5 (`4`) syncopation up only, and nothing below (no easy read); theory.6 onward (`5`–`7`) nothing. What each move brings is measured and listed (adding the left hand at level 2 also brings the bass staff and its roots' leaps; 6/8 brings dotted quarters and eighths; the designed syncopation brings eighths), and the taught-at gate checks all of it.
4. *The rows are what their rungs say* — the moves do not depend on S16 or S22. `2-right` on 2.2 still writes past C position as the row's own (C2's `KNOWN_EARLY`); C position is a step down the reader can take, not a fix. 3.4's row still writes no ledger note (S22); ledger range is not a dimension below level 4. Both stay D's.

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code, the diary and the pictures; nothing heard)

Read as a practice diary (`DIARY.md`), the month is a teacher's shape in outline: the rung's phrase, another like it, the left hand added after two clean days, one easy phrase in four, a step back after two bad days, keys when keys are taught. Three things a teacher would not say. (1) Days 3–6: the learner misread skips; the app took the left hand away and then held the right-hand phrase — it cannot see that the skips were the trouble. (2) Days 11–20 on 2.5: nothing to move for ten days (ties and dotted quarters are taught at 2.4 but the generator ties them to higher levels), so the line reads *The next step waits for a later lesson* four times; true, and flat. (3) *Now in F major* after G is a new key, not a harder one; the line says "now", which is accurate but reads as progress. The reason lines are honest and plain; they tell the learner what changed and one number, not what to watch for. Whether the phrases read as music is unverified as music: the one on day 3 opened with four C4s.

- **P1 (C3 gap, the evidence function):** `right` per demand, not only per skill, would let the reader and the line act on the weakness a read showed (skips, a ledger note, the left hand) — the diary's misread week is the case.
- **P2 (C6):** at Shuffle 0 on 2.2 the warm-up slot takes the rung's reading row (its first exercise option), so the card has no reading slot and the warm-up opens the row on its own recipe.
- **P2 (evidence version):** the stamp is the observation's `definitions`; a change to the vocabulary or the evidence function must move it too, or stored evidence reads as current (`01` §4.5). An evidence version of its own would decouple them.
- **P2 (D):** levels bundle dimensions the reader cannot move alone — dotted quarters and ties (taught 2.4), ledger lines (3.4), a second accidental in the key at level 2 — so 2.5 and 3.1–3.3 run out of moves.
- **P2 (D, S10):** the reading run is judged by the rung's tempo floor, so a perfect read at the default 70 % is headed *Run finished* (seen on all three sheets).
- **P2:** a learner who reads with the keys guide on earns practice-standard evidence only and never moves up; the line says *Another like it* without saying why.
- **P2:** unseen is guaranteed over what is recorded; a phrase heard and left unplayed is not recorded (as `04` §2 already says, not closed). The day's seed could equal a seed on the record only by a 32-bit hash coincidence; not guarded.

### Entry 74 — T42: the tempo ladder holds on a pass nothing judged and says so, and the test that relied on the old fault misses under a judging input (2026-09-26)

**Judgement.** Yes for the three decided items. **On the glass** (the build with the change, desktop Chromium, light, Hot Cross Buns, bar 1 looped, the ladder on at 40 %, input *None*, two pass boundaries): the status line reads *Nothing listening — staying at 40 %*, the slider stays at 40 and the notes stay black. At 1180 × 920 it sits in the header beside *bar 1 / 4* while the loop runs. At 390 × 844 the header is folded away while the run goes (pre-existing, every ladder line alike — Follow-ups), so the learner meets the line after a tap brings the chrome back: *Hot Cross B… Nothing listening — staying at 40 %* at the top right. At 342 × 740 after a tap it is shown whole (its box is as wide as its text; the title gives way to *Hot …*). **Mechanism, traced on the committed build** (not only inferred from the slider): the hold case's recorder, installed before ▶, caught the committed screen writing *Clean — up to 50 %* and *Clean — up to 60 %* at the first two pass boundaries. `climbLadder` judges a pass clean when the engine's miss, wrong and early totals have not moved since the last lap; since C3 a run with no input counts no miss (`judging: false`), so every lap read as clean and the ladder climbed notch by notch to `LADDER_CEILING_PCT`. The CI failure reproduces locally on the same build with the old test: `Expected: "30"`, `Received: "100"`. So the mechanism is the one the brief inferred. Before C3 the same comparison walked down on misses nobody made (L44).

Not heard; nothing here is about sound. A teacher's read: if the app cannot hear you it should not tell you to go faster or slower, and now it does neither and says why in six words. The line does not say how to be heard; the sheet at the end does (*connect a piano or choose Screen keys in ⋯*).

**Deviations, each with its reason.**
1. **The misses case plays one note.** The brief suggested the screen keys with no key pressed, or the MIDI mock silent. Either one holds the run for ever: a Keep tempo run with an input holds at the start for the learner's first note (`05` §3b), so no pass would ever end. The revised case presses the note the run is holding for (read from `scoreRun().expected`, not written into the test) and then nothing, so pass 1 has two misses and every later pass has three. That is what a learner who starts and then keeps missing gets.
2. **`LADDER_TEXT` holds the whole ladder line, not only the new sentence.** One line with three verdicts is one set of words in `help.ts`. The *Clean* and *A mistake* strings moved out of `ScoreScreen.ts` unchanged, and the existing floor and ceiling cases hold them.
3. **`listening()` replaces `input !== 'none'` on C3's `judging:` line.** The hold and the run's `judging` read one fact, so they cannot come apart. An input change restarts the run, so at a lap it is still the input the lap was judged by. Nothing in `ScoreSession.ts` changed: the screen owns the input, as Entry 72's deviation 1 argued, and the session reading its options back would restate the engine's rule a second time.

## Done — per item: mechanism, the red line, before → after

**1. The ladder holds on an unjudged pass (Q33, P1).** *Change:* in `climbLadder`, after the pass base is updated, `if (!listening())` writes `LADDER_TEXT.line(LADDER_TEXT.nothingListening, tempoPct, tempoPct)`, renders and returns: no tempo change up or down, no restart, the lap the engine has begun runs on. `Hear it` keeps its own earlier guard. The record path is untouched. A loop run is still recorded at its summary, and with nothing heard that summary is T40's *Not measured* sheet, recorded with the learner's answer (read from the code, not driven here). *Red:* `the ladder moved the tempo on a pass nothing judged … + "Clean — up to 50 %", + "Clean — up to 60 %"`. *After:* no line moved the tempo, the slider reads 40 after two passes, and the status line reads *Nothing listening — staying at 40 %*.

**2. The misses case revised (class: revise; old assumption: no input means every note is missed).** Screen keys, the first note played to start the clock, nothing after it. It now asserts *A mistake — staying at 30 %*, so a hold at the floor cannot pass for a walk down. *Red:* it passes on the committed build, because the screen keys judge there as well. Reverting the engine's `judging` guard cannot make it red either: with a judging input that guard never acts. It was seen red on a copy of the committed build with `judging` forced off for every input, spliced into the built bundle so the shared tree was not built: `Expected: "30"`, `Received: "40"`. With judging off the engine's `feed` returns before the latch, so the run holds for its first note for ever. That is the revised test failing because its input is not judging, the failure CI met in the old form (`Expected: "30"`, `Received: "100"`, reproduced locally on the committed build). *After:* green.

**3. The clean-pass case** already taps every step under the screen keys (a judging input, Rhythm only), so it did not rely on nothing being judged. Preserved, green.

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code and the pictures; nothing heard)

A hold is what a teacher would do. They would add that a ladder switched on with nothing listening is a control that can never act: the row could say so on its label, as the metronome row does in Free play (Follow-ups). The standing line under the header, *The count-in clicks, then play along.*, is the mode's default, and a no-input loop leaves it as it was.

## Follow-ups

- **P2 (pre-existing, every ladder line):** on an upright phone the header, and the status line in it, is `display: none` while the chrome is folded during a run. So *Clean — up to 70 %*, *A mistake — down to 50 %* and now *Nothing listening — staying at 40 %* are unseen until a tap, and the tempo label that `04` §5 marks as moving by itself is folded too. The corner chip shows only *bar n / m*. The learner hears the loop get faster with nothing on the glass saying why.

### Entry 75 — C4a: evidence per demand with the overlap between demands kept, three readings that name a demand only where the reads single it out, and the evidence's own version (2026-09-26)

**Judgement.** Yes for the brief's items 1–6, with the shape changed in one place (the overlap is derived rather than stored beside every entry, deviation 3, because the size hypothesis failed) and one finding about the tree that the orchestrator has to act on first: **the T42 commit (30c63e4) carries C4a's two Score screen lines** (the `stampedEvidence` import and the save line) **and C4a's §9b text, but not `app/src/evidence/`**, so HEAD on its own imports a `stampedEvidence` that HEAD's evidence module does not export. The working tree is whole (`tsc -b` 0); HEAD is whole again once C4a's files are committed.

**The skip learner, five first readings of 2.2's row** (`sight-reading-2-right`, generated, played through the real engine at 70 % with a reader's small unevenness, every skip read as the step below, evidenced as the Score screen does and stored with the stamp; `demandReadings.test.ts`). What C4 stored on day 4 was *sight-reading 14 of 21* and *reading by interval 10 of 17*. What the row stores now, for the same run: sight-reading's skips **0 of 7**, steps **10 of 10**, eighths 7 of 12, "shorter than a quarter" 7 of 12, beyond the five-finger position 2 of 2 — and, derived from where each demand is, that every wrong eighth was also a skip. What `demandReadings` reads over the five: misread on all five days, skips 0 of 26, below the support share in five phrases, and **`pattern`** under sight-reading and under reading by interval — where no eighth was, the skips went 0 of 9; where the skip was not beyond the position, 0 of 23; and every other demand held where no skip was (steps 52 of 52, eighths 31 of 31, beyond the position 7 of 7). Steps: 52 of 52, not named. The eighths: 31 of 48, below in five phrases, **not** named — where no skip was they went 31 of 31, and the skips went wrong without them. Three good days then two misread: after the first bad day nothing is named (skips below in one phrase, their wrong steps mostly shared with eighths); **after the second, skips are a `pattern`** (13 of 26; 5 of 9 where no eighth was) and nothing else is. That answers C4c's inherited question: the pattern is there by the second bad day.

**One wrong note with four properties** (the left hand's F♯3 in G major: a skip, an eighth, the bass staff, the key signature, under the right hand's held note): sight-reading keeps that step as wrong under every demand on it ("shorter than a quarter" too) and every demand's reading is **`ambiguous`**, on one day and on two — the skip was never read without the eighth (0 of 0), so repetition cannot separate them.

**The mixed-demand ambiguity adversary**, both profiles (the coordinator's addition; the brief carried one half). Two phrases whose wrong notes are all skips and eighths at once: skips 0 of 16, eighths 0 of 16, the same sixteen steps; both **`ambiguous`**, and so is reading by interval's skip. Then (a) skips in quarters read right and steps in eighths read wrong: the eighths become a **`pattern`** (2 of 24; 2 of 8 where no skip was, 2 of 18 where no step was; skips 4 of 4 and steps 15 of 15 where no eighth was) and the skips do not (4 of 20, but 4 of 4 where no eighth was). (b) skips in quarters right and eighths in steps right: **both stay `ambiguous`** (eighths 8 of 8 where no skip was, skips 4 of 4 where no eighth was): the failures were at the combination, and nothing is named, isolated or patterned anywhere.

**What a teacher can now see that Entry 73's `n, right` hid**: which notes went wrong (the skips, every one), which held (every step), that the wrong eighths were the skips and not the rhythm, and whether the reads have separated the two yet. The evidence still says only "right and in time under these conditions" at each demand's notes; nothing on it names a cause. Not heard; no screen changed (the sheet and Today read what they read before); not looked at on the glass (no browser, as briefed). Whether the phrases are music is unchanged from Entry 73 and unverified as music.

**Deviations, each with its reason.**
1. **A skill read over every step counts every demand its steps contain.** The brief says "each demand in the skill's opportunity list"; sight-reading's list is *every step*. Without this the reader's own skill (C4c acts on sight-reading) would have no per-demand evidence, and the ambiguity adversary could not exist: under reading by interval a wrong pitch is a skip failure and under subdivision it is no timing at all, so only a skill that judges pitch and timing as one outcome sees the eighth and the skip fall together.
2. **The overlap names every vocabulary demand on the steps, in the hands played**, not only the declared skills'. Hiding a co-located demand because no declared skill names it would make a mixed failure look isolated — the false specificity the reviewer warned of.
3. **The overlap is derived, not stored per entry** (`overlapOf(evidence, demand, vocabulary)`; per result `otherDemands` for the demands a skill with a list does not count). Stored beside every entry, the evidence of a sight-read was about three times its bare observation for a four-bar one-hand phrase and five for an eight-bar two-hand one, and compaction keeps it. Each (demand, step) is now stored once (a test holds it): about twice the bare observation for both.
4. **Each entry also keeps `wrong` and, where needed, `unattributed`.** The readings need which steps went wrong; a demand on some notes of a chord partly wrong cannot be told (C1 keeps the code, not which pitch was missed, L56), so the step is out of that demand's `n` and said — the brief's "n over what can be told". `StepMeasure.uniform` (in `measurement.ts`) marks the verdicts that hold for every pitch (`h`, `m`), so a demand on one note of a chord all missed is still told.
5. **`demandReadings` in its own file** (`evidence/demandReadings.ts`), as the brief allowed; it reads `storedEvidence`.
6. **The stamp is a row field** (`SessionRow.evidenceDefinitions`, the brief's db.ts ownership), put on by one function (`stampedEvidence`) that the Score screen, `recomputeEvidence` and the test helper all use. The Score screen change is the save line and its import.
7. **`recomputeEvidence(row, played, vocabulary, targetSkills?)`**: the skills default to those the row's stored results name, since a pure function cannot look up the item; a caller whose item's declaration has changed passes them.
8. **Test helpers revised**: `helpers/observed.ts` gains `wrongKey` (a misread the engine cannot hold as an early strike of the next note) and `wrongPitch` (one hand of a chord); `helpers/reader.ts` stamps as the record call does, without which every C4 test built on it would have read nothing.
9. **§9b's first paragraph** said "Nothing selects by it yet (C4)", false since C4; corrected in the same targeted replacement.
10. **The poor-left-hand case has a two-read variant**: over two reads the bass staff is a `pattern` and playing together is not (the right hand held over the left, 4 of 4) — the fact C4c's "the left hand only when hands-together itself patterns" rule needs.

Per-demand counts and the overlap (L64, P1).** *Mechanism, confirmed in the code:* C3's `opportunitySteps` put every demand's steps into one set per skill and `evidenceFrom` counted the set; a skill read over every step never located a demand at all; so the stored evidence was `skill, n, right` and the reader could only back out its last move (Part 8's central finding). *The brief's first inherited hypothesis*: the per-demand steps were available only as that union; splitting needed every vocabulary demand's locations, not a second pass over the run. *Change:* one pass over the detectors per run (`locateDemands`, shared by the opportunity, the precision rule and the counts, where C3 ran them per skill), and `evidenceFrom` splits the same counted steps by demand (`byDemand: {demand, n, right, steps, wrong, unattributed?}`), with `otherDemands` and `overlapOf` for where the other demands are. The skill's `n` and `right`, the decision order, every refusal and its `cites`, and the self-assessed class are untouched; the ladder reads only `n` and `right`. *Red:* `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` (five cases), `(reading 'map')` (three), `TypeError: result.byDemand is not iterable`; the first build's per-entry overlap: `AssertionError: sight-reading: interval.step@2 is stored twice: expected true to be false`. *After:* the numbers above; the cost of the call is about the same as C3's on a four-bar one-hand phrase and under one and a half times on an eight-bar two-hand one, either a small fraction of building the phrase's model (jsdom, this machine, medians).

Demand readings.** `demandReadings(rows, vocabulary, today)`: per reading-strand skill and demand, over the skill's last five reads under the current stamp — `n`, `right`, phrases, phrases below, `below`, one of `pattern` / `isolated` / `ambiguous`, and `basis` (the arithmetic). The rules and the four constants (`DEMAND_WINDOW_READS` 5, `PATTERN_MIN_PHRASES` 2, `MIN_CONTRAST` 2, `MIN_ALONE_WRONG` 2) are printed in `05` §9b and marked hypotheses; "below" and "held" are relative to the ladder's support share. A *rival* is another skill's demand on a wrong step; demands one skill copes with (step, skip, leap; the eighth and "shorter than a quarter") are siblings, never rivals — "shorter than a quarter" is every eighth again — but are held to the selectivity rule. *Red:* `Error: Failed to resolve import "../../src/evidence/demandReadings" from "tests/unit/demandReadings.test.ts". Does the file exist?` *After:* the three worked examples above; two had to be looked at before they came out right: rivals are taken from every demand on the wrong steps, not only the skill's own (reading by interval's skip came out `pattern` in the adversary until then: `interval-reading interval.skip was named where the observations do not separate it: expected 'pattern' to be 'ambiguous'`), and "every other demand held where this one was absent" needs at least one such comparison, or a rhythm skill that sees only its own eighths would name them.

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code and the constructed reads; nothing heard)

The three facts read as a teacher would put them: "it's the skips — they go wrong in quarters too, and your steps are fine"; "one note went wrong; I can't tell you why from one note"; "those were all fast skips; I can't tell yet whether it's the skips or the speed" — and, after the contrasting reads, "it's the speed" or, in the reviewer's profile, "only when they come together". Two places a teacher would put it differently. "Shorter than a quarter" is named alongside the eighths whenever the eighths are (the same notes); a teacher says "the eighths" (C4c maps both to one control). And `ambiguous` covers both "held" and "fell together with something" — a demand going fine and a demand in a mixed failure get the same word, told apart by `below`; C4c must read both. Whether the thresholds are a teacher's is unverified: they are hypotheses tested on constructed learners who misread every skip, never on real playing.

**Deviations, each with its reason.**
1. **A sixth new option, `leaps`.** `interval.leap` is taught at 1.5 and had no control; the brief's principle ("new options where a taught demand has none") covers it.
2. **An "off" for every demand, and tri-state options.** The brief's map names the option that turns a demand on; C4c's brief steps down by turning a demand off ("skips off", "eighths off") and hopes to delete C4's table for this one. `true` promises, `false` keeps out, absent is the level's own; `skips`, `eighths`, `syncopation`, `triplets`, `accidentals` gained `false`; `position: false` promises a melody wider than one position. The contract found dotted quarters on 2.2's row at 2.4 leaving some phrase with no beamed pair, which 2.2's "eighths beamed in their beats" check reads as a broken promise; the check is kept, the phrase now keeps what it checks.
7. **S16 is fixed where the rung is known, not in the row.** Setting the row's own recipe in C position would make 2.5's lesson sentence ("its phrases already reach up to the C above middle C") false on this tree, since the committed reader cannot move range up from a row whose params hold it. The generator side is proven; the app asks for the held shape once `readingOptions` calls `heldToRung` (C4c).

## Pedagogical verdict (from the notation; nothing heard)

The contract makes the 2.5 plateau impossible on the generator's side and says honestly where the curriculum asks what the reader's row cannot give: 2.1 teaches hands together over a one-hand row; 1.5's song teaches the leap its drill forbids; 4.5's row cannot drop skips, leaps or eighths. Three things a teacher would not accept yet, each recorded, none fixed (D's): a tie can be followed by a fifth (seed 71282 on the right-hand row: A4 tied into bar 4, then E4; C4 tied into bar 2, then G4); the first left-hand pattern (3.6) arrives two octaves below middle C with ledger lines, two new things at once (seed 11: C2 G2 E2 G2 under C4); and the day-14 tie phrase's left hand holds C3 for four bars. Whether any phrase reads as music is unverified as music.

### Entry 77 — C4c: the demand-sensitive reader — a step down moves the control of the demand the reads single out, nothing is blamed where they single nothing out, a step up turns on the next demand the rung has taught, a key is named and never ranked; the phrase held to the rung that opens it; the thirty days and the mixed-demand learner run again (2026-09-27)

**Judgement.** Yes for items 0–6, with one finding the second stop has to hear first: **with both hands, a skip learner's skips are not singled out by the reads until a one-hand read separates them.** In a level-2 two-hand phrase the left hand holds a whole note under every right-hand note, so C4a's "both hands sounding at once" sits on every skip that went wrong; the skips never went wrong without it, and `demandReadings` rightly calls them `ambiguous` (the two-hand learner of `readerMovesTheDemand.test.ts`, five reads all with both hands: skips 16 of 23, `withoutRival` for playing together n = 0). The reader then says it is not sure, names nothing, keeps the left hand, and offers the easy read — right hand only, the newest thing added, undone — and that one-hand read is what separates them: the next morning the skips are a `pattern` and the step down is *skips off, both hands kept*. The thirty-day learner's move on day 6 rests on the same kind of read: its day-4 easy read was right hand only, and the skips' share where nobody played together (7 of 9, over days 1, 2 and 4) is what makes them a pattern. C4a's thresholds were not touched (as briefed). A learner who never reads a one-hand phrase would hear "not sure yet" until one comes, which is honest and slow (Follow-ups, C4a).

**The thirty days again, read as a teacher, against the first diary** (`docs/prompts/checkpoint-2026-09-27-diary.md`; the first is `checkpoint-2026-09-26-diary.md`):
- **Days 3–7.** Then: both hands on day 3, the easy right-hand read on 4, *Another like it* on 5, and on day 6 *This one right hand only — 10 of 14 right and in time yesterday* — the left hand taken because it was the last thing added. Now: the same days 3–5, then day 6 *This one by step only — skips went wrong in 3 phrases*: both hands kept, the skips out, and the phrase on the glass is stepwise under the held left hand. Day 7 *Another like it — 14 of 14 right and in time yesterday*; day 8 *Now with skips*, the skips back once the steps were clean on two days. That is what a teacher does: take the skips away, keep what was going well, bring them back when the rest is secure.
- **Days 11–20.** Then: ten days of the same phrase, *The next step waits for a later lesson* on four of them. Now: day 11 *This lesson's phrases can reach beyond C position* (2.2's row is held inside C position until 2.5 teaches leaving it, so 2.5's own demand arrives that day, and the reader moves nothing else), day 12 *Now with dotted quarters*, day 13 the easy one without them, day 15 *Now with tied notes*, day 17 the easy one without ties, and *The next step waits for a later lesson* only on days 19–20, when every demand 2.1–2.5 taught is in the phrase and shown. The wait is true there.
- **Days 22–25.** Then: *Now in G major* (22), *Now in F major* (24) — "now" of a key, as if F were harder (U52). Now: day 21 *A key signature to read: F major, one flat*, day 22 *An easy one, for fluency: in C major*, day 23 *Another like it: F major, one flat*, day 24 *Now with a note outside the key*, day 25 *Another like it: G major, one sharp*. The key is a set the seed chooses from (G or F at level 2), named each day, never "now", never ranked.
- **What a teacher would still question.** By day 26 the working recipe holds both hands, dotted quarters, ties, a key signature, an accidental and a promised leap: each taught and each shown on two days, but a dense phrase for the first week of 3.1, and some of those phrases do not keep all their promises (demonstration 4). *Now with a leap* on day 26 is a demand taught at 1.5 coming back as if new, because the five-read window had too few phrases with a leap held in them to count it shown. The phrases are still the random-walk generator's (D). Whether any of it reads as music is unverified as music: nothing was heard, and the notation was read, not played.

**The mixed-demand ambiguity learner** (same file; 2.5; every skip-eighth misread on days 1–2). Day 3, both halves: *An easy one: in C position — not sure yet what went wrong*; nothing named, no control moved for it. **(b) The reviewer's profile** (skip-eighths still wrong, skips in quarters and steps in eighths right): ten days, no demand ever singled out, no step down, the working recipe never moved; *Another like it — not sure yet what went wrong* on day 4, holds on the days the reads went right as a whole, one easy read on the cadence. It never moved up either: a proficient pair of reads in which a demand of the phrase still went wrong holds the recipe (deviation 5). **(a) The variant** (every eighth misread from day 3): day 4 *This one without eighth notes — the eighth notes went wrong in 3 phrases*; the skips stay unnamed (they held where no eighth was). Then both hands on day 6 and the eighths back on day 9, where the learner, constructed never to improve, fails them again: an oscillation with the window's memory as its period (Follow-ups).

**Each demonstration, with the evidence it rests on.**
1. *Repeated skip-specific failure changes the interval control, not hands* — yes: day 6's move is `interval.skip` off with `hands: 'both'` kept; that morning's readings: skips `pattern` (3 phrases below, 7 of 14), bass staff and playing together `ambiguous` (`firstThirtyDays` demonstration 1, `readerMovesTheDemand`). With the caveat above: it needs a read that separates the skips from playing together.
2. *Ambiguous mixed failure produces no specific diagnosis, and the contrasting reads then do* — yes: day 3 `unsure` in both halves, every sight-reading reading `ambiguous`; (b) never names a demand in ten days; (a) names the eighths on day 4 and only them (`firstThirtyDays` demonstration 2).
3. *The 2.5 learner reaches the next taught rhythm instead of waiting* — yes: dotted quarters on day 12, ties on day 15; no "waits" line at 2.5 before them (demonstration 3).
4. *Every legal move is generatable and detector-confirmed* — **partly.** Single moves: C4b's contract holds every taught demand on and off at every core rung, and the reader never asks for a move `UNREALISABLE_AT` declares or `unrealisable` gives a new reason against (`sightReadingFromReadingState`); every move the diaries asked for writes its demand in every phrase or none, over twelve seeds, with nothing untaught. **Composed recipes do not all hold:** the 3.1 working recipes (both hands, dotted quarters, ties, a key set, an accidental, and later a leap) miss a dotted quarter, a tie or the accidental at 5 of 12 seeds (13 lines), and day 28's own phrase has no tie. The contract proves each move from a rung's base, not moves composed on moves; that is C4b's to close, listed as `KNOWN_BROKEN` in demonstration 4 with the seeds (47615, 87210, 101, 39696, 71372; day 28's seed 3497510848). No line claimed a missing demand: day 24's *Now with a note outside the key* phrase has one (demonstration 5 checks).
5. *Every reason line says only what was established* — yes for the fifty lines both diaries produced: each "n of m" equals the latest read at the working recipe and its day word; each "X went wrong in k phrases" is a demand the readings that morning single out, below in exactly k phrases; "not sure yet" never stands beside a singled-out demand the last phrase held; every key named is the key the phrase was written in; every "Now with X" phrase has X (demonstration 5).
6. *Old item-completion semantics cannot contradict the evidence-derived rung state* — **not yet, by design; C5 owns it.** The old path still decides: the learner's rung comes from `nextRecommended` over pass records (`lessonComplete`), which is what the reader's row and taught-at gate stand on; a pass still credits every rung listing the item (L8); completion is a count over mixed lists (L9); a sight-read is still recorded like a piece, mastery and calendar (S8).

**What I looked at on the glass** (the final build, `vite preview`, 342 × 740, light, desktop Chromium; pictures in the scratch folder `glass/`; the rows restored were the diaries' own, moved in date): the skip learner's Today on day 6 — the daily card *This one by step only — skips went wrong in 3 phrases*, whole on two lines — and ▶ opening `recipe=hands:both,skips:0`, a stepwise right hand over whole-note C3 and G3; day 7 (*Another like it — 14 of 14 right and in time yesterday*); the ambiguity learner's day 3 (*An easy one: in C position — not sure yet what went wrong*, ▶ opening `recipe=position:1,easy:1`, one hand inside C4–G4); the variant's day 4 (*This one without eighth notes — the eighth notes went wrong in 3 phrases*, ▶ opening quarters and halves with the skips kept). The session card's reading slot was not on any of these cards: at 60 minutes and Shuffle 0 the warm-up takes the rung's reading row (L65), so its one-line reason (U51) was not seen with the new words. The brief's "day 7" for the skip learner's move is day 6 in the diary: the step down is due the morning after the second bad read at the recipe, as C4's was.

**Deviations, each with its reason.**
1. **`router.ts`** (not named): the route carries every control the reader moves (`skips:0`, `dottedQuarters:1`, `ties:1`, `fifths:1|-1`, `leftHand:…`); without it Today's recipe would be dropped on the way to the Score screen and the phrase written would not be the one offered.
2. **`ScoreScreen.ts`** (not named): the phrase is written through `readingOptions` with the route's rung (`taughtAtRung(judging rung)`) — the brief's "call `heldToRung` with the route's rung, for Today and for a row opened from the rung page" can only be done where the phrase is generated. One call site and its comment.
3. **`content/lessons/3.4.md`** and its claims row: the lesson said the daily read "changes one thing at a time … its key, or how far it ranges" (C4's two open dimensions at 3.4), false once any taught demand can move. Rewritten to "adding something a lesson has taught, such as a ledger line, a dotted rhythm or a key signature, or leaving out for a while a kind of note that keeps going wrong"; the row checks it against `readingMoves`. The longer text made the lesson 419 words, so its `readingTime` is 3 (`lessonShape`). Content rebuilt.
4. **`sightReadingPromises.test.ts` revised** (the brief listed it as preserve): removing `KNOWN_EARLY` means generating each row as the app now writes it — held to each rung listing it — so the rungs' promises are read at their own rung and the declared-skill check across the listing rungs (2.2's row declares position-shift, whose opportunity is 2.5's).
5. **A step up also needs every demand of the phrase held in the proving reads** (`heldBack`, my judgement on item 2): a phrase right as a whole on two days, in which some demand still went below the support share, is held, and the line names that demand where the reads single it out or says the app is not sure. Without it the reviewer's (b) learner moved up to both hands on day 7 while still missing every skip-eighth.
6. **The lesson line** (`why: 'lesson'`): calling `heldToRung` makes the phrase change when the row's rung changes (2.2's row leaves C position at 2.5). On that day the reader holds its recipe and says what the lesson adds, so one thing changes a day.
7. **The easy band's fallback is range, then hands** — C4's documented order ("else range, then hands"); C4's code sorted by its dimension list, which put hands first. The two differ only for a row with both hands its own and nothing added (4.5's).
8. **The e2e rows are a fixture made and guarded by a unit test** (`tests/e2e/fixtures/reader-learners.json`, written by `readerMovesTheDemand.test.ts` with `C4C_WRITE_E2E_ROWS=1`, and held equal to the real path's output on every run, in any time zone: the rows are dated noon UTC). Playwright cannot run OSMD and the engine on its own side; this is the real path's output, serialised, and it cannot rot silently.
9. **The thirty-day test's "one dimension from one day to the next" is revised to "one move from the working recipe"**: a targeted step down after an easy detour is one move from what the learner was working at and can be two from the detour's phrase (the variant's days 3–4).

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code, the diaries and four mornings on the glass; nothing heard)

The reader now does what a teacher does with the evidence a teacher would trust: it takes out the thing that keeps going wrong and keeps what goes well, it says when it cannot tell, it brings in what the rung taught once the learner is secure, and it treats a new key as a new key. Three places a teacher would put it differently: a two-hand learner's skips go unnamed until a one-hand read (the confound is in the evidence, the honest answer is "not sure", and the fix belongs to C4a's handsTogether reading); the month accumulates many demands at once by the end of 3.1; and a constructed learner who never improves oscillates with a period of about a week because the readings' window forgets. The words are plain; "skips went wrong in 3 phrases" means at least one skip went wrong in each of three phrases, which is what the evidence holds. Whether the phrases are music is unverified as music.

### Entry 78 — C4d: the contract over the composed recipes the reader can reach, and a hands-together opportunity that means coordination — the missed promises were the redraw budget, counted before it changed; playing together is counted where the left hand strikes under the right, so a two-hand skip learner is singled out the morning after the second bad read (2026-09-27)

**Judgement.** Yes for S29, L72 and the four reruns, with one finding the reviewer should hear first: **the composed misses were never a composition the generator could not write; they were a redraw budget sized for one promise at a time.** Counted before anything changed (probes in the scratch folder): at every missing seed the generator's own tally and the detectors agree, the loop had run all 64 draws, and every miss was in G major, where level 2's raised fourth (C sharp) lies at the bottom of the C4–C5 range — a draw keeps the accidental about once in forty there (once in eight in C, once in five in F), and all five of 3.1's working promises (skips, eighths, dotted quarters, ties, the accidental) about once in two hundred. Unbounded, the failing seeds keep every promise after 70–490 draws. The budget is now 4096, sized from the rarest recipe the reader can reach (about once in 370 draws, seeds 1–20,000; a seed of it now misses about once in 60,000). The same budget was quietly failing single promises too: five phrases in the unchanged golden (the older `accidentals` option at levels 3, 4, 5 and 7, hands together, four bars) had gone out without their promised accidental; they are the only golden entries that moved. The contract now walks what the reader can reach (about 1,100 recipes over twelve rung groups) and every one keeps its promises at every seed; two compositions the walk found were not the budget, and each is dealt with honestly (below). **L72:** the two-hand skip learner who never reads one-handed is singled out **the morning after the second bad read** — C4c's hypothesis holds; it does not take a third day.

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code, the diaries and the notation; nothing heard)

A teacher would recognise both repairs. A learner who misreads skips with both hands is told the skips are the trouble after two bad days, and keeps the left hand — no detour to one hand to find out. And a phrase the reader promises with a tie now has one. The 3.1 phrases are still dense and still the random walk's: day 28 keeps every promise and still leaps a tritone, ends on an off-beat eighth and holds its bass for four bars — D's. The held position in G is withheld rather than bent; a keyed learner at levels 2–3 whose range is singled out is held and told so (*Another like it — the notes beyond the hand position went wrong in 2 phrases, and every phrase here has them*), which is less helpful than a G-position phrase that fits, and whose last clause is true only where the recipe promises the range (C4c's P3 wording, now reachable here; Follow-ups). Unverified as music.

**Judgement.** Yes for L8, L9 and S8, and for the reviewer's exit criterion as far as the tree can show it: there is one path from evidence to rung state (`evidence/rungState.ts`), the old count-and-pass path is deleted (`lessonComplete`, `idsToCompleteLesson`, `passedIds`, `recordSets`, `demandsMeasuredAccuracy`, `paperPassAllowed`, `PassRecord`, `lessonForItem`, `requirementTerms`, `gateWaivers`, `mastery.exercisesRequired/songsRequired/custom`), stored rows under an older evidence version are recomputed on open, and Plan, the lesson page, Today and Skills read the derivation. Three things the reviewer should hear first:

1. **A learner on 2.2 with the owner's history** — constructed in the shapes his store holds, since his own rows are not in the tree (`pictures/owner-shaped-backup.json`: passes on the items of 0.1–2.1, the daily reads an older build passed, the Petzold mastered from the Library, a read compacted to bars, and one run of 2.2's eighths drill from Today's card for 2.2, restored through the app's own backup import onto a database marked as made before C5). On the first open the job carries 0.1–2.1 over (fifteen rungs, the practice track's five among them), puts the three reading rows back to *started*, and keeps the compacted read out, saying so. **Plan** (`pictures/plan-342x740.png`): *Next up · Stage 2 · Eighth notes and counting*; a legend over the stages, *done before* (a lighter, broken fill) · *counted since* (solid); Stage 0 *4 of 4 done before · 0 counted since* and Stage 1 *10 of 10 done before · 0 counted since*, each bar full in the broken fill; Stage 2 *1 of 5 done before · 0 counted since*, a fifth of its bar broken and none solid; 2.1 badged *done before*, 2.2 *in progress*; 4.7 wears nothing, where the old rule had it complete on the Petzold alone. **The lesson page** (`lesson-2.2-342x740.png`, `lesson-2.2-counts-open-342x740.png`): *in progress*, and *What the app counts — 1 of 3* folded under the actions; opened, the exercise requirement counted (*Rhythm reading with eighth notes*), a song *not yet*, and *Subdivision: familiar or better, from what your reads show wherever you read. (not shown yet)*, then *A run counts for this rung when you open it from this page, or from Today's card for this rung.* **Today**: working on 2.2; the review row an ear drill he passed, the repertoire row the Petzold (*A piece you know*, and he does); no reading row on the calendar. **The storage report**: *Evidence from your runs: 0 up to date. Kept out: 1 recorded before the app kept each note.* Why: 2.2 is the first rung the evidence has not met after the carried ones; its one qualifying run is the drill Today's card for 2.2 opened; nothing he played before C5 names 2.2, and no current evidence shows subdivision. **Skills** (`skills-342x740.png`): every concept of the carried rungs says *introduced* — the ladder's first state, the carry-over fed to it as an exposure dated the day it ran — and none says *learning* or *measured*, because the carry-over is not evidence and an item's pass no longer promotes a concept. Both were decided by the coordinator after the first pass (Questions, answered) and built with a red first (Done 6).
2. **The carry-over — decided: kept as built** (the coordinator: "a teacher does not erase a student's place"). Runs before 2026-09-21 name no rung, and from then every run until T37, and a run opened from no rung until C1, named the first rung listing its item, so the owner's rungs from before C5 cannot be re-derived from evidence. Without a carry-over his Plan would drop to 0.1. I carried over, once per device and only on a database made before C5 (the version 7 upgrade marks it), the rungs the old rule had done **before the rung it was recommending**, shown apart as *done before*, set aside and never met. A rung beyond that point that the old rule counted done only because a pass there credited every rung listing the item (the Petzold completing 4.7) is not carried. The alternative — carry nothing, and the owner walks 0.1 to 2.1 again — was declined.
3. **Rows from 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-26 still name the first rung listing their item** where they were opened from no rung (every run until T37; a run from nowhere, every Today card among them, until C1). `rungState` counts such a row for that rung, as it counts any row naming a rung — **decided: kept**, because that rung is the one that actually judged the run at the time (its thresholds decided the pass and it is the rung the row names), so the decision that the run meets *that rung's* requirement is truthful. It is at most one rung per run, never every listing rung, and re-judged at that rung's standard.

**The sixth verification** (the reviewer's fifth message) is `noCompletionBesideTheEvidence.test.ts`, both halves:
- *At the source:* no file in `app/src` names `lessonComplete`, `idsToCompleteLesson`, `lessonForItem`, `PassRecord`, `passedIds`, `recordSets`, `paperPassAllowed`, `demandsMeasuredAccuracy`, `requirementTerms`, `gateWaivers`, `exercisesRequired`, `songsRequired` or `mastery.custom`; the readers of rung state (`rungState.ts`, `session.ts`'s `nextRecommended`, `prerequisites.ts`, Plan, the lesson page, Today, Skills) read no item's pass or mastery flag; the first listing (`proseRungFor`) has one caller, the Score screen's side panel prose; `nextRecommended` is handed `RungStates`. Red on the committed tree: `AssertionError: expected [ 'curriculum\load.ts', …(5) ] to deeply equal []` (`lessonComplete` named in six files), and the same shape for the other names.
- *On the built curriculum:* for every item two or more rungs list, a qualifying run judged by one listing rung moves no other listing rung; the design's two proofs (a pass of the Petzold at 3.4 completes neither 4.4, 4.6 nor 4.7; two ear drills do not complete 1.5); and where the learner is follows the evidence, whatever was passed elsewhere. The same proofs on the committed code (a scratch probe calling the committed `lessonComplete`; not in the tree): `AssertionError: a pass at 3.4 completed other rungs by listing: expected [ '4.7' ] to deeply equal []` (4.7 asked for one song and the Petzold is one of its songs; 4.4 and 4.6 follow as soon as any of their listed exercises is passed anywhere); `AssertionError: 1.5 complete on two ear drills: expected true to be false`; and S8, `AssertionError: a generated phrase was put on the review calendar: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []` (`reds/committed-mechanism-probe.txt`). On C5's code the same assertions are the green cases of `noCompletionBesideTheEvidence` and `sightReadingIsNotAPiece`.

## Deviations, each with its reason

1. **The carry-over** (Judgement 2): not in the brief, which says the owner's real rows are the first test. Without it the first test is a reset.
2. **The learner's word is about the rung.** *I already know this* and *Mark done* used to mark every item of the rung self-passed, which credited every other rung listing them (L8 by another door). They now record `PlanRow.rungWords`, badged *you said you know it* / *marked done*, kept apart; `nextRecommended` sets the rung aside as it sets aside the rungs behind a placement. The per-item *Know it* button still marks the item's own record and counts for no rung.
3. **Placement stays a floor** (`startAt`), not predicates: its answers are the learner's own account, not runs of each rung's material; running it through `rungState` would make a self-report meet requirements, which C5's principle forbids.
4. **A rung that lists an item on none of its requirements' pools cannot be met by it.** A shelf twin's run counts only where the twin is one of the rung's songs (Follow-ups).
5. **`requireTwoSongs` moved into `rungState`** (`LearnerRecord.requireTwoSongs`): the setting raises a songs requirement to two where the rung asks for songs, is not song-optional and has two. It was `lessonComplete`'s.
6. **The drill route carries its rung** (`#/drill/<id>?rung=`): a drill opened from Today or a lesson page is judged by that rung; it was judged by the first rung listing it. The checklist, the placement test and the tour record *not measured* for accuracy, with the rung, and meet a `done` requirement of the rung that opened them when nothing was left undone (item 8).
7. **Three faults of my own, found in the pictures and fixed with a red first** (on the C5 code, since the committed tree has none of it): the job's write handed IndexedDB a key beside a row that carries its own, which it refuses, so in the browser the job wrote nothing and the report read *0 up to date* over a row it had not marked (`rungRowsStore` › the evidence job's write: `DataError: Data provided to an operation does not meet requirements.`); a store failing part way left the job *done* with a line like a finished one (`evidenceJobRecomputes`: `a failure read as a finished job: expected undefined to be true`), and while the job was still looking its line read the same (`evidenceJobReport`: `Expected: "Evidence from your runs: 3 up to date, still checking."`); a skill requirement said *(not yet — now not shown yet)* (`help`: `expected 'not yet — now not shown yet' to be 'not shown yet'`). The line is marked `data-settled` when the job is done, which is what the pictures wait on.

## Done — per item: mechanism, the red line, before → after

**1. Requirements are predicates over evidence.** *Mechanism:* a rung was complete on `mastery.exercisesRequired` + `songsRequired` counted over its lists, and `mastery.custom` was a string nothing enforced (L9); C2's `requirementTerms` mapped some terms to skills for the build gate only, with three waivers. *Change:* every rung states `requirements` (`content/curriculum.schema.json`, a `oneOf` over six kinds: `runs`, `reads`, `skill`, `done`, `measure`, `unjudged`); `mastery` keeps only `minAccuracy` and `minTempoPct`, the standard one run is judged at. The stage files were spliced as text (a round-trip differed from the raw bytes; `splice_requirements.py` in the scratch folder holds the per-rung table). `requirementTerms` and `gateWaivers` are deleted; `validate.py`'s `evidence_gate` works over requirements and waives nothing: 1.5's waiver became a `reads` requirement (five first readings of its row, 90 % right and in time at the full standard, keys guide off) and a `skill` requirement (interval reading, familiar); 3.4's became a `reads` requirement at the practice standard (five, 85 %); 4.6's *reading ahead* became `unjudged`, printed on the page as the lesson's rule. Nineteen lesson rules are `unjudged` and listed on every build. *Red:* `test_evidence_gate` `TypeError: evidence_gate() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`; `test_validate` `AssertionError: Lists differ: ['lesson 1.1: 0 song option(s), needs 3 — …'] != []`; `vocabulary` `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'flatMap')` (no `requirements` on the committed rungs); `requirementsCanBeShown` the same.

**2. One pure derivation.** *Mechanism:* `lessonComplete(lesson, records)` counted `passed.has(id)` over the lesson's lists, so a pass credited every rung listing the item (L8), and `nextRecommended` and Plan read it. *Change:* `rungState(rows, curriculum, vocabulary, today, learner)` walks the session rows once and gives every rung `met` / `in progress` / `not started`, each requirement's reading (holds, have, need, the items counted), `judged: false` where every requirement is `unjudged`, and the learner's word and the carry-over apart. `nextRecommended(curriculum, states, activeTracks, options)` skips met rungs and sets aside rungs with a word or carried over; its fallbacks are the first locked rung, then the first behind a placement, then the first set aside. Placement is a floor. `rungForSlot` gives a Today row the rung it was offered from where that rung lists it, else the one rung listing it, else none. *Red:* `rungStateFromEvidence` (no module on the committed tree); `todayOpensWithItsRung` `AssertionError: the first listing judged a run nobody opened from it: expected '1.2' to be undefined`; `prerequisites`, `recommendRespondsToEvidence` (no module).

**3. Skill evidence is the learner's; the decision is the rung's.** *Change:* a `skill` requirement reads `ladderState` over every current-stamp evidence record, whichever rung judged the run (`storedEvidence`); `runs`, `reads` and `measure` count only rows whose `lessonId` is the rung, each re-judged under `masteryCriteriaFor(rung)` from what it measured (Keep tempo at the rung's tempo; a Wait run only where the rung asks no tempo; drills on accuracy; Simon by its chain; nothing heard, rhythm only, a phrase met before and a self-report are not runs). Item credit across rungs is gone: no reader holds a per-item flag. Skills reads the ladder for vocabulary skills; an item's pass promotes no concept. *Red:* `rungStateFromEvidence` (above); `skillsReadTheLadder` `AssertionError: expected 'unseen' to be 'known'`; the probe (above).

**4. S8: a sight-read is not a piece.** *Mechanism:* the reading row's progress row was passed, mastered and put on the review calendar like a piece, and offered as repertoire. *Change:* `recordRun` treats a run with `unseen` or `recipe` as generated: no pass, no mastery, no best; the daily done-day stays. `reviewQueue(rows, now, isGenerated)` and `repertoireOf(rows, isGenerated)` take the predicate (required); `normaliseGeneratedRows` puts back to practised, once, the rows an older build passed or mastered; the Score screen offers no generated phrase as a mastery run; the repertoire row says *A piece you know* only when the piece it offers was mastered (L18). *Red:* `sightReadingIsNotAPiece` `AssertionError: expected 'mastered' to be 'started'`; `scoreSummaryTruth` `a sight-read was offered to the store as a mastery run: expected true to be false`.

**5. The recompute job.** *Change:* `data/evidenceJob.ts`. On every open, 1.5 s after the first screen is mounted (a dynamic import from `main.ts`), then one row per idle slice (`requestIdleCallback`, a two-second deadline; OSMD loaded only when a row needs a phrase written again, parsing into a detached element): the carry-over (once), the S8 normalisation, then every stored run whose evidence is under another version and not already kept out under the version in force — found by walking the sessions store, not the catalog (item 8). A row is rewritten from item, seed, recipe and the rung that held it, trying the writers the Score screen has used newest first, and a candidate is used only where it matches the run's own record (steps, bars, expected notes, early notes); otherwise it is kept out with its reason on the row (`no-steps`, `item-gone`, `no-seed`, `not-generated`, `phrase-differs`) until the version moves. Progress is on the storage report (`#settings-evidence`: *Evidence from your runs: n up to date, m being brought up to date. Kept out: …*). It never blocks the first screen: nothing before the delay, one row per idle slice, one announcement at the end. *Red:* `evidenceJobRecomputes`, `evidenceJobReport`, `carryOver` (no module); `dbUpgrades` 7 failed (`DataError` on the version 7 flag). In the browser, on the owner-shaped history, the job carried fifteen rungs, put three reading rows back to *started*, and kept the compacted read out with its reason on the row and on the report. The hypothesis that the owner's rows regenerate is tested on rows made in their shapes by the real path (`evidenceJobRecomputes`: a C1–C3 read, a C4 read and a C4a read each made current; a compacted read, an item gone and a phrase the generator now writes differently each kept out), not on his rows.

**6. The screens read the derivation.** The lesson page: the state badge (`rungBadge`), *What the app counts — n of m* folded under the actions, one line per requirement with what counted (`requirementWords`, `RUNG_TEXT` in `help.ts`, `04` §3f holds the words and `help.test` joins them), the lock line naming the rung's title and *Open that lesson* (T26). Plan: badges from `rungBadge`; a stage line of the rungs met, the learner's word apart (*3 of 9 lessons · 1 by your word*), and where rungs were carried, the carried first and the rungs met since after them (*10 of 10 done before · 0 counted since*, `stageCountWords` in `help.ts`); the bar the same way — the carried rungs first in a lighter, broken fill of their own (`.plan-stage-bar__carried`), then the rungs the evidence met, solid — with a legend over the list (`#plan-legend`: *done before* · *counted since*) drawn only where something was carried. The carried part is never the measured fill. Skills: the ladder, and the concepts of the carried rungs fed to it as exposures (`carriedExposures` in `rungState.ts`, `skillLadders(…, exposures)`; for a concept the vocabulary does not measure, the same first state when the skills store has it as never met), so they read *introduced* — a sixth state on the screen, the ladder's first — never *learning* or *measured*; what the learner said or showed outranks it. Today: `nextRecommended` over the states. *Red:* on the committed build, the lock line read *comes later Usually comes after 4.2 Flat keys and minor scales. Go to 4.2* (`carry-overs.spec`, `reds/e2e-revised-on-committed.txt`); `lessonPageReadsTheEvidence` `AssertionError: expected null not to be null` (no counts block); `planHierarchy` `expected null to be truthy`; `help` `` `04` has no §3f under that name ``; `drillWalkthrough` `a tour measured an accuracy: expected 1 to be 'not measured'`; `techniqueMeasures` `expected false to be true` (a `measure` requirement not read). The two builds after the coordinator's answers, red on the C5 code before them: `planHierarchy` › draws the carried rungs into the bar apart: `AssertionError: expected '1 of 7 lessons · 3 done before' to match /^3 of 7 done before · 1 counted since/`; `skillsReadTheLadder` › a carried rung's concepts are introduced: `TypeError: carriedExposures is not a function` (`reds/planHierarchy-carried.txt`, `reds/skillsReadTheLadder-carried.txt`).

**7. The other two learners, and the sixth verification as tests.** `firstThirtyDaysOnTheLadder.test.ts`: the returning intermediate (placed at 3.1) and the experienced musician (placed at 4.1, who says he knows 4.1 and 4.2), through the real reader, engine, evidence and store. The recommendation moves only the morning after the rung before it was met; a Library morning playing every option of the next rung moves nothing; 3.4 waits for its five reads, not a count of its pieces; the Petzold played from 3.4 moves none of the other rungs listing it; the musician's word sets 4.1 and 4.2 aside and meets neither; reads from 4.6's page begin 4.5 through the skills it names before any run 4.5 judged; 4.5 is met only by runs 4.5 judged. *Red:* no module on the committed tree. The sixth verification: above.

**8. The reviewer's two boundary defects (the C5 review of d06d7b7), each red first.**

*`done` is the judging rung's.* *Mechanism:* `runs`, `reads` and `measure` read the rows the rung judged, but `done` searched every row of the item across the learner's history and took any with nothing missed — not a live cross-rung credit today (0.1's checklist, 0.3's tour and 0.4's placement test are each listed by one rung) but a breach of C5's invariant. *Change:* `done` reads the rung's own runs like the other three, finished with nothing left undone and, where the run measured an accuracy, at the rung's standard; the per-item index is gone from `rungState`. I found no reason `done` must be global. *Red* (`rungStateFromEvidence` › a done requirement is the judging rung's, on a constructed curriculum where a second rung lists the checklist): `AssertionError: a run nothing opened from the rung met its done: expected true to be false`, and `a run judged by E met D's done: expected true to be false`. *The consumer it would have broken:* the tour leaves the drill screen on every step and the Score screen's Back returns to `#/drill/<tour>` without `?rung=`, so a tour begun from 0.3 finished as a run no rung judged, and 0.3 could never have been met by the tour it offers. The drill screen now keeps the rung that began the tour beside its position (`pianopath:walkthrough:<id>:rung`, cleared with the position when the tour finishes or starts over) and judges the finished tour by it; a tour opened from nowhere with nothing kept is judged by none. *Red* (`drillWalkthrough` › a tour begun from its rung and resumed after the Score screen): `AssertionError: the resumed tour lost the rung that began it: expected undefined to be '0.3'`. The checklist and the placement test finish on their own screen, so they keep the rung from the route.

*The job finds its rows in the store.* *Mechanism:* `runEvidenceJob` walked the current catalog's evidence-bearing items and asked each for its runs, so a run of an item the catalog no longer has was never enumerated; `item-gone` was reachable only by calling `candidatePhrases` with `undefined`. *Change:* the job walks the sessions store (`walkRuns`, in the browser `progressStore.walkSessions`, a cursor over every stored run with its steps and key) and takes each run whose stamp is missing or old where the item declares `targetSkills`, or where the item is gone and the row itself shows it bore evidence or was a generated phrase (`boreEvidence`: evidence, a stamp, the first-reading flag, a recipe or a seed) — so a gone reading row is kept out as `item-gone` and counted on the storage report, and a gone song's runs, which never bore evidence, are not reported as kept out. Stale rows are taken newest first. *Red* (`evidenceJobRecomputes` › a run of an item no longer in the catalog is found, through `runEvidenceJob` itself): `AssertionError: the run of a gone item was never found: expected undefined to deeply equal { definitions: 3, …(1) }`; the store's walk, `rungRowsStore` › the evidence job's walk: `TypeError: walkSessions is not a function`. *In the browser:* the owner-shaped history with a run of a retired reading row added — the production job kept it out and the storage report read *Evidence from your runs: 0 up to date. Kept out: 1 whose exercise is no longer in the catalog; 1 recorded before the app kept each note.*

`phraseMatches`'s limitation is unchanged and recorded as before (L80): a regenerated phrase that differs only in pitches where the learner played nothing early would match, because the generator's version is not on the row.

## Pedagogical verdict (from the code, the pictures and the requirements; nothing heard)

A teacher would recognise the change. A rung now asks for what its lesson teaches, and the page says what that is: 2.2 asks for an exercise and a song from its own page at its standard and for subdivision shown in the learner's reads, which is the skill of the rung; 1.5 asks for five first readings with the keys guide off, not two ear drills; 3.4 for five reads, not a count of pieces; and the nineteen rules no run can show are printed as the lesson's, never counted. Playing a piece from the Library moves no rung, and the page says where a run has to come from — a teacher would say it too, though a learner may feel his Library practice goes unrewarded until he opens it from the rung. The two things a teacher would have questioned in the first pass are answered: Plan now reads *10 of 10 done before · 0 counted since* over a bar full in a fill of its own — his place kept, and plainly not what the app has measured — and the concepts of the rungs he walked past say *introduced*, which is what a teacher would say of material the student has met and not yet shown her. Unverified as music: nothing was heard; the requirements are read against the lessons' own rules, not against playing.
