### Entry 92 — E0: measured truth on every notated item — every bundled score carries the demands the app's own detectors measured on it, cached on its bytes, with what it provides at a useful density; provenance on every catalogue entry and import, each fact labelled; one gate, `eligibleFor`, at every offer path, through which C6's demand tier and repertoire claim go live and the skill tier widens only where the notes establish the skill; a rung-claims report and an inventory the build regenerates; the evidence readers untouched (2026-09-27)

**Judgement.** Read from the built catalogue, the generated rung-claims report and inventory, the three constructed learners' thirty days as the app printed them (cards and each row's swap sheet), and the code. Nothing was played or heard. On a screen: only what the Today spec asserts at 342 × 740, and the two page snapshots Playwright saved when its first run failed (the 1.5 card and the 2.2 card with their swap sheets, read as accessibility trees; `e2e-1-snapshots/`).

**The rung-claims report, read as a teacher** (`docs/prompts/rung-claims.md`). The rungs make 670 claims about their 1,021 options; 576 of them name something the vocabulary can check against notation, and **349 of those are not established** by the option's measured notes (310 absent, 39 present only incidentally). Another 467 claims name something no detector measures — and no option carries a person's teaching-use review. Where the promise holds and where it does not:

- **Kept.** The core spine's first rungs keep their measurable promises on most options: 1.1's steps (10 of 10), 1.5's interval reading (9 of 9) and skips (6 of 9), 2.1's hands together (9 of 10), 2.5's shifts beyond the hand (8 of 8). `latin`'s syncopation is established on 12 of 17 options, the generated clave, tumbao and montuno among them.
- **Not kept by any option (9 claims).** 1.5 teaches leaps and none of its nine checked options has leaps at a useful density; 3.1 teaches accidentals and none of eleven has notes outside the key at density; `ragtime.5`'s oom-pah left hand is a moving left-hand pattern on none of nine; `technique.5`'s syncopation on none of fifteen; and the walking bass on `blues.5`, `blues.6`, `blues.8`, `jazz.6` and `jam.6` on none — E22's walking-bass reading is the detector's, so "none" is itself unverified, and the one place a walk is found on `jazz.9` is the stride exercise, which is the recorded misreading.
- **Nothing the notes can establish.** `jazz.7` (rootless voicings, quartal colour, tritone substitution), `jazz.8` (extended chords, modulation), `hymns` (four-part harmony, walk-ups, voice leading) and `technique.7` (double notes, octaves) claim nothing the vocabulary can measure: every option there rests on a person's judgement, and no judgement is recorded. What the notes do show there is a placement fault: the PDMX Jingle Bells jazz and Skating on `jazz.7`, two of `jazz.8`'s three pieces and four of `jazz.9`'s carry sixteenths no rung teaches, and seven of `hymns`' ten PDMX arrangements carry syncopation at stage 3, taught at 4.5.
- **The études.** `technique.4`'s one measurable claim (notes outside the key) is established by its two chromatic scales and one of its three Lemoine études; `technique.5`'s Duvernoy études establish none of its three claims (hand independence, syncopation, ties); `technique.6`'s Czerny Op. 299 studies do not have the moving left hand it claims (only the two 3:1 independence drills do); `technique.4`'s "avoid repertoire pieces" is finder prose no measurement can test. A teacher would say the technique rungs' études are chosen for touch, velocity and evenness — which is exactly the part the app cannot measure — and the report says so rather than validating them.

**The three learners with the tiers live** (the diaries' swap lines, `diaries-after/`; before, `diaries-before/`). The cards changed on 9 of the skip learner's 30 mornings and on none of the intermediate's or the musician's:

- **The skip learner (2.2 → 2.5 → 3.1, reads only).** Days 2–10 on 2.2, the repertoire row is *Hot Cross Buns — "A piece with eighth notes — your reads support them"* where it was *Merrily We Roll Along — "More music from this lesson"*: the repertoire claim C6 built dormant, now firing — a stepwise tune with eight eighth notes in its four bars (the density rule's floor for eighths), every demand of it (steps, one skip, eighths) supported by the learner's reads, and eighths the new thing 2.2 teaches. A teacher would use it for exactly that (its eight eighth notes are bar 3's repeated Cs and Ds and its one skip is bar 1's C to bar 2's E, read in the score; unverified as music: not heard). It repeats nine days because this learner never plays the card, as C6's review row repeated (L96); from 2.5 on nothing is ready (its new demand, the shift beyond the hand, has no supporting reads) and the row is the rung's own music again. The review row is unchanged every day. Its swap sheet now offers, under their own headings, items that *also practise the eighth notes* (the riffs in A minor and C major beside Hot Cross Buns) on 2.2 and that *also practise the notes beyond the hand position* on 2.5 (Cielito Lindo, Simple Gifts, the minor vamp, the amen cadence) — true claims, though a teacher might not swap a scale for a Latin song; the "Not a song" filter is a tap away.
- **The returning intermediate (3.1 → 4.6).** Every card as before. The review rows' swap sheets keep the lesson's own options first and add, where the gate finds them, *also trains reading by interval* (the other steps-and-skips drills and the level-1 reader, 3.4), *also practises the moving left hand* (the two-octave arpeggios, 3.6), *also practises the ledger-line notes* (Carol of the Bells, the Contredanse in F, K. 15h, the B minor five-finger pattern, 3.4), *also practises the key signature* and *the dotted quarters*. These tiers are wide: every piece that provides the rung's new demand and brings nothing the learner has not met, nearest level first — so on 3.1 "A Brotherhood of Heroes" (a game theme from PDMX) is offered beside the I–IV–V7–I drills. Nothing false is said; which of them a teacher would pick is ranking, Part 25's layer 7, not this seam.
- **The experienced musician (4.1 set aside → 4.6).** Every card as before. On 4.4 (days 2–5) the technique row's swap sheet is empty and the review row's (a Hanon number) offers only *Ode to Joy (easy variation)*, where both offered Hanon 3, 4 and 5: Hanon has sixteenths, **sixteenths are taught at no rung** (`taughtAt: null`, D0's L101), and on those mornings the musician's reads do not show subdivision familiar, so no Hanon number is one this learner can be said to cope with. A teacher would question an empty swap on the Hanon rung. The gate is right about the data and the data is wrong: the fix is the vocabulary's (a rung — 4.4's own — that teaches sixteenths), not a bypass for same-rung options, which the reviewer denied (constraint (b), Part 23). The card itself still gives him Hanon every day, from the rung's own list.
- **`familiar` against `introduced`**: no card and no swap sheet differs on any of the ninety mornings. The floor was never the constraint: whatever one floor refuses the other refuses too — inferred, the refused pieces carry a demand whose skill the learner has no evidence of at all (the ladder's `not introduced`), which neither floor admits. No learner is locked out of everything; the floor stays `familiar`.

Four things the reviewer should hear first:

- **The detectors read every bundled score** (the brief's first hypothesis, run before designing around it): 1,982 of 1,982 score files measured, none refused by the bridge; the 8 unmeasured entries are the seven import-only rock songs and one Chopin placeholder whose notation is not bundled, and the 71 runtime drills write no score. What the detectors *misread* is another matter: beside E22's three, **`detect.ts`'s own clef assumption** (staff 1 read as the treble clef, its module note) bites 74 catalogue scores whose upper staff is written in the bass clef somewhere — six one-staff bass-clef parts (the 1.3 left-hand songs among them, measured as every note on a ledger line and none on the bass staff) and 68 grand staves whose upper staff moves into the bass clef. The build finds them from the file's own `<clef>` signs, marks the two readings `misread`, and never lets them establish anything; the readings stay among the ids, so the gate still treats them as something the learner may have to meet. The reading itself is the detectors' owner's to fix (E22's seam): recorded, not done.
- **Every piece measured turns C6's demand tier into the catalogue by level unless it is anchored.** Almost every tune has steps, so "also practises steps" would offer everything a learner copes with. The demand tier's want is the demand the row's rung *teaches* (`taughtAt`), provided at a useful density: a swap for a 1.5 row keeps the skips 1.5 is about. The tiers are still wide (the intermediate, above); ranking among eligible candidates is Part 25's layer 7.
- **The gate makes D0's L101 bite.** Sixteenths are taught at no rung, so no learner copes with them through the lessons, only through reads that show subdivision familiar: 134 notated rung options carry sixteenths untaught on the earliest rung listing them (Hanon, Czerny, the jazz PDMX pieces), and on 4.4 the Hanon rows lose their swaps (the musician, days 2–5). Likewise Mary Had a Little Lamb, Merrily We Roll Along and Au Clair de la Lune carry a skip on 1.1, taught at 1.5, so 1.1's swap sheet does not offer them as equivalents; the rung's own list still gives them. Both are placement findings in the report, for F, G and the vocabulary's owner.
- **A rung's skill requirement is not a practice claim.** The gate serves a `skill` requirement (1.3's bass clef, 1.5's interval reading…) only with an item whose runs the evidence readers act on, because only those runs can meet it; the generated interval drills, whose notes establish interval reading, are offered on the swap sheet's skill tier as practice ("Also trains reading by interval"), never as what the rung is waiting for. So the session's skill want and its skill and demand steps still find nothing on shipped content — as after D0 — because the evidence boundary keeps them dormant, and D4 is what moves it.

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**Measurement on the arrangement played (item 1).** *Hypothesis:* the attach step can reuse D0's bridge unchanged for every source, because the detectors read the score model OSMD makes of any MusicXML. *Alternative:* the Kern and MuseTrainer conversions lose what a detector needs, and whole families come back unreadable. *Test:* every bundled file through `demands.measure_each` (which, unlike `measure_opportunities`, returns a file the app cannot load as an error row instead of failing the run). Result: no file refused; the one systematic misreading found was the clef assumption above, found by reading the 1.3 left-hand songs' rows (every note a ledger line) against the files' `<clef>` elements. *Cache:* `build/demands-cache.json` on each file's sha256 and on `demands.definition_fingerprint()` — the bytes of the detectors, the model and its extractor, the MXL reader, the bridge spec, the vocabulary and the lockfile — so the second build re-measured nothing and a detector change re-measures everything.

**The bridge regression on the build.** The ten pinned generated items and Anh. 113 carry in the built catalogue exactly the ids `demandsOfFiles.test.ts` holds the direct reading of the same files to (`test_measured_truth.TestTheBridgeRegressionOnTheBuild`); red on the baseline catalogue (`KeyError: 'demands'`).

**The gate at the consumers (items 3, 4).** *Hypothesis:* C6's tiers can be turned on by feeding them demands. *Alternative:* overlap by set intersection offers the catalogue. *Test:* `gateAtTheConsumers.test.ts` written to the consumers' own signatures and run on the committed code (red: the unmeasured option, the declaration the notes lack, the incidental sharer, the unready candidate, the large-hand voicing, the incidental "piece with skips") and on E0's (green). `session.test.ts`'s last-resort case showed the second half on real shapes: with items measured, the committed demand tier offered everything sharing a step.

**The incidental demand.** The density rule tells "two skips in forty bars" from practice of skips (`usefulDensity`, `established_by_density`), one rule per demand, and a Vitest case holds the app's reading equal to the build's on every built item (after subtracting the clef-misread readings, which the build never establishes).

**The corrected hand split (R34's truth half).** `eligibility.test.ts` imports a two-staff MusicXML whose falling bars the split sent to the left hand (measured in jsdom through OSMD, bass-staff notes among its demands), refuses it for a learner on the first rung, corrects the hands through `correctImportHands`, and finds it measured again as steps alone, the stored score the corrected one, the provenance saying the hands are the learner's, and the gate's answer eligible.

**The skill tier's order.** On the built catalogue a reading row's skill tier first interleaved the generated interval drills with the other reading rows by level, and the lesson's options filled the sheet before the left-hand reading row appeared (`alternativesShareASkill`'s reading-row case and the boundary test, red on the first E0 run). The tier now orders by the row's skills in their declared order — the primary, sight-reading, first — and then by level: another reader before an interval drill, which is what "trains the same skill" should mean for a sight-reading phrase.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **The per-demand useful-density minimums** (`content/sources/opportunity-density.json`): a located count *and* a count per bar for each of the nineteen demands, each with its reason and marked a hypothesis (the two every-bar detectors, left-hand pattern and walking bass, are not: presence already means every bar). Both, because a long piece passes a count by accident and a short one cannot reach one. One file read by the build (which writes `measurement.established`) and by the app (the import path); a Vitest case holds the two readings equal on every built item. A generated item may also establish a demand by its family contract where the contract states a density (a count per bar, or a count of two or more) — the family's own considered threshold, and a four-bar drill cannot reach a whole-piece count — and a presence-only rule establishes nothing, which is how the tie drill's one tie in four bars is not adequate practice (D0 finding 6).
- **`demands: "unmeasured"`** is the string itself, not an empty list beside a flag: `CatalogItem.demands` is `string[] | 'unmeasured'`, so every reader has to handle it or fail to compile, and an empty list can only mean measured-and-empty. The reason sits in `measurement.reason`. A runtime drill has no `demands` and `measurement.status: "runtime"`: its notes are made per phrase, and it is not a notated item.
- **The provenance record's shape**: `source`, `edition`, `composition`, `arrangement`, `converter` or `generator`, `facts` (each `{kind, via}` with kind one of measured, inferred, authored, reviewed, unmeasured, runtime), `review` (`score`, `teaching`, `null` = no person has decided), `quarryKeep` (PDMX only, neither bit), `physical` (the declared large-hand voicing). A learner's correction of the hands is `authored` with `via` naming the learner. A generated or runtime item's identity is its generator (family, version, seed, or the drill kind), and it names no composition: an exercise is not a work, and the inventory counts none.
- **What a rung claims**, for the report: its `skill` requirements; its concepts that are vocabulary skill ids; its concepts that name a notated fact a detector finds (a small table in `claims.py`: `alberti`, `waltz-bass`, `oom-pah-bass`… → the left-hand pattern; `walking-bass`; `skips`; `eighth-notes`; `chromatic`…); and the demands `taughtAt` names it for. Everything else it names is a claim the notes cannot establish, listed per rung with the review bit.
- **The demand tier's want is the demand the row's rung teaches** (`taughtAt` of the rung it was offered from, or the first rung listing it), not every opportunity of the row's target skills: with every piece measured, "also practises steps" would make the tier the catalogue by level, which is Part 23's trap by another road.
- **A rung's skill requirement is served only by what the evidence readers act on** (`want.for: 'requirement'`), because only those runs can meet it; selection's skill tier and skill step may offer a generated item whose notes establish the skill's opportunity, as practice, never as what the requirement counts.
- **The repertoire claim has no judging rung**, so the gate reads the evidence alone there: "your reads support them" stays true, and the old rule is unchanged but for the density.
- **The readiness floor stays `familiar`** (the brief's instruction unless a learner is locked out of everything; see the reruns).
- **D0's suite keeps its own run of the plan**, through the same bridge (one definition, two runs): it tests the generator in process, before any build and in its red trees, which the build's attach step cannot.
- **The reports** go to `docs/prompts/rung-claims.md` and `docs/prompts/inventory.md` from the default build only; a `--out` or `--quick` build writes the JSON under `build/` and leaves the documents alone.
- **The Today swap sheet reads the learner's skills as well as their rung.** `swapOptions` takes the stored runs (`rows`) and reads the skills from them as the session does (`skillEvidenceOf`), and `TodayScreen.ts` hands it the runs the card was built from — three lines in a screen file outside the brief's list, because without them the swap sheet would ask only half of the gate's decided first question (the lessons, not the evidence), and a learner whose reads show subdivision familiar would still be refused every sixteenth-note piece. No pixel of the screen changes.

## The rung-claims report and the inventory, in brief

- **The report** (`docs/prompts/rung-claims.md`, the JSON in `build/rung-claims.json`): 109 rungs, 1,021 rung options, 670 option-claim pairs; **576 checkable against notation, 227 established, 349 not** (310 absent, 39 incidental, 0 unmeasured); 7 the reading rows' own and 87 other runtime drills'; **9 rung claims no option establishes** (1.5's leaps; 3.1's notes outside the key; `ragtime.5`'s oom-pah left hand; `technique.5`'s syncopation; the walking bass on `blues.5`, `blues.6`, `blues.8`, `jazz.6`, `jam.6`); 156 measured options establish none of their rung's measurable claims; 467 concept claims no detector can measure, 0 teaching-use reviews; 74 scores marked for the clef assumption; the generated items' untaught-on-rung combinations 71, D0's record exactly; 206 notated options carry a demand untaught on the earliest rung listing them (sixteenths on 134, syncopation on 47, a shift beyond the hand on 27). **The worst**: the rungs whose promise no option keeps, and the rungs (`jazz.7`, `jazz.8`, `hymns`, `technique.7`) whose every claim rests on a judgement nobody has recorded.
- **The inventory** (`docs/prompts/inventory.md`): **2,061 items — 1,982 measured, 8 unmeasured (each with its reason), 71 made at runtime; 784 distinct works and 813 distinct arrangements; excerpts as their own objects 0 (E1); 0 score reviews and 0 teaching-use reviews (the 542 PDMX quarry keeps are neither); 236 items at a tempo the converter supplied.** The cliff it shows: of the measured songs at level 1, 17 of 19 are one hand only, at level 2, 63 of 73, and a left-hand pattern appears first at level 3 (3 songs) — a learner reaching hands together at 2.1 has ten two-hand songs at level 2, and most levels are estimates.

## Done

1. **Demands measured on every notated item at build time (item 1; R38, E23).** `build.attach_demands`: every bundled score through the bridge (`demands.measure_each`), `demands` and `measurement` (located counts, bars, steps, notes, `established`, the contract share, the definitions measured under, the clef `misread` marks) on the row, cached on the file's bytes and the definitions' fingerprint; `demands: "unmeasured"` with the reason where no notation is bundled, `measurement.status: "runtime"` on a runtime drill; a reader failing on more than a tenth of the files stops the build. An imported score is measured at import (`importStore.measureImport`, the same detectors through OSMD, the same density rule) and again when the learner corrects its hands (`correctImportHands`). D0's suite keeps its own run through the same bridge (one definition).
   - *Technical:* 1,982 of 1,982 files measured; the build's demands equal the pinned direct readings; the density rule held equal between build and app on every built item.
   - *Pedagogical:* what a piece asks of a learner is now the notes', never its title, level or genre; where a reading is known to be wrong it is marked and establishes nothing. Whether the per-demand minimums are the right ones is a teacher's judgement: hypotheses, each with its reason.
2. **Provenance on every content object (item 2; R35, R15, R11, Part 21 §B).** `build.attach_provenance` on every catalogue row and `importStore.importProvenance` on every import: source, edition, composition, arrangement, converter or generator by version, each fact labelled (measured, inferred, authored, reviewed, unmeasured, runtime), R42's two review bits apart, the quarry keep (the decision alone; the reviewer's note stays in the source table) neither, the large-hand declaration; tempo-sensitive demands listed untrusted where the tempo is inferred (236 items); the learner's hand correction recorded as authored by the learner.
3. **One gate (item 3).** `app/src/curriculum/eligibility.ts`: `eligibleFor` answers can-cope and opportunity from the facts the candidate has, returns eligible, exploration-only with the missing measurement, or ineligible with the reason; unmeasured is exploration-only on every path; it reads declared skills only through `skillActivation.declaredSkills` (added), so D0's boundary is extended, not duplicated; the evidence readers are untouched and keep `SHIPPED_SKILL_ACTIVATION`.
4. **C6's dormant tiers live through the gate (item 4; L36).** The swap sheet's four tiers and its last resort, the session's skill requirement, its skill and demand steps and the repertoire claim call the gate and nothing else; the untaught-demand filter in `swapOptions` became the gate's first question; level orders eligible candidates; the words are *Also trains …* / *Also practises …, with the other demands you have met*. The Today screen hands the swap sheet the learner's runs as well as the rung (three lines in `TodayScreen.ts`).
5. **The rung-claims report (item 5; R38, Part 12 §1).** `tools/content/claims.py`, written by `build.step_reports`; `validate.py` warns with its count and never fails; nothing removed from any rung; D0's 71 combinations carried and matched; E22's readings and the clef assumption marked.
6. **The inventory (item 6; R39).** The same module and step; works, arrangements, measured and unmeasured, reviewed and not, texture, keys, range, rhythm, level bands, demand coverage by rung, whole against excerpt.
7. **Record.** `docs/02` Part E2 (the gate) and a rung-claims note; `docs/03` §3 (the merge step and the reports step), §4 (measured demands) and a new §4a (provenance); `docs/04` §2 (the tier words, which the spec quotes); `docs/08` (a row for E0 and the file lines); `catalog.schema.json` (`demands` as ids or `"unmeasured"`, `measurement`, `provenance`; the stale `targetSkills` and `role` descriptions, E24).

## The red lines

Seen before the change each proves, for its reason; the worktree untouched (the scratch app is built by `scripts/make_red_app.py` from `git show HEAD:` snapshots in `head/`, with the E0 build's `catalog.json` and `curriculum.json` and no score files).

**`red-content-baseline-catalog.txt` — `test_measured_truth.py` against the catalogue the committed build wrote** (the baseline build, before E0's attach steps; the test file as first written). 23 tests, 4,126 failures and 2,296 errors, each for its reason: `no measurement record` on all 2,061 entries; `no provenance` on all 2,061; `KeyError: 'demands'` on the ten pinned generated items and Anh. 113 (the committed build wrote no demands, so the bridge regression on the build has nothing to hold); `rung-claims.md` and `inventory.md` missing; the generated untaught-on-rung combinations not the record (nothing measured, nothing found); the inventory's headline `0 != 2061`. Green on the committed tree by design: the density rule's own adversaries (the incidental and presence-only cases they carry are their power).

**`red-clef-build1-catalog.txt` — the clef-assumption case against E0's first build**, saved before the build marked those files: `0 not greater than 0 : the LH songs in the bass clef on one staff are no longer found` — the one-staff bass-clef songs' ledger-line reading stood as measured truth.

**`red-app-consumers.txt` — E0's consumer and revised tests against the committed app code** (`redapp`: the committed `selectors.ts`, `session.ts`, `types.ts`, `skillActivation.ts`, `help.ts`, `importStore.ts`, `db.ts`; no `eligibility.ts`). 93 tests collected, 11 failed, each for its reason:

The fourth (the clean piece chosen) is green on both: the old rule chose it too.

[]).some is not a function` — the committed tier reads `demands: "unmeasured"` as an array, which is what the string sentinel is for.

## Unverified, beside what passes

1. **Nothing was heard.** Hot Cross Buns as "a piece with eighth notes", every "also practises" offer, and the report's verdicts are the notes' as the detectors read them; none was played.
2. **The density minimums are mine**, each a hypothesis with its reason in `content/sources/opportunity-density.json`; they hold as arithmetic on the built catalogue, and a reviewer may set them otherwise. The report is where a threshold that refuses a good piece would show.
3. **The detectors' readings are the detectors'**: E22's three, and the clef assumption on 74 scores, are marked, not corrected; a reading absent from the report because a detector cannot see it (a tie across the barline on the beat, a short off-beat note) is unverified absence.
4. **The composition identity is inferred** for every piece that is not an authored variant (`work_key`, conservative by design: two keys that differ may be one piece).
5. **The learners are constructed**, and the owner's rows are not in the tree; the three reruns show cards and swap sheets as the code prints them, not as a person uses them.
6. **The e2e cases** assert the demand tier's heading and one option, and the warm-up's empty sheet, on the glass at 342 × 740; the other options were read only in the failure snapshots' accessibility trees, not looked at.
7. **The catalogue is larger.** The E0 fields roughly double the gzipped `catalog.json` and more than double the text the app parses on load (measured here as a relationship; no timing taken on a phone).

## Not done

- **Scores imported before E0 are not re-measured.** They carry no measurement, read as unmeasured, and are offered for exploration only — not as swap equivalents — until re-imported or corrected. A background job like the evidence recompute is the follow-up; nothing in E0 runs one.
- **The detectors' clef assumption is marked, not fixed** (the detectors' readings are E22's seam, and the brief keeps them out of E0).
- **No hand-split correction screen** (R34's UX is X's): `correctImportHands` is the truth half the screen will save through.
- **The review bits are all `null`**: no person's score or teaching-use review exists to record; the workbench that records them is E1 with E16.
- **Not this brief's, named so they are not claimed**: excerpt-local demands and the whole-versus-excerpt refusal (E1); the PDMX excerpt judged on the bars played (E1); the chooser's purposes, sources and ranking (later); repertoire recommendation beyond the existing slots (G, X); widening what earns evidence (D4).

## Follow-ups

- **P1, vocabulary (L101):** sixteenths are taught at no rung, so the gate never lets the lessons cover them; 134 notated rung options carry them, and 4.4's Hanon rows lose their swaps. A rung that teaches sixteenths (4.4's own, where Hanon is practised) is the vocabulary's change, with its test.
- **P1, placement (R38, L101):** the report's 206 notated options with a demand untaught on the earliest rung listing them (the 1.1 songs' skip, the hymns' syncopation at stage 3, the jazz pieces' sixteenths) and its 9 rung claims no option keeps — F's and G's to rewrite from; nothing moved here.
- **P1, placement (seen on the glass):** a learner placed at 1.5 gets **Hanon No. 1 hands together** as a new row, because practice.1 (on by default) lists it as its one exercise option and its `runs` requirement asks for it; the session's `runs` pool is the rung's own list, which E0 does not gate ("nothing removed from a rung"). A teacher would not give a beginner at 1.5 Hanon with sixteenths. Practice.1's Hanon is in the report's generated untaught-on-rung record; the fix is F's (another exercise for practice.1).
- **P2, placement:** 2.3's chord drill has no swap: 2.3's cadences and inversions measure the shift beyond the hand (2.5), so a learner on 2.2 whose warm-up is 2.3's drill sees "Nothing else trains the same thing yet." In the report; F's to re-place or re-voice.
- **P2, detectors (E22):** the clef assumption on 74 scores (six one-staff bass-clef parts; 68 upper staves moving into the bass clef) beside E22's three.
- **P2, imports:** re-measure the scores imported before E0 (a background job, as `evidenceJob` recomputes evidence).
- **P2, converter version:** the MIDI converter should own its version (`MIDI_CONVERTER_VERSION` lives beside the provenance writer for now).
- **P2, can-cope is per skill (the skip learner):** the gate asks the ladder of a demand's `copedWithBy` skill, so a learner whose interval reading is familiar through steps is taken to cope with a skip even when their last two reads misread every skip (Hot Cross Buns' one skip, bar 1's closing C to bar 2's E, read in `content/scores/authored/hot-cross-buns.abc`). That is the decided semantics and the evidence readers' reading; a per-demand check within a skill is the evidence owner's to weigh.
- **P3, catalogue size:** a compact encoding of the provenance's repeated `via` strings, if the first load on a phone shows the parse.
- **P3, the demand tiers' breadth:** ranking among eligible candidates (Part 25 layer 7) is what would put the Petzold before a game theme; E0 orders by level only.

## Questions

None that block. One for the reviewer: the gate refuses a rung's own options on its swap sheet when they carry a demand the rung has not taught (Mary Had a Little Lamb's skip on 1.1, Hanon's sixteenths on 4.4). That is constraint (b) and Part 23 as written, and it is the placement report made visible to the learner; if the reviewer prefers the same-lesson tier to wait until F re-places those options, it is one condition in `tieredAlternatives`, and I did not add it. A second, smaller one: the swap sheet judges every row at the learner's placed rung (`rung` from Today), while the session judges a parallel strand's row at that strand's rung (`learnerAt(ctx, strand.rung)`); for a strand row the two can disagree about what is taught. I left the sheet at the placed rung, because its practice tiers' words promise "the other demands you have met".

### Entry 93 — E0a: "taught by this rung" is the rung's ancestry — the core path in stage-and-unit order, a track rung's prerequisites followed back and the core path up to its stage — and, where the gate has a learner, the rungs they have reached; the walking bass `blues.5` teaches is no longer taught at `jazz.5`; the build's "untaught here" and D0's rung check read the same ancestry (2026-09-27)

**Judgement.** Read from the predicate's answers on the shipped curriculum, the swap sheets the app computes for fixed rows (a probe, before and after), the three learners' thirty mornings as the app printed them, and the regenerated report. Nothing played, heard or looked at on a screen beyond what the Today spec asserts.

- **The walking bass at `jazz.5`.** Before: taught — `blues.5` is stored before `jazz.5`, and the committed predicate credited any demand whose teaching lesson came earlier in the file. After: not taught at `jazz.5`, `jazz.6`, `classical.5` or any rung off `blues.5`'s path; taught at `blues.5` and `blues.6`; taught for a learner on `jazz.6` whose reached rungs include `blues.5` (the session's `reached`, now handed to the swap sheet by Today). On the shipped catalogue no `jazz.5` or `jazz.6` sheet changes (`probe-compared.txt`: no option on those sheets carries a measured walking bass); where it shows is `latin`'s sheet, which no longer offers the generated walking bass over ii–V–I to a learner who has not been through `blues.5`.

The learner's own path then gives back what that learner has actually passed — and can give more than the file did: a learner who reached `blues.5` meets syncopated hymns on `hymns`' sheet, which the file's order refused (4.5 is stored after `hymns`).

Why: all three walk the core path alone (`activeTracks: ['core']`), where the ancestry is the core path to the rung and the file's order agrees with it (no track rung stored before a core rung teaches a demand), and their reached rungs are core rungs.

Neither rung's path goes through `blues.5`, so the hold now keeps the walking bass out of every row-7 phrase there (200 of 200 seeds' options change, `probe-holds.txt`; no other row at any rung changes). ## The mechanism

`app/src/curriculum/session.ts`: `rungAncestry` (line 1715, memoised per curriculum object in a `WeakMap`) and `taughtAtRung` (1772: a demand is taught when its `taughtAt` is in the rung's ancestry, or in the ancestry of a rung in the optional `reached`). The ancestry is the rung plus the ancestries of its parents:

- **A core rung's parent is the core rung before it in stage-and-unit order** (plus its own prerequisites, which are earlier core rungs). The brief's deviation clause, taken: the core path's ancestry is **not** expressible from `prerequisites` alone — 4.6's, followed back, never reach 3.4 (3.5 builds on 3.3, 3.4 on 3.1), 4.7 names none, 2.3 does not reach 2.2, and Stage 0 is nobody's — while the spine is walked in that order (`nextRecommended`, `strandsOf`). Proved on 1.5 (0.1–1.5) and 4.6 (every core rung to it, 3.4 included).
- **A track rung's parents are its `prerequisites` and the last core rung of an earlier stage.** The brief's hypothesis was that prerequisites alone give a track's ancestry. They do not: `jazz.5` → `chords-pop.5` → `chords-pop.4` → `chords-pop.3` → 3.2, so prerequisites alone would read 4.5's syncopation and 3.6's moving left hand as untaught at `jazz.5` and `classical.5` for every learner — yet a Stage 5 track rung opens only once the core path is done (`strandsOf`, line 578: `next.stage <= spineStage`; `docs/04` §2: "open: the spine has reached its stage"). So a track rung stands on the core path up to its stage, by the app's own opening rule, and never on the file's position. A track's own earlier rungs count only through its prerequisites.
- **The learner's own path (item 2)** is a fact the session holds: `strandsOf`'s `reached` (met, set aside, behind the placement, or a strand's open rung). `learnerAt` passes it (line 681); `buildSession` now returns it; Today stores it and hands it to `swapOptions` (`reached`, line 1485); the diary helper hands it the same way.
- **`lessonOrder` keeps its one other reader**, the easy move's "newest thing the recipe added" sort among demands the learner's rung has taught — all in one ancestry, where the file's order is a linear extension of it (every prerequisite and every earlier-stage core rung is stored before its rung; checked in `taught-moves.txt`).
- **The build** (`tools/content/claims.py`): `rung_ancestry` (line 120) is the same reading in Python, `first_listings` (169) reads an option at every rung that no other rung listing it precedes on its path (the file's "earliest listing" hid an option's second track), and `untaught_on` (263) reads the ancestry. The report JSON carries every rung's ancestry (`"ancestry"`, line 368), and `taughtByAncestry.test.ts` holds the app's equal to it. D0's rung check (`test_measured_demands.py`) now calls the same three functions, so the record the report is held to and the check that writes it are one reading; `family_contracts.untaught_on` (the flat reading, read by that test alone) is deleted.

**Discriminating tests.** The two-track constructed curriculum and the reordered shipped file (every stage's track units stored before its core units: 108 readings differ on the committed predicate, none after) tell "ancestry" from "file order"; the `jazz.5` syncopation case tells "ancestry with the spine" from "prerequisites alone"; 4.6's ledger lines tell "core by stage-and-unit order" from "core by prerequisites".

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**Stopping.** *Hypothesis:* phrases stop because the walk writes the last bar's rhythm with no rule about how it ends: the last note is whatever length the bar ran out on. *Alternative:* the levels' palettes cannot end well at all. *Test:* the arrival measures over each level's valid draws. Result: levels 2–7 can never put the final note on the last downbeat in 4/4 — no bar-long note is in their palettes — at either version (0 % "on the last downbeat" in both tables), but a valid draw ends on a note held a felt beat often enough that one is almost always among sixteen: arrival by the rule reaches 87–100 % by selection alone. So the brief's first inherited hypothesis holds for arrival by the rule, and no level needed arrival in the hard layer (none has valid draws that never arrive); it fails for the downbeat, which would need a closing cell (new cells are not D1's; Follow-ups).

**Wandering.** *Hypothesis:* scoring the attempt sequence's candidates reaches one contour at every level. *Alternative:* the walk itself — a leap drawn uniformly up to the cap, about half the cap on average — is the ceiling, and no count of candidates reaches it at levels 5–7. *Test:* the same seeds with 48 candidates instead of 16, on the final scorer. Result: level 7's one-contour units 13 % → 14 %, level 6's 22 % → 26 % (`runs/probe-candidates-16.txt`, `probe-candidates-48.txt`): the walk is the ceiling at 6–7. The hypothesis holds at levels 1–2, partly at 3–5, and fails at 6–7; the bounds there are modest and say why.

**The drift the suite caught.** The first scorer passed every single-phrase test and the suite found two failures no example showed: level 2 fell from about four notes a bar to three and a half (a sparser phrase is easier to shape and ends long more often), and level 1 collapsed onto a handful of five-note phrases that half the seeds wrote. *Mechanism:* the strict best among candidates is biased to sparse draws, and where the best-shaped phrases are few the strict best is the same few phrases. *Fix:* the choice keeps the level's density (only draws at or above the valid draws' lower quartile of notes are eligible; the median held density too but halved the pool) and takes the earliest draw within 0.05 of the best (level 1: 156 distinct in 200 seeds at the strict best, 182 with the tolerance, 192 at version 1).

**Sitting on a note.** The reader's read found version 2's level-2 seed 4242 writing eight of sixteen notes on C: the walk's floor at C4 clamps moves down into repeats, and nothing in the scorer asked otherwise, so it chose among C-heavy draws. *Fix:* one pitch struck more than three times running costs the contour (a factor, like rocking). Repeated notes went back to version 1's level (e.g. 2.2's row 30 % → 25 %, version 1 24 %), at a cost of a few points of contour at level 3 and more rocking on 2.2's five-note row (bounded, with its reason).

**S26.** *Mechanism:* the tie-closing pass set the next bar's first note to the tied pitch after the walk had moved on from where the tie started, so the note after it was chosen from elsewhere. *Test:* seed 71282 on the right-hand row with ties (the reader's move at 2.4–2.5), through `readingOptions`: version 1 writes C4 tied into bar 2 then G4 (four scale steps) and A4 tied into bar 4 then E4 (three), where the cap is two; version 2 holds the walk through the tie. (The row's "a fifth" is the first of the two; the A–E one is a fourth.) The chord-tone snap at 5–7 was the other way past a cap (it moved a strong beat one step from wherever the walk put it); version 2 moves to a chord tone only within the cap of the note before — which keeps every strong beat on a chord tone at 5–7 (100 % at both versions), where scoring alone got about two in three (below, the builder's calls). By kind, on version 1 over 200 seeds (`runs/probe-s26-kinds.txt`): at level 4, 122 phrases tie from off the beat and 42 leap past the cap after a tie; at level 3, 80 and 38; at levels 5 and 7, no off-beat tie counts (syncopation is designed there), 26–28 leap after a tie and 17–18 leap on a snapped strong beat.

**Identity.** *Premise checked at the lines:* the brief expected the runtime drill's identity where `fromCatalog.ts` builds drills; it does not build sight-reading drills (`drillFromCatalog` returns null for them). The only identity a sight-read has in the learner's history is the run's record, `SessionRow` in `data/db.ts`: the row, the recipe, the rung and the seed (`evidenceJob.ts` says so: "the generator's version is not on the row"). Two readers key on the seed: the Score screen's phrase-seen check and the evidence job's rewriting of a stored run's phrase (whose match test, `phraseMatches`, can pass a phrase with the same rhythm and other pitches). So a version-2 phrase from a seed already read would reach the history as the same encounter. That is the brief's stop line: see Not done.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **Version 2 behind an option, version 1 in force.** The brief: stop at the schema line, and do not ship the scorer behind the existing identity. So `version` is an option, `SIGHT_READING_IN_FORCE` is 1, and every consumer (the Score screen, the evidence job, the transposition drill, the lab) writes exactly what it wrote: the unchanged golden's hashes and the level 5–7 goldens hold. Keeping version 1 writable is also what the follow-up needs: a stored run with no version reads as version 1, which the generator still writes note for note, so no evidence is lost at the flip.
- **The capped move to a chord tone at 5–7, not scoring alone** (a deviation from the brief's "the snap becomes a scored quality rather than a rewrite"). The decided item's purpose was to stop the snap leaping past the cap. Scored only, the strong beats on chord tones fell from every strong beat to about two in three at 5–7 — selection among sixteen random walks cannot do better (S7 names "the right hand ignores the left hand's harmony" as the fault) — while a move to the nearest chord tone within the cap keeps both: 0 violations and 100 % agreement. The harmony part still scores the agreement at 2–4 (where the left hand picks its own chord) and what the move leaves at 5–7.
- **Ties off the beat only where the phrase syncopates on purpose** — designed at levels 5–7, promised at 1–4 (4.5's row) — stricter than the brief's "below 4.5": T37's placement rule for levels 1–4 is every note where its length belongs, whatever the rung, and a tie from an off-beat is syncopation the row does not promise. It moves `sight-reading-4` at 4.6 (a level-4 row on a rung after 4.5): version 1 had a violation in 53 % of its phrases, most of them such ties.
- **Contour on the beats.** A four-bar unit's contour is read on the note sounding at each felt beat, with a turn counted once the line comes back a third: on every note, level 5's eighths "turned" on half their notes while the line rose. One contour per four bars (an arch, a valley, an ascent or a descent), so an eight-bar phrase may be two arches; no form is required.
- **The arrival grades and weight.** The rule is the reviewer's, stated in the tests; the score grades within it (downbeat 1, the half bar held 0.9, another beat 0.7, off the beat 0.5) because a quarter on beat 4 is weaker than a half from beat 3; arrival weighs 5 against contour's 3, because at 3 each one phrase in five still ended short at 5–7.
- **Candidates 16, window 96, tolerance 0.05, lower-quartile floor**: each with its measurement above. The window bounds rare recipes (row 4's accidental keeps about one draw in eight: it makes about a hundred draws a phrase, within the budget).
- **The suite reads the page.** It measures the MusicXML read back, not the generator's own model, so the same suite measures the committed generator's pages (the red tree) and confirms the page is the phrase the generator chose (the page's score equals the reported one). Page reading is by pattern (the writer emits one fixed shape); jsdom's parser cost tens of milliseconds a phrase.
- **Seeds**: 200 per level, 150 per row per rung (rows on two rungs get 300); every configuration's phrases are written once and every case reads them.
- **Felt beat in odd metres.** 6/8: the dotted quarter, held from the second beat counts, a whole-bar note lands on the downbeat (levels 3–4's 6/8 figure makes it possible, 11 % → 53 % on row 3). 5/4: a quarter, as a teacher counts. 7/8 and 5/8: `feltBeat` gives an eighth, which a teacher reads as a subdivision of 2+2+3; the arrival measure uses a quarter there. No row asks for 5/4 or 7/8: the brief's "5/4 and 7/8 rows" do not exist (the nine rows ask 4/4, or 6/8 and 4/4).

## Done

1. **Hard constraints and soft qualities separated** (`sightReadingScore.ts`, new): the hard layer is what the generator had (promises, taught material, range, metre, key, physical bounds, `unrealisable`) plus S26's two constraints (`hardViolations`); a draw that breaks one is never scored (`chooseCandidate`, tested with a spy). Technical: deterministic from the seed (tested per level). Pedagogical: the endings change as described; unverified as music.
2. **The scorer's parts**, each a pure function with its constructed cases and its weight's reason: beginning, arrival (the reviewer's rule, 6/8 and 7/8, the approach from level 5), contour (on the beats; rocking, sitting and random turning cost it), motif (from level 2; exact repeats beyond one cost), rests (levels 3–7), harmony, leaps (a soft cost below the cap).
3. **S26 as a hard constraint**: red first with seed 71282 from the row, and levels 3–4's off-beat ties; `unrealisable` declares neither way past a held cap at version 2.
4. **Identity**: `SightReadingResult.generator` `{ family: 'sight-reading', version, seed }` in D0's shape, `version` an option, bumped to 2 for the new music; **stopped at the history's schema** (Not done).
5. **The distribution suite** with the table, the bounds with reasons, red on the committed generator for phrase ending, contour and S26, green after, local budgets.
6. **The reader's read**: 21 phrases rendered and read (above).
7. **Docs**: `05` §8 (the phrase chosen for its shape; the two `unrealisable` sentences marked version 1; the level-2 tie note; row 7's right hand); `08` (a row and two file entries).

- *S26, the search, the floor*, 69: `the generator reports its search (the committed generator reports none)` — not built there;
- `sightReadingScore.test.ts`: seed 71282 `expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal []` (its two leaps after ties); a hundred seeds of the row with ties, 29 failing; level 3's ties off the beat at seeds `1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, …(21)`; `unrealisable` still names the tie's closing note; level 5 held to steps, seed 1 over the cap; the identity and report cases, not built.

## Unverified, beside what passes

- **Heard: nothing.** Every phrase is unverified as music; the teacher's read is of notation, and a rendered read is not evidence of musical feel (the reviewer's finding 8).
- **What a learner meets is unchanged**: version 1 stays in force until the record carries the version. The promise suite on version 2's phrases passed only in the scratch flip (below), not in CI.
- **The bounds** are set from these seeds; a different seed set would move every share by a few points (two to three at 150–200 phrases). The committed-generator reds are deterministic on these seeds.
- **The suite's page counts of promised demands** (density) are simple counts on the written notes, not the detectors; presence is also held by the promise suite through the detectors.
- **Timing**: the suite alone took about 18 s on this machine; version 2's phrase costs about sixteen of version 1's draws. Nothing was timed on a phone.
- **The rendering** is OSMD drawing the written files in a static page (Playwright on port 4183, `scripts/shots.mjs`), not the app's score screen with its layout.

## Not done

- **The identity in the learner's history (the brief's stop).** Carrying the version needs: `SessionRow.generator?: { family, version, seed }` in `data/db.ts` — an optional field on a value, no `DB_VERSION` bump and no upgrade (C1's rule in `db.ts`) — written by the Score screen from the phrase (`ScoreScreen.ts`, the run it records and `generateSightReadingFor`), read by the evidence job (`candidatePhrases` passes the row's version, absent meaning 1) and by the phrase-seen checks (`ScoreScreen.ts` `phraseSeen`, `session.ts`'s daily-met and seeds-on-record compare seed and version); then `SIGHT_READING_IN_FORCE` becomes 2. Outside D1's files (a screen and `db.ts`), so left for the reviewer; until then the scorer ships behind no identity and the app writes version 1.
- **`fromCatalog.ts`**: not touched — it builds no sight-reading drill, so it holds no identity to version.
- **A downbeat arrival at levels 2–7 in 4/4**: impossible without a bar-long final note in their palettes (a new cell, not D1's).

A leap distribution weighted to steps and skips, or a walk with a contour it aims for, is the realiser's change the scorer cannot make (D3's study will need the same).

### Entry 95 — D2: the microscope and the human review record — one builder-only route where a person sees an item drawn by the app's renderer, plays it through the app's audio, reads its contract and measured facts beside it, and records decisions one dimension at a time, bound to the item's identity; an append-only record merged idempotently from an exported file; the build reading it into every item's provenance and the rung-claims report; the first decision made through the screen and merged (2026-09-27)

**Judgement: the screen as a reviewer meets it, one music-family item from queue to decision.** Driven through the screen in headless Chromium at 342 × 740 (the owner's width) and 1280 × 800, on this worktree's build; the pictures are in `pictures/`. **Nothing was heard by a person**: I cannot listen, so the one decision I made rests on the notation, and says so.

- **The queue.** `#/dev/microscope` opens on the first tier, *Music families · 46*, the chip pressed, the picker listing the 46 canonical items of the fourteen music families and `meter`'s twelve-eight row, each marked `··` (undecided), `✓·` or `✓✓`. The tumbao in C (`exercise.tumbao.c`) is 41st of 46. On a phone the tiers scroll in one row and ◀ / ▶ step within the tier, so the item's title and notation start in the first screenful (`queue-342x740.png`).
- **Seen.** At 342 px the stage takes the whole width of the phone, as the Score screen's does, and draws what the Score screen draws there: the same three buffers (bar 1 in the window, bar 2 beside it, bar 3 dimmed ahead), engraved at the same widths and scaled 0.563 against the Score screen's 0.5625 — the stages differ in height by the Score screen's own rows — measured on both screens in one browser. I read the eight bars one window at a time (`tumbao-342x740-window-1.png` … `-8.png`): bass clef under an empty treble staff, three flats, 4/4; every bar the contract's figure — a dotted-quarter rest, the chord's fifth on the and of two (G2 over Cm, C3 over Fm, finger 2), an eighth rest, the next chord's root on four (F2, then C2, finger 5) tied over the barline; Cm and Fm alternating; bar 8's anticipation ending on the final barline. The notes read here were cross-checked against the file's own events (music21, bar by bar).
- **Played, not heard.** *Hear it — both hands* started the app's piano at the written tempo (♩ = 88, 100 %), scheduled exactly the item's pitches (C2 F2 G2 C3, the left hand; the right hand has none, so *Right hand alone* is disabled) and, played to the end, turned on the `heard` basis for that visit; a stop part way says "a partial playback stays notation" and leaves it off. Headless Chromium renders to a null device: the path ran, nobody listened.
- **The facts beside it**, each under its own hook: the identity the decision binds to (generator `tumbao` v1, seed `null` — "a deterministic family: the recipe is the identity" — recipe and tempo); role canonical; promise *music*, "a bass pattern with the chord anticipated"; *unheard*; target syncopation, also tie and dotted-quarter; every measured demand with its located count and the contract's verdict — `rhythm.syncopation` 8, **required, at density**; `interval.leap` 11, `rhythm.ties` 7, `rhythm.dotted-quarter` 7, `clef.bass` 16, `pitch.ledger` 4 established and assumed; `interval.step` 4, `range.beyond-position` 1 incidental; the physical limits (one-hand span 12, a leap of up to 14 semitones with at least a second, fingering "the generator's own convention, not a published source"); the provenance facts as E0 labels them; the one rung listing it, `latin`, where syncopation is established, the walking bass absent, and clave, tumbao, montuno, comping, bossa nova and tango need a person's judgement; and "No review of it yet".

Four things the reviewer should hear first:

- **The brief's identity hypothesis is half wrong: `drill.generator` is not an item's identity.** The seed is `null` on every family the plan ships, so the triple names 63 identities for 1,176 items (read from the built generated catalogue). Every item in C of one family shares one triple. The identity is G21's: the triple **and** the recipe that wrote the notes (`drill.params` with the hands, and the tempo) — so a recipe changed without a version bump (bars 8 → 4) makes the old decision stale, which the triple alone would miss (case `ev-case5-b`). A notated item's identity is the built file's sha256, E0's cache key, as the brief supposed; the screen hashes the bytes it rendered, and the merge refuses a line whose identity the catalogue no longer has.
- **The Hear it hypothesis holds, on a two-hand groove first.** On the Latin groove (`exercise.latin-groove.c.son-3-2`) the app's `ScoreSession` Listen run, built by the microscope and recording nothing, scheduled only the right hand's pitches for *Right hand alone* (63 67 68 72), only the left's for *Left hand alone*, and both for *both* (the e2e holds it; probe in the browser pane first). Each hand alone is the app's own "play the hand you are not practising". No product change.
- **Found while proving it: the Score screen's Hear it is silent when the screen is opened by address.** `ScoreScreen` builds its session with `audioEngine.contextOrNull` at load, before any gesture on a fresh open (a reload, a link, a home-screen shortcut to a piece), and the session keeps that `null` for the whole visit. Probe (`probe-score-hear.txt`): sample starts after Hear it, opened by address, **0**; opened after a tap on another screen, 5. P0, a learner screen's, not fixed here (Follow-ups). The microscope builds its session inside the first Hear it tap, so it does not share the fault.
- **The report's data reaches the screen through the build**, not through a Python-free recomputation: the reports step writes `content/review/microscope.json` (the queue, each item's contract verdicts, rungs and claims, and the record's events), about 2.6 MB, which the PWA does not precache (`vite.config.ts` `globIgnores`, one line). That is a build step outside "the `reviewed` facts only", and the one vite line outside the brief's list; the reason is that the screen must show the rung-claims report's data and the contract's verdicts, and the app can read neither `build/` nor `tools/`. The alternative, recomputing claims and verdicts in TypeScript, is a second definition of both.

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**Per-dimension resolution (the reviewer's required change).** *Hypothesis:* one event per dimension, resolved per item and dimension by time among valid human events, keeps R42's two truths apart. *Alternatives, each spliced into the resolver and run against the shared cases:* one basis per item, the strongest winning across both dimensions (the brief as first drafted); line order instead of time order; the identity ignored; a triage line counted. *Result:* each turns the cases red, in both languages — Python `red-resolution-mutations.txt` (four mutants, four reds), TypeScript `red-unit-record-mutations.txt` (four mutants — the fourth an unidempotent merge — each red on the case written for it; `record.ts` restored byte for byte after each).

**One contract, two implementations.** The build's half (`review.py`) and the screen's half (`record.ts`) read one fixture of cases (`tools/content/tests/fixtures/review_cases.json`), and a Vitest case holds the screen's resolution equal to the build's bits on every built item, hashing each built file as the screen does.

**The build's reviewed facts.** *Test:* `test_review_record.TestTheBuildFillsTheReviewedFacts`, called as the committed build calls `attach_provenance`, red on the committed provenance step (`red-build-reviewed-facts.txt`: `{'score': None, 'teaching': None} != {'score': True, 'teaching': None}`), green after.

**`heard` held to the record.** *Test:* the committed table with `tumbao` marked heard and nothing heard in the record: red (`red-heard-consistency.txt`: "tumbao is marked heard with no heard decision on a current item of it"); the table as committed: green. The adversaries — no decision, a notation decision, a stale identity, a triage line — each fail; a heard decision on a current item passes; `heard: false` beside a heard decision is allowed (never the reverse).

**The route and the learner's stores.** The microscope spec against a build whose router and shell are the committed ones (the microscope unreachable): 4 of 4 red, "element(s) not found" on the screen (`red-e2e-committed-app.txt`; the navigation case's own assertions pass on both by design — it fails there on opening the item first). Against a mutant whose microscope records a run when Hear it is stopped: the store case red, the diff naming a new `progress` row, a `sessions` row and the streak's minutes (`red-e2e-mutant-writes-a-run.txt`). So the byte-identity check sees a write; on D2's build it passes.

**The queue's stand-ins.** A family with no canonical item at all (`power_chord` ships A, D and E; its contract makes C canonical) is stood in for by its first item. The first rule stood in for families whose canonical items were already in the first tier (`intro`, `modal_vamp`, `riff`, `stride`, `secondary_rag` — music families the app also does not judge); the queue test caught it (`red-queue-standin.txt`), and the rule now stands in only where a family has no canonical item anywhere.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **Time order decides; `supersedes` is recorded, not required.** One reviewer on one device is the expected case, and time order needs no chain repair when a line is lost; the screen writes `supersedes` when it knew what it replaced, for the reader. Ties go to the later line.
- **`at` always carries milliseconds and `Z`,** so the strings sort as the times they name (`…:56Z` sorts after `…:56.789Z`; the short form is refused).
- **A bit is `yes` → true, `no` and `fix` → false**: E0's schema and type keep `boolean | null`, and "usable as it stands" is false for a score that needs a fix; the value, basis, date and event id are in the `reviewed` fact beside it (`reviewedScore`, `reviewedTeaching`). No app code reads the bits; `claims.py` counted only true ones as "reviewed", and now counts any decision.
- **The reviewer's name stays in the record and the screen's data, not in the catalogue**: the fact carries the event id, which leads to it.
- **Categories**: the usable score's from R42's list (notation, transcription, fidelity, identity, rendering, playback, other); the teaching use's from R42 and Part 15 §18 (role, opportunity, demands, physical, musical shape, style, usefulness, placement, other).
- **The screen's decisions live in localStorage under `pianopath.microscope.*`**, not a new IndexedDB store: no schema version bump, no path near a learner store, and the e2e compares every IndexedDB store and every other localStorage key.
- **`heard` is offered only after a complete both-hands playback at 100 % in that visit** — the screen enforces what the record means; a person can still choose `notation` after hearing.
- **Hear it is the Score screen's path** (`ScoreSession`'s Listen run through the shared piano), not a playback helper: the same scheduler, the same piano, the same tempo map, which is what "the app's audio" has to mean. Built inside the first tap, for the reason above. No helper file was needed.
- **The notation is drawn from the learner's display settings, as the Score screen draws it**, and on a phone the stage breaks out of the card to the screen's width, because the renderer's bars per window follow the stage's size; at 342 px the two screens were measured drawing the same buffers.
- **`review.py --check` exits 1 only for a fault in the record** (a refused line, an event on an item the catalogue does not have), never for undecided items: nearly all of the catalogue will stay undecided for a long time, and a check that is always red says nothing.
- **Within tiers:** families in name order; rung options in the curriculum's order with generated before authored before imported; the rest by source, then id.
- **The reviewer's name for my decision is "D2 builder (Entry 95)"**: what I am in this repository, and no model's name.

### Entry 98 — U67: `Hear it` sounds after a reload — the Score screen's session asks for the audio context and its master gain, as one pair, at every start, frame, latch and resume instead of keeping the none it was built with before the first tap; the first tap awaits the engine's start where the context is not running; a browser case opened by address counts sounds at `Piano.start` and the metronome's click, red on the committed screen (2026-09-27)

**Judgement.** A learner who reloads on a piece, or opens a link straight to one, and presses `Hear it` once: on the committed screen no piano note was scheduled (`Received: 0` after a 30 s wait), and with the click on, no click either; `▶` in Listen was as silent. After a tap on another screen first, notes were scheduled on both builds. After U67 all four cases schedule notes (and clicks, where the click is on) within the wait, opened by address. Read from the app's own count at the scheduling boundary (`window.__pianopath.audioStarts`), in the Chromium the suite drives. **Nothing heard by a person**, and no screen looked at beyond what the cases assert. Not exercised anywhere: a phone's refusal to start audio before a tap. This Chromium ran the app's context before any tap even under `--autoplay-policy=document-user-activation-required` (a probe that captured the app's own context as it was made, `probe-autoplay-document-activation.txt`), so the tap's wait for the sound to start is reasoned from the code.

## The mechanism, and the test that told it from the alternatives

**Hypothesis (D2's):** `ScoreScreen` built the session as the piece loaded with `audioContext: audioEngine.contextOrNull` and `destination: audioEngine.masterGain`, both null before any gesture, and the session read those construction options at every boundary for the whole visit. The immediate cause is an ordering inside one function: the session was built at line 4258 and `getPiano()`, which creates the context through `ensureStarted()`, was called at 4336, just after. **Alternatives:** the piano never loaded after a reload; the context existed but was suspended. **Test:** the browser case counts calls at `Piano.start` with the samples loaded. By address it read 0 while the control, a tap on another screen first, read above zero in the same build. The two cases with the click on read 0 clicks, and the metronome needs no piano, so an unloaded piano does not explain them. A probe that captured the app's own context as it was made read it as `running` before any tap (`probe-autoplay-document-activation.txt`), so a suspended context does not explain them in this browser either. What was left was the missing context in the session, and the fix removes it.

**The change.** `ScoreSession` takes an optional `audio: () => SessionAudio` provider. Every boundary (`schedulePlayback`, `onLatched`, `startMetronome`, `startMetronomeOnGrid`) reads the context and the destination together from `audioNow()`, one call for both. The Score screen passes `() => ({ context: audioEngine.contextOrNull, destination: audioEngine.masterGain })`. `ScoreSession` never makes or owns a context. Without a provider, the static `audioContext`/`destination` options are read as before, so the microscope and the existing tests are unchanged. `toggleHear` awaits `audioEngine.ensureStarted()` before the toggle where the context is not running. It runs at once, as before, where the context is running, where there is no Web Audio, or when the tap is a stop. A second tap during the wait is ignored, and a screen torn down during the wait does nothing.

**Provider, not setter (the brief left it to me).** I built the setter first (`setAudio({ context, destination })`, called at every `startRun` and before both `session.resume()` sites). The full unit run then failed 13 tests in `scoreMidRunSettings`, `scoreSummaryTruth`, `scoreTourRoute` and `observationsFromRun` (`run-vitest-all.txt`, "setAudio is not a function" 30 times): their hand-written session doubles have no such method. The brief requires that test doubles keep working unchanged. A provider is a construction option the doubles already ignore, and it meets the brief's condition for one: the gesture still awaits `ensureStarted()` first, and each boundary reads the pair in one call.

**Item 3, the resume sites and the Play path.** The red case proved the ordinary ▶ path silent too: the session held null whichever button started it, so the app-level first-gesture start alone never reached the session. With the provider, ▶, both `session.resume()` sites, the long-press bar preview and every other start read the live pair. Nothing else resumes or creates a context: `AudioEngine` remains the one owner. ▶ does not await `ensureStarted()`. It keeps the app-level first-gesture contract, and making the core practice button asynchronous risked a ▶ that does nothing when a resume never settles. On a first tap the context may be suspended for a moment; a count-in covers that moment for notes.

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**The unchecked phrase (finding 1).** *Premise checked at the lines.* The brief's policy — "continue drawing within `PROMISE_ATTEMPTS`, return the first window that yields a valid candidate" — was already D1's loop: the candidate window opens only at the first valid draw (`attempt > firstValid + CANDIDATE_WINDOW`), and until then the loop runs on to the budget. So `chooseCandidate` returned `undefined` in exactly one case, a whole budget with no valid draw, and then `compose` returned whatever the last draw had left in `rightBars`/`leftBars`. *Hypothesis:* that fall-through is the only way an unchecked phrase leaves version 2. *Alternative:* a valid-looking chosen phrase could still break the hard layer or a promise. *Test:* read every returned phrase back from its MusicXML and check it independently of the generator (`brokenOnThePage`: `hardViolations` on the page's model, each promise counted on the written notes). On D1's `compose` the three cases that reach the zero-valid path each came back with a phrase that broke the rule named in the red line (below); on D1a they throw `SightReadingRefusal`; the valid cases' pages break nothing at either version. *Change:* the fall-through became a refusal carrying its reasons (`refusalReasons`: what was asked, the promises and rules with the draws spent, what the draws broke, and `unrealisable`'s own sentences). Nothing else in the search moved, so version 2's phrases where a valid draw exists are D1's note for note (the distribution suite and the promise suite green unchanged).

**How often the path is reached.** *Sweep* (`runs/probe-sweep.txt`): every level, each hand (R, both, L), 4/4 and 6/8, no option and each control on and off, the realisable ones (`unrealisable` empty): 536 option sets, six seeds each, 3,216 phrases. Every phrase found a valid draw; of 49,930 draws that kept their promises none broke the hard layer — version 2's walk respects the cap and the tie rule by construction, so `hardViolations` is a check that has not yet fired on a promise-keeping draw there. *The rarest recipes* (`runs/probe-exposure.txt`, 2,000 seeds each): level 2's right hand in G with the raised fourth, ties, dotted quarters, skips and eighths needed at most 1,238 draws to its first valid; the two-hand version with a ledger line, at most 1,905; row 4's accidental, at most 93. None refused. The budget is 4,096. So the refusal is reached, in what was tried, only by options that contradict themselves (which the reader never composes: it refuses any move that adds an `unrealisable` reason). That is why two regressions use a test seam (`sightReadingReportWithin`: a smaller budget, or a hard-layer cap tighter than the walk's) — to drive the path on ordinary options.

**The run's identity (finding 2).** A seed names one phrase per version (G21), and 815 of the 1,004 keys of the unchanged golden write other music at version 2 (`runs/golden-diff.txt`; the left hand read alone at levels 2–7 and the seeds whose first draw was already within the tolerance of the best do not). *Every reader that keys on a row's seed*, found by `\.seed\b` over `app/src` and decided:

| Reader | What it asks | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScoreScreen` `phraseSeen` | has a stored run met this phrase? | seed **and** version (`phraseVersionOf`, absent = 1) |
| `session.ts` daily-met (`readingOffer`, `purpose: 'daily'`) | is today's phrase already on the record? | seed, day **and** version in force |
| `evidenceJob.candidatePhrases` | write the stored run's phrase again | by the row's version; absent = 1; a version this build cannot write → `phrase-differs` |
| `ScoreScreen` `seedsOnRecord` → `freshSeed` | which seed may the screen draw? | **every** seed on record, any version (below) |
| `session.ts` slot seeds (`onRecord`) | which seed may the slot offer? | **every** seed on record, any version (below) |
| `progressStore.recordRun` → `markDailyRead` | tick the day's habit | unchanged: it reads only the run being recorded, which the version in force wrote |
| `evidence.ts` (context), `TodayScreen` (route), `review/record.ts` (D2's catalogue identity) | not a phrase-seen check | untouched |

*The avoid-sets are the one place I did not compare the version, a deviation from the brief's list ("session.ts's … seeds-on-record checks").* Their question is which seed may be drawn, not whether a phrase was met. Keeping every seed costs nothing in a 32-bit space; comparing the version would let a seed read under version 1 be offered again, and a seed can write the same notes at both versions (7 of 30 two-bar level-1 seeds probed, `probe-differ.ts`; 189 of the golden's 1,004 keys). Guarded by a test (below). The same fact limits the decided rule for the phrase-seen checks — Follow-ups, P2.

**Why the reader's order changes at 3.1 — traced, not inferred** (`runs/trace-reader-31.txt`, the same two seeds and recipe read at each version). D1 inferred that level 2's leaps came only from the tie fault. Half right. *In the melody*, yes: over 200 phrases of the 3.1 recipe (both hands, beyond position, dotted quarters, ties), version 1 leapt a fourth or wider in 62, every one of them after a tie's closing note, none elsewhere; version 2, none. The rows as they stand at 2.5 and 3.4 leap in no phrase at either version (level 2 ties nothing unless asked). *In the reads*, no: the leaps detector reads **both staves**, so the left hand's roots moving by a fourth or fifth count too. Version 1's two clean reads: seed 7000's melody has no leap, its left hand leaps in bars 2 and 4; seed 7001's melody leaps a fourth after the tie in bar 4 and its left hand leaps in bars 2 and 3 — leaps shown in 2 phrases, which is the reader's "shown" (`phrases − below ≥ 2`), so it skipped `interval.leap` and offered the key signature. Version 2: seed 7000's phrase leaps in the left hand (bars 3–4), seed 7001's phrase on neither staff — 1 phrase, not shown — so the first taught demand (`interval.leap`, taught at 1.5) the phrase does not promise and the reads have not shown comes on. **The new order at 3.1 after two clean reads of that recipe: a leap in the melody first, then, once the reads show one, the key signature as a set of keys.** (In the skip learner's diary the key signature still comes on day 21 and the leap on day 26 at both versions: its reads differ.)

**Why the ambiguity learner's day 3 changed** (`runs/trace-ambiguity-day3.txt`). The learner is constructed: "the first date whose two daily phrases carry enough skip-eighths for the misreads to go against the recipe". On 3 November version 1's phrases had 4 and 5 skip-eighths (18 of 22 and 14 of 19 right: both against); version 2's phrase of 3 November's first seed has none (13 of 13), so day 3 held ("Another like it"). Searching from 1 November at version 2, the first date whose two phrases both go against is **6 November** (13 of 15 and 16 of 18). The test's condition was right; its date was version 1's.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **Refuse by throwing, not by a union return.** `generateSightReading` keeps its type, so no caller can take a refusal for a phrase; the callers that must show or survive it catch `SightReadingRefusal` (the Score screen shows it; Today's reader takes the key from it; the evidence job's loop already treats a thrown write as not matching). A union would also have forced an edit into the untouched `sightReadingPromises.test.ts`, which the typecheck covers.
- **The refusal's reasons in `unrealisable`'s shape**, and for the contradiction cases `unrealisable`'s own sentences appended: "A melody held to steps cannot leap." is the concrete cause there. No seed in the words (an identifier; it stays on the refusal as `generator`).
- **`generator` on `RunHeader`, beside `recipe`**, so `SessionRow.generator` exists and the run a screen hands `recordRun` (`RunResult`) carries it too without touching `progressStore.ts`; `version` typed as a number, because a row outlives the code that wrote it. No `DB_VERSION`: C1's rule in `db.ts` (lines 34–37 before this change: "every field is optional on a value, which IndexedDB does not describe — so they are not a version"). No reader validates row shapes strictly (`backup.importAll` copies rows whole; compaction and `replaceSessionEvidence` spread them), so the deviation clause did not apply.
- **The refusal's reason in the stage**, not the header: the header's `.score-status` is one line, `nowrap` with an ellipsis at 65 % of the row (`style.css`), and the first render showed the sentence cut after a few words. A paragraph where the music would be (`.score-refusal`, 13 lines of CSS).
- **Today's reader and the refusal** (`keyOfPhrase` in `session.ts`, outside the seed checks): the reader asks the generator for a phrase only to name its key; a refusal there would have thrown inside `readingOffer` and taken Today down. The key is chosen before any draw, so the refusal carries it.
- **The goldens: version 1's pinned, version 2's recorded beside it**, rather than re-recorded over: the pinned golden is the proof that version 1 is note for note what it was (its hashes did not move), and the new one records what version 2 wrote when it went into force. Version 2's golden has its own time budget (1,004 phrases of up to sixteen scored draws timed out at the default under the full parallel run and passes alone).
- **The ambiguity learners' start moved to 6 November** rather than the test's day-3 expectation changed: the day-3 demonstration is the point of the learner, and its construction rule names the date.
- **The 3.1 case split in two**: the new order asserted (the leap first), and the key-signature case kept with its premise made true (reads that show a leap).

## The diaries compared (`diaries/compared.txt`)

Both at the same dates, only the version differing (the ambiguity learners' new start, 6 November, at both).

- **The skip learner, 30 mornings.** The reader decides the same move on every morning at both versions: both hands on day 3, the skip control off by day 6, dotted quarters on 12, ties on 15, "the next step waits" on 20, the key signature on 21, a note outside the key on 24, a leap on 26. The phrase (and so the reading's count) differs on 25 of 30 mornings; 18 Today lines, and the card's reading-slot line on the same 18 mornings, differ only in the count they cite ("14 of 14 right" where version 1 said "13 of 13"); the other 12 are word for word. Where a phrase differs, "inside/beyond one hand position" can flip with it (days 11, 13, 14, 23, 24, 26, 29, 30). Every changed morning changed for that one reason: another phrase from the same seed.
- **The ambiguity learners, 10 mornings each.** At version 1 on these dates day 1's read was not against the recipe (12 of 13), so day 3 held; at version 2 both reads go against (13 of 15, 16 of 18) and day 3 is "An easy one: in C position — not sure yet what went wrong", as the learner is built to show. After that (b) never names a demand and keeps saying it is not sure (days 3, 4, 7, 8), and (a) moves the rhythm control (eighths off on day 4) — the demonstrations the test holds, at version 2.
