**Judgement.** This is plumbing: no learner screen changed, and there is nothing to hear or judge as music. The builder's screen was checked by `microscope.spec.ts` (four cases: the item drawn and settled, every fact under its hook, Hear it through the app's piano, a decision exported and merged), not looked at by a person.

- **P19 on the committed tree**, rebuilt in this worktree (`red-e2e-committed.txt`): `offline.spec.ts:302 › and nothing under content/ is served without being precached (P19)` red, "1 file(s) are served but never cached", and the received list is `"content/review/microscope.json"`. That is CI run 36361532736's failure word for word (`ci-36361532736-log-failed.txt`).
- **P19 after the move** (`run-e2e-final.txt`): green, and the case's text is unchanged. There is no exception in it. The projection now lives under `dev/`, and the walk over `dist/content` finds nothing uncached.

## The mechanism, and the test that told it apart

**Cause.** D2's reports step wrote the projection into the built content (`out_dir / review/microscope.json`), and `globIgnores: 'content/review/**'` kept it out of the precache. P19 walks every file under `dist/content` and requires each one in the manifest, so that file was the one served and never cached. **Alternative:** some other new file under `content/`. CI's list and the local list each name exactly one file, the projection, so the alternative is ruled out.

**The premise, corrected in one line:** the path was set in `review.py` (`MICROSCOPE_FILE`, `write_microscope(out_dir, …)`), not in `build.py`. So the move is made there: `dev_root(out_dir) = out_dir.parent / "dev"`, which is `app/public/dev` for the default build. The identities are still read from `out_dir`. `step_reports` also deletes the copy D2 left at the old path, because a checkout built before D2a keeps it otherwise. The main checkout has one now (seen with `ls`), and that copy would keep a local P19 red until the next build.

**The fetch:** `devUrl()` is a local helper in `DevMicroscopeScreen.ts`, base-aware in the same way `contentUrl` is. I kept it in the screen because the screen is its only consumer and a builder screen, so `curriculum/load.ts`, the learner's loader, stays untouched.

**The ignore pattern moved:** `globIgnores: ['**/node_modules/**/*', 'dev/**']`, and the learner globs are untouched. No learner glob reaches a `.json` under `dev/` today, so the ignore shows up only under a mutant (below).

## The mechanism

The vocabulary could say one rung per demand, chosen as "the first rung whose concepts name it" — first in the file, the order E0a stopped reading as the path. So where two tracks teach a demand, the second was invisible, and after E0a (which reads the path) the jazz track's own teaching counted for nothing.

- **The shape** (`demands.schema.json`): `taughtAt` is an array of rung ids, unique, `[]` requiring `taughtAtNote`. A string or `null` is refused.
- **The rule** (`validate.taught_at_findings`, called by `vocabulary_errors`; warnings printed by `main`): every listed rung exists; no listed rung is on another listed rung's path (`claims.rung_ancestry`: one teaching rung per path); each listed rung's concepts name the demand (`claims.concepts_naming`: `CONCEPT_DEMANDS`, and a skill whose opportunity is that demand alone; a skill coping with several demands names none) — else an error, unless `taughtAtNote` names the rung, which is a hand reading and a warning; and a warning for every rung the derivation gives with no listed rung on its path.
- **Every reader** reads the list, and a demand is taught when any listed rung is in the rung's ancestry or the learner's reached set: `session.taughtAtRung`; the strand's edges (the repertoire claim); the reader's no-rung fallback and its "newest thing added" order (the listed rung on the rung's path); `eligibility.targetDemandsFor` (the demand tier); `claims.rung_claims_of`, `untaught_on`, the generated rows' `taughtAt` column and the inventory's coverage; the TypeScript type (`readonly string[]`). No reader names a demand; no generator is touched.
- **The test-side copies of the flat reading** (`generatorContract`, `composedContract`, `firstThirtyDays`, `readerMovesTheDemand`, `lessonClaimsAboutApp`) read `taughtAtRung` now: with `latin.3` listed, the file's order would credit 4.1–4.4 (stored after `latin.3`) with syncopation. `scoreSummaryTruth`'s constructed two-rung line keeps its own order reading, over the list.

**Discriminating tests.** `jazz.6` against `blues.5`'s ancestry (not in it) tells "taught on its own path" from "taught through the blues"; `blues.5` with `blues.6` listed tells one-per-path from any list; `classical.6`, `chords-pop.6` and `theory.9` tell "any listed rung on the path" from "any listed rung anywhere"; `latin`'s warning tells a derivation the validator enforces from one it only records.

### Entry 100 — D3: the generated study — an 8–16-bar miniature around one target on the family-contract architecture: harmony first from a small grammar with a cadence closing every phrase, the tune drawn and kept only where it keeps the hard layer and clears a musical floor, the left hand an accompaniment texture, fail closed at build time; one musical evaluator for the Python families that promise music, D1's parts ported and twinned with the study's multi-phrase, minor and declared-harmony semantics stated; a distribution suite red on a random walk; 24 studies in the Library on no rung, measured by the attach step, six in the microscope's first tier, three walked and their scores recorded from the notation; a candidate-rungs report instead of any placement (2026-09-28)

**Judgement.** Read from the notation — every study written out bar by bar with its declared chords in nine passes (`read-1.txt` … `read-9.txt`), and three drawn by the app's own renderer through the microscope at 342 × 740 and 1280 × 800 (`pictures/`) — from the distribution table, the gates and the code. **Nothing was heard; every study is unverified as music.**

Three studies as a teacher reads them, the evaluator's verdict beside each:

1. **The canonical interval-reading study** (`exercise.study.interval-reading.c-major.4-4.8bar.sustained.01`, written for 2.1): C D C | E G F | F D E | D C D, the consequent restating bars 1–2 and closing D E D | C, in quarters and halves in C position over one held root a bar (C3, F3, G3). **It reads as an exercise with an accompaniment**, primer-shaped: a real period — a question closing on D over V, an answer on C — with steps against skips throughout, but five notes over a single held note a bar is a reading study, not a piece. The evaluator gives it 0.90 (contour 0.57), comfortably over the floor. We agree on its shape (arrival, cadences, the opening cell restated and varied); what makes it an exercise — the five-note compass and the bare left hand — is outside every part the evaluator has.
2. **The canonical 6/8 study** (`…metre-compound.c-major.6-8.8bar.broken.01`, written for 4.5): C5 D5 C5 | A4 B4 C5 | A4 B4 G4 | G4 B4, then A4 F4 G4 | C5 at the close, in dotted quarters, quarters and eighths over broken chords beamed in threes. **It reads as a small piece**: a line felt in two over a moving bass, a half cadence on B and a dotted-half close; the one weakness a teacher would mark is the close, up a fourth from G after a skip down to F. The evaluator: 0.96 (contour 0.97).
3. **The D-minor syncopation study** (`…syncopation.d-minor.4-4.8bar.broken.01`, transfer, 4.5): A4 B♭4 A4 F4 D4 | D4 E4 D4 C4 D4 on an eighth, off-beat quarters and an eighth, a half cadence on A with C♯ in the bass, the close on D5. **It reads as a small piece built on one rhythmic idea** — and it did not until the walk's preparation: its first recipe put the off-beat notes over blocked chords held a whole bar, so nothing sounded the beat they play against. That is now a recipe rule (a syncopation study's left hand sounds the beat), and the study is over broken chords in quarters. What a teacher would still mark: the tune sits around A4–D4 and the close leaps up to D5. The evaluator: 0.97 (contour 0.97).

The evaluator orders them as I do (0.90, 0.96, 0.97), but by 0.07 at most: it is a floor against a random tune, not a judge of piece against exercise. Across the plan, the studies at 2.1–2.2 (five notes over a held root) read as exercises with an accompaniment; the 6/8, syncopation and pattern-bass studies at 3.6–4.5 read closer to small pieces.

Five things the reviewer should hear first:

- **No study is on any rung, and the candidate-rungs report shows why placement is a person's.** For every 2.1 study it lists 2.1 — and `blues.7` and `ragtime.9`, because the left hand's root motion (C–F, G–C) establishes those rungs' "leaps" concept at density. The report is exactly `claims.py`'s reading (a test holds it rung by rung), and that reading happily offers a primer piece to the last rag rung.
- **D0's musical hook never matched.** It compared `row["promise"]`, a list, with the string `"drill"`, so every family, drills included, read "applies, not evaluated"; nothing consumed the difference. Fixed with the gate (red on the committed hook).
- **The microscope says two false things about a study** (D2's screen, not mine to change; Follow-ups): its musical line says no evaluator exists, and "Contract requires but the notes lack" lists the other targets' requirements because the screen ignores a rule's `when` — a fault for every family with conditional requirements, seen first here.
- **An unheard study can reach a learner's swap sheet** through E0's demand and skill tiers — as the unheard grooves already do, and as the microscope itself says ("it reaches a learner only through the Library or a swap"). That is Library behaviour, not placement; whether unheard music-family items belong in swap tiers before their teaching use is decided is the reviewer's question (Questions).
- **The floor separates, it does not identify.** On forty seeds of each canonical recipe every grammar study scored at least 0.86 and the random walk's median 0.74–0.78 (68–92 % of walks below 0.80); a walk that happens to take a shape passes, and the deviation clause is not taken.

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**Bridge or port (item 3).** *Hypothesis:* D1's scorer can be called over the written file, the way `demands.py` calls the detectors. *What decided it:* not the file — D1's own helper reads MusicXML, so the bridge's precondition held — but the semantics: the scorer reads degrees in a major key from the signature, infers each bar's chord from the left hand's first note and treats the phrase as one unit. A study in A minor read that way closes on the sixth degree (`TestTheMinor`: D1's reading of an A-minor close gives `endsOnTonic` false and arrival 0.75; the study's, 1.0); a first-inversion V is read as vii (`TestTheDeclaredHarmony`); an antecedent that stops short is invisible to a single-phrase arrival (`TestMultiPhraseSemantics`: D1's rhythm grade 1.0 on the whole, the study's arrival 0.30 on the stopped phrase and 0.77 over the period). Changing the scorer to read a study is a change to the sight-reading generator's module, which D3 may not make. So: ported, and held equal on 51 constructed phrases by both languages (the twin), and the study's semantics composed on top of the ported parts, each with its own cases.

**The hook that never matched (found building the gate).** D0's `musical_gate` compared `row["promise"]` — a list of rules — with the string `"drill"`, so it never matched and every family, drills included, read "applies: true, not evaluated". Nothing consumed the difference (the census asked only whether a gate claimed an evaluation, and the microscope computes its own line from the promise), so no screen showed it. Red on the committed hook (`red-hook-gate.txt`: `test_the_gate_evaluates_only_where_the_row_names_an_evaluator`, `True != False` for `scale`), green now: the promise is read per recipe (the `meter` family is a drill in 5/4 and music in 12/8).

**Render and read before the suite (the brief's first inherited hypothesis).** *Hypothesis:* accompaniment textures and constrained draws make a small piece, not an exercise with an accompaniment. *Test:* the 24 studies written and read as notation, bar by bar with the declared chords (`read-1.txt` … `read-9.txt`, the first before any distribution was measured), and each fault a teacher would circle traced to its mechanism and fixed in the grammar, the construction or the study's stated semantics — never by adding weight:

| Read | Mechanism | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the motif part 1.0 on every draw; any two bars of half notes "recur" | D1's motif counts any two bars sharing a rhythm | the study's motif is the *opening* cell's recurrence (`study_motif`), with its adversary |
| `C4h C4h`, `D4h D4h` closing phrases | the cadence cell's first note chosen with a weak penalty | hard: a phrase never closes on a repeated note |
| F4 → B4 in the syncopation study; G♯5 → C5 across a phrase join in A minor | only the cap was checked | hard: every melodic interval diatonic in quality (`DIATONIC_SIZES`) |
| `C5q C5q C5e B4e`, three strikes running | a soft weight | hard, and never drawn |
| the close reached by a leap from outside V (F → C) | the approach weighted, not required | the note before a phrase's last a step from it where one exists, else the dominant; hard at the close |
| the five-note studies wandering: one contour in 12 % of four-bar units (the suite's first run) | skips inside five notes turn the line both ways | against the contour's direction only a step back (50 % after, on the final run) |
| D4 on a bass-staff ledger line under `iv` in D minor; nine left-hand moves past an octave | roots placed by the tonic alone, the ledger checked on the root only | roots voice-led from the chord before, every sounding tone checked; two 12.5-semitone returns left, forced by the ledger limit, declared |
| `C C`, `E E` padding the 2.1 tunes | repeats weighted like a small move | the walk's weight on a repeat lowered |
| the D-minor syncopation study's off-beat notes over blocked chords held a whole bar: nothing sounds the beat they play against | the recipe let any texture carry any target | a recipe rule: a syncopation study's left hand sounds the beat (broken, Alberti, waltz); that recipe moved to broken chords, and a refusal case added |

Three came from the gates and the suite, not from reading: the distribution suite (contour, `oneContour 0.125 < 0.45`), the pedagogical gate through the detectors (`forbidden: pitch.ledger is present`) and the physical gate (`leap: LH moves 14 semitones in 0.75 s …, and the row declares no leaps`), each red on the plan as it stood (`runs/dist-draft1.txt`, `runs/run-targeted-1.txt`). The rest came from reading the notation, the syncopation texture while preparing the microscope walk.

**The floor (the "when to deviate" clause).** *Hypothesis:* a floor separates the grammar's studies from the random walk. *Test:* both generators over forty seeds of each canonical recipe, with the same hard layer, harmony and rhythm. Result: every grammar study at or above 0.86 on the page; the walk's median 0.74–0.78 and 68–92 % of walks below 0.80 per recipe; one-contour units 50–99 % against 0–32 %. The floor separates the medians and refuses most walks; it does not refuse every walk — a walk that happens to take a shape is then shaped, and the floor is not a detector of provenance. So the deviation clause is not taken: the evaluator gates.

**The first set (the brief's second inherited hypothesis).** *Hypothesis:* the targets D0 judges can each be placed at a useful density in sixteen bars of music. *Test:* the contract's density for each target, measured by the detectors on every plan study and on the forty-seed sets. Result: all six place, none dropped — each at or above its contract's density in every study (the table's last column). Two needed more than a melody: syncopation needed cells of its own (off-beat quarters, only where it is the target) and, from the walk's reading, a left hand that sounds the beat; 6/8 is a metre, so its density is met by every note in the bar and the study's content is the lilt, not the demand. Hands together is carried by every study; its own recipe differs only by the left hand changing twice a bar, which places at density but which a teacher may not tell from the 2.1 reading study (Follow-ups).

## The grammar (`tools/content/study.py`; `docs/02` Part E2)

Harmony first, then the tune; a grammar and a distribution, never one template.

- **Forms, in four-bar phrases.** 8 bars: an antecedent closing on the dominant (a half cadence) and a consequent restating the antecedent's first two bars and closing on an authentic cadence. 12 bars: antecedent, a contrasting phrase closing on the dominant, consequent. 16 bars: antecedent, consequent, contrast, and the consequent again. The restated bars are declared (`drill.study.restated`), and neither the evaluator nor the pedagogical gate counts them as repetition.
- **Progressions.** Antecedent `I x y V`, with `x y` one of `IV I`, `vi IV`, `I IV`, `V I`, `ii IV`. Consequent: the antecedent's first two chords, then `V | I`, `V7 | I`, `IV V | I` or `ii V | I`. Contrast: `IV I IV V`, `vi IV I V`, `IV V I V`, `ii IV I V`. Minor: `i x y V` with `x y` from `iv i`, `VI iv`, `i iv`, `V i`; closing `V | i`, `V7 | i`, `iv V | i`; contrast `iv i iv V`, `VI iv i V`, `iv V i V`. The minor's dominant carries its leading tone (spelled by interval: E G♯ B in A minor, A C♯ E G in D minor). The hands-together target moves the opening bars of each phrase through two chords a bar (`I V`, `IV I`, `ii V` …), never the cadence's own bar. A chord whose root the left hand cannot reach at the rung is not drawn: at 2.1 the hand keeps a five-note position, so `I ii IV V` (and `V7`, whose seventh a held root leaves to the tune) and not `vi`.
- **The left hand**: the texture over the progression — a held root (at the pre-2.5 rungs within a fifth: C3 D3 F3 G3 in C), blocked chords, broken chords (1-3-5-3; 1-3-5 in 3/4 and twice in 6/8), Alberti (1-5-3-5), a waltz bass (root, then the chord twice); the last bar a root and a held chord, so a pattern stays a pattern in every bar; F2 to middle C, off ledger lines.
- **The tune.** A cell for bar 1 (the motif) from the metre's cells the rung has taught (quarters and halves at 2.1; eighths from 2.2; the dotted quarter from 2.4; off-beat quarters only for the syncopation target), restated or varied in the bars after it; a cadence cell holding each phrase's last note a beat or more (a breath after a half cadence where the cell has one). Pitches by a walk guided toward a contour chosen per phrase (arch, ascent, descent, valley): strong beats on the chord's tones; **against the contour's direction only a step back**; a leap recovered by a step the other way; never a third strike of one pitch; no rocking; the note before a phrase's last a step from it (else the dominant); the consequent restating the antecedent's opening; the contrasting phrase carrying the motif's interval shape to its own chord (a sequence); for position-shift, the contrasting phrase in a second five-note position (up a fourth where the staff has room, else down).
- **The hard layer** (valid first): the rung's taught set in the realiser's own terms (rhythms, the five-note position, the key, off ledger lines), the leap cap (a fifth), every melodic interval diatonic in quality (no tritone, augmented second, diminished fourth or augmented fifth), no pitch struck three times running, every phrase closing on its cadence's tone and not on a repeated note, the close approached by step or from the dominant, the target at the recipe's density (skips and steps; eighths; off-beat notes; the widened position; the right hand sounding at every left-hand strike), no bar repeated exactly beyond the grammar's restatement. A draw breaking any is never scored.
- **The choice**: up to 24 valid candidates within 600 draws, scored by the musical evaluator; those at or above the valid draws' lower quartile of notes (D1's density floor) and at or above the musical floor with no wrong cadence are eligible; the earliest within 0.01 of the best is kept. None eligible: refused with the reason (`StudyRefusal`), and the build stops.

## The evaluator (`tools/content/musical_evaluator.py`), its parts and weights

**Port, not bridge — the call and its reason.** D1's scorer (`app/src/engine/sightReadingScore.ts`) models a four-bar phrase in a major key and infers the harmony from the left hand's first note in a bar; a study has several phrases, may be minor and declares its harmony. A bridge would call a scorer that cannot read a study, and the scorer is the sight-reading generator's module, which D3 may not change. So the parts are ported, and every ported part is held equal to its TypeScript twin on a shared fixture of 51 constructed phrases (`tools/content/tests/fixtures/evaluator_twins.json`): `app/tests/unit/studyEvaluatorTwin.test.ts` holds the scorer to the recorded values (and records them with `STUDY_TWIN_WRITE=1`), `test_musical_evaluator.py` holds the port to the same values. The bridge's precondition — reading a written file — held (D1's helper reads MusicXML); it was the semantics that ruled it out, not the file.

**The study's semantics, stated and tested** (each on a case built to pass and one to fail; parity on major four-bar phrases proves none of them):

- *Degrees in the key's own scale*: the major, or the natural minor with a raised degree read as the degree it raises (D1's rule, which the minor's leading tone needs: G♯ is A minor's seventh degree, a step below the tonic).
- *The harmony declared*: each bar's chords from the recipe's progression (`drill.study.progression`), a note judged against the chord sounding at its onset; never inferred from the left hand (a first-inversion V read from its bass note is vii).
- *An arrival per phrase*: D1's rhythm grades on each phrase's final event, a close judged against that phrase's own cadence (an authentic cadence's tonic, or third or fifth for a half; a half cadence's tone of V), and the approach (by step, or from a tone of the chord before); the phrases' mean, the last counting twice.
- *A cadence per phrase* (a part of its own): the progression has the cadence the phrase claims (V then I; V), and the melody closes on its chord's tone. A cadence on a note outside its chord is wrong, and the gate refuses the item whatever the total.
- *The motif on the opening cell*: the first bar's rhythm under other pitches, or its shape at another pitch, in a bar the grammar does not restate (D1's part counts any two bars sharing a rhythm, which two bars of half notes always do); exact repeats beyond the grammar's restatement and beyond one cost a half each.
- *Contour, rests, beginning, harmony, leaps*: D1's functions as they stand, the harmony read from the declaration.

| Part | Weight | Why |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| arrival | 4 | an ending per phrase is what makes eight bars of legal notes a piece in phrases; below D1's 5 because the cadence now carries part of the ending |
| cadence | 3 | the cadence that makes each ending one, and the authentic close |
| contour | 3 | as D1: one shape per four bars against a line that wanders or rocks |
| motif | 2 | a study promises a cell restated and varied — heavier than in a sight-reading phrase |
| harmony | 2 | a tune agreeing with the progression it declares |
| beginning | 1 | as D1 |
| rests | 1 | as D1; rests fall at a phrase's breath |
| leaps | 0.5 | a tiebreaker below the cap, never a reason to lose the target's skips |

**The floor: 0.80**, below which the realiser refuses a candidate and the gate an item; any wrong cadence refused whatever the total. Set from the distribution table: every study the grammar wrote on the suite's seeds cleared it (the worst 0.86), and the random walk's median fell below it for every recipe (0.74–0.78).

Bounds (the grammar must meet each; the random walk must fail a shape bound on every recipe):
- `refused` <= 0.1: a recipe the plan ships must write: more than one seed in ten refused means the recipe is at the edge of its rung
- `cadence` >= 1.0: every phrase closes on its cadence's tone: the hard layer, measured on the page
- `arrives` >= 0.95: a phrase that stops rather than arrives is the fault Part 15 §9 names first; the cadence cells hold a note a beat or more
- `scoreWorst` >= 0.8: every study kept clears the musical floor, read again on the page
- `oneContour` >= 0.45: at least a phrase in two with one shape; the grammar's lowest recipe (the five-note position at 2.1) sits near half, and the walk falls well below it
- `scoreMedian` >= 0.85: the typical study clears the floor with room: a median at the floor would mean the floor is doing the composing
- `repeats` <= 0.2: a tune that sits on a note (D1's reader's read at level 2) is a degeneracy: at most one move in five a repeat
- `leaps` <= 0.25: at most one move in four a fourth or wider: a study reads by steps and skips, with a leap recovered
- `nearDuplicates` <= 0.1: a seed names a study; two seeds writing one page more than one time in ten is a space too small
- `motif` >= 0.9: the opening cell comes back varied in nine studies of ten: the grammar's promise

**The headline:** the grammar clears every bound on every recipe — no seed refused, every cadence right, every phrase arriving, the worst study 0.86 against the floor 0.80, one contour in 50–99 % of four-bar units, the opening cell varied in 98–100 % of studies, repeated notes 4–15 % of moves, leaps 3–8 %, no near-duplicate, the target at the contract's density in every study — and the random walk fails a shape bound on every recipe (median 0.74–0.78, 68–92 % below the floor, one contour in 0–32 % of units, leaps 23–36 % of moves). The weakest grammar recipe is the five-note study at 2.1 (one contour in half its units; 84 % of its draws refused by the hard layer, within the budget).

## The candidate-rungs report (`candidate-rungs.md` beside this entry)

Written by `python tools/content/study.py --candidate-rungs app/public/content/catalog.json app/public/content/curriculum.json` from the final build; `test_study.TestTheCandidateRungsReport` holds the function equal to `claims.py`'s reading on every study and every rung. For each study: its measured demands with their located counts, what they establish, and every rung whose ancestry has taught all of them **and** one of whose claims they establish, with the claims established and not. In short:

| Studies (recipe rung) | Candidate rungs |
| --- | --- |
| interval-reading, hands-together at 2.1 (six) | 2.1, `blues.7`, `ragtime.9` |
| subdivision at 2.2 (three) | 2.2, `blues.7`, `ragtime.9` |
| position-shift at 2.5 (three) | 2.5, `blues.7`, `ragtime.9` |
| the G-major interval-reading transfer at 3.1 | `blues.7`, `ragtime.9` — not 3.1: its key signature's letters sound five times, below the density that establishes 3.1's claim |
| the waltz and broken-chord studies at 3.6 (three) | 3.6, `blues.4`, `ragtime.5`–`ragtime.9`, `technique.5`, `technique.6`, `blues.7` |
| 6/8 at 4.5 (four) | 4.5 and, for the broken-chord two, the ragtime and technique rungs from 5 up; `blues.7`, `ragtime.9` for all |
| syncopation at 4.5 (four) | 4.5, `latin`, `ragtime.5`–`ragtime.9`, `technique.5`, `technique.6`, `blues.7` |

Read as a teacher: each study's own rung is a candidate where its claims are ones the study establishes, and the rest are artefacts of a mechanical reading — `blues.7` and `ragtime.9` claim "leaps" and a held root's C–F is one; the ragtime rungs claim a left-hand pattern and any broken chord is one. That is the reviewer's reason for placement by a person on a resolved teaching-use review, and the report is the evidence that decision reads, not a recommendation.

## Unverified, beside what passes

1. **Nothing was heard.** Every study is **unverified as music**: the reading is of notation (text dumps of every study, nine passes, and the three walked on the app's own renderer), and the evaluator judges phrase shape from the notation. Whether any study reads to a listener as a small piece is a person's, through the microscope, by hearing.
2. **The evaluator is a model of phrase shape**, D1's parts with the study's semantics; its weights and its floor are mine, each with its reason. It passes every study the grammar writes on the suite's seeds and refuses most random walks; it does not refuse a walk that happens to take a shape, and it knows nothing of idiom, voice-leading between the hands, or register beyond the leap cap.
3. **The distribution numbers are this realiser's on these seeds** (forty per canonical recipe), not product facts; another seed set would move each share by a few points. The variable and transfer recipes are held by the single-item gates, not by the distribution.
4. **The realiser's hard layer is its own construction**, verified on every plan study by the app's detectors (every measured demand taught at its recipe's rung; the contract's densities) — not a Python reading of a demand. A recipe outside the plan is held by the same construction and by the build's gates when it is written, not by the suite.
5. **The candidate-rungs report is `claims.py`'s reading** of the built catalogue: a rung listed there is one whose taught set holds every demand and whose claims the notes establish — never a judgement that the study teaches what the rung teaches. Placement stays F's and the owner's, on a resolved teaching-use review.
6. **The twin holds on 51 constructed phrases**: the port could differ from the scorer on a phrase shape none of them has (a tuplet rest, a 5/4 bar); D1's own distribution suite is not re-run through the port.
7. **The microscope walk** drew three studies with the app's renderer at 342 × 740 and 1280 × 800 in headless Chromium on port 4193; no playback was listened to.

## Not done

- **Nothing of the brief's decided items is not done.** Named so none is claimed: any rung placement (the reviewer's change: F's and the owner's, on a resolved teaching-use review); any teaching-use decision (a person's, by hearing); the microscope's spec (`app/tests/e2e/microscope.spec.ts`) was not re-run — the queue's tiering code did not change (its rule, "a music family's canonical items", took the six canonical studies into the first tier as written), and the brief runs it only if the tiering changes; the walk itself drove the screen on every study it opened.
- **`content/sources/opportunity-density.json` is unchanged**: every target demand already has a row, and a study's own densities are its contract's, which the build's `established_by_contract` reads (the brief allowed an addition; none was needed).
- **The D-minor record line's "and V7"** is owed a superseding line (above); not re-recorded here.

## Questions

1. **Unheard studies on swap sheets.** E0's demand and skill tiers read the whole catalogue through the gate, so a study that establishes a rung's taught demand can be offered as "Also practises …" before anyone has decided its teaching use — the reviewer's worry about placement, by the side door, and already true of the unheard grooves. Keep (Library behaviour, labelled by what the notes hold), or keep unheard music-family items out of the swap tiers until a teaching-use decision exists? A product choice, and an app change D3 may not make.
2. **The 2.1–2.2 studies.** Within a fifth over a held root they read as exercises with an accompaniment. Keep them as reading studies at the first rungs that allow them, or move those targets' canonical studies to 2.5, where the hand may leave its position and the tune can breathe?

## Follow-ups

- **P2, the microscope's musical line (D2's screen; found on the walk).** `DevMicroscopeScreen.ts` prints, for every family promising music, "Promised as music: not evaluated — no musical evaluator exists and no hearing counts until a person hears it here." For the study that is now untrue (the gate evaluates phrase shape), and the study row's own unjudged lines, shown just below it, say so — the screen contradicts itself on a builder-only route. The fix is the screen's and `review.py`'s projection: carry the gate's verdict (`evaluated`, total, floor, wrong cadences) per item into `microscope.json` and print it, keeping "unheard" beside it. Not D3's file.
- **P2, the microscope's "requires but the notes lack" ignores `when` (D2's screen; found on the walk).** `DevMicroscopeScreen.ts` line ~772 filters `family.requires` without the rule's `when`, so a study is told it lacks the other targets' requirements (`range.beyond-position, rhythm.eighths, rhythm.syncopation, metre.compound` on the 2.1 study), and any family with conditional requirements gets the same false warning (the interval drills' bass clef on a right-hand item). The projection (`review.family_projection`) sends the rules whole; the screen, or the projection per item, should select them by the recipe as `family_contracts.selected` does.
- **P3, the record.** The D-minor line's reason says "over V and V7"; the study has V only. A superseding usable-score line through the screen corrects it.
- **P2, swap sheets can offer an unheard study (E0's gate, by design).** The demand and skill tiers read the whole catalogue through `eligibleFor`, so a study that establishes a rung's taught demand at density and brings nothing untaught can appear on that rung's swap sheet as "Also practises …" — as the unheard grooves already do (Entry 92's minor vamp on 2.5). That is Library behaviour, not placement, and D3 changes no app file; whether unheard music-family items belong in the swap tiers before their teaching use is decided is a product question (Questions).
- **P2, the five-note studies (2.1, 2.2).** Within a fifth over a held root the grammar writes primer-level periods; a teacher is likely to call them exercises with an accompaniment. A later recipe could open them with more rhythm (the dotted half at 2.1 is taught, the 3/4 cell `q h` already reads better) or place the canonical interval-reading study at 2.5, where the hand may move.
- **P2, the hands-together target** is carried by every study; its own recipe differs only by the left hand changing twice a bar. It places at density and was kept; a teacher might not tell its canonical study from the interval-reading one except by the left hand. For F: whether coordination wants a study of its own or a harder texture (a moving left hand under a held tune).
- **P3, fingering.** No study prints fingering (G47: a printed number is a claim, and no source covers a generated melody). The position-shift studies are where a teacher would print the shift's finger; that needs a policy with a source, not a convention.
- **P3, record.** Matrix rows G19, G16 (built, unheard), G9 (the Python half built), G22 (the study's suite), G14 (the six stages exist for one family end to end); `catalog.schema.json` gained the kind `study` (outside the brief's list, for the reason in Files).

## The mechanism, and the tests that told it apart

**Cause.** E0's gate answers two questions: can the learner cope, and is the opportunity established. Neither question reads provenance's teaching bit. Since E0, the skill and demand tiers iterate the whole catalogue through the gate. So a study whose notes establish 2.1's hands together, and which brings nothing untaught, passes the gate and reaches the sheet as *Also practises …*. The same-lesson and named stand-in tiers call the same gate with `equivalent`, so a rung's own groove passes there too. **Alternative:** some other path offers them, one that does not go through the gate. **Test:** the call-site table below. Every automatic offer path is an `eligibleFor` call. The regression refuses at the gate and turns every path's case green without touching a caller. `selectors.ts` and `session.ts` are unchanged.

**The fact, not the table, at runtime.** The gate cannot read `family_contracts.json`, and it should not: that would be a second definition beside the build's. So the build writes the promise per item. A runtime drill has no contract row and gets no fact, which covers the nine reading rows. A notated item gets no fact either.

**Where the check sits.** After the physical refusal, which already refuses every want including exploration, and before the unmeasured check and Question 1. A music-promising generated item is always measured, so the order against the unmeasured check changes no answer.

### Entry 103 — D3b: the session card's rows drawn straight from a rung's list pass the gate's own teaching-use admission, exported once from `eligibility.ts` and read in `session.usable`, the one filter every slot chooses through; a music-promising generated item with no affirmative decision reaches no automatic row, the row filled by the slot's next admitted candidate or the ladder's next step, a refused ask left unmet and never said to be met; the Library, exploration and the swap sheet untouched (2026-09-28)

**Judgement.** The card no longer offers an unheard groove because a rung lists it. I checked it on the phone at 342 × 740. I read it from the DOM and compared it row for row with the unit probe. I checked it across the whole curriculum with the unit probe. I also traced the code at every place a slot takes an item. Nothing was heard, and no teaching-use decision was made.

- **At `jam` and at `holiday.5`, before.** A fresh learner with every track on (D3a's probe setting), at 30 and at 60 minutes, got this warm-up: *Ostinato over a pedal bass in A minor — broken minor triad*, "Holiday asks for it — not counted yet", L3.4.
- **After.** The warm-up is *E major arpeggio — 2 oct, both*, with the same line, "Holiday asks for it — not counted yet", now at L5.1. The line is still true: `holiday.5` asks for a run of any one of its exercises, and the arpeggio is one. Every other row is unchanged at both lengths. The DOM equals the unit probe's card for both rungs, both lengths, before and after (`runs/compare-dom.txt`; `pictures/before/card-jam-30.png` and the rest, against `pictures/after/…`).
- **As music: unverified.** The replacement is a two-octave arpeggio, hands together, a level and a half above the ostinato. It is inside a stage-5 rung's band, and it is the rung's own listed exercise.
- **Across the curriculum.** D3a's probe looked at 30 rungs at two lengths. Widened to every rung (109), every length (15, 30, 60, 120), a fresh learner, every track on, the committed code put an unapproved music-promising generated item on **146 rows on 59 rungs' cards**. That is 44 warm-ups the rung "asks for", 50 reviews "Nothing due for review — more from …" and 52 jams. D3a's own scope inside it is 23 rows, reproduced exactly. After: **0**.
  - **Every one of the 146 was filled, none dropped.** 44 took the ask's next admitted exercise under the same line. 50 took the rung step's next admitted option: the stride became *Turnaround in F — iii-VI-ii-V*, the pinetop boogie *Turnaround in C — I-vi-ii-V*, the E♭ walking bass *Ninth chords*, the secondary rag *Play back a tune — eight bars* or *Search-Light Rag*. 52 took the next admitted option of a reached jam rung: comping became *Play the form with the chart* or *add9 voicings in E♭*, the walking bass *Twelve-bar blues shuffle in E* or *I-V-vi-IV in D*.
  - **Knock-on changes.** 116 cards change, every one a card that held such a row. Sixteen knock-on rows moved on them, each because the replacement took an item another slot would have had (`runs/compare-cards.txt`, `runs/changes-grouped.md`).
- **What a teacher would notice among the replacements.** The jam slot and the rung step take a rung's options in list order. With the grooves out, a few non-chord items now sit under "Chords, form and feel": `chords-pop.7`'s second jam at two hours is *Transposition — a harder page, further away*, and `theory.8`'s jam is *Play back a tune — eight bars*. `ragtime.9`'s review is the same ear drill, under "more from Ragtime". These are the rungs' own authored options. That is a property of the jam slot and the rung step that the grooves used to hide (Follow-up 3), not something this seam invents.
- **Two asks cannot be filled until a person decides.** Every exercise `latin.3` lists is a clave or the tresillo, and every one `latin.6` lists is a tumbao, a montuno or a Latin groove. Their exercise asks stay unmet.
  - **`latin.3`, for a learner with only the core path and Latin on.** Its new slot moves from *Clave — son 2-3* ("Latin asks for it") to *Cielito Lindo*, the rung's song ask, with the same line.
  - **`latin.6`.** Its warm-up moves from *Tumbao — latin bass in G minor* ("Latin asks for it") to *Rhythm: syncopated — 4 bars*, "From Clave, tumbao and montuno, which this lesson builds on" (the ladder's prerequisite step). Its review moves from the montuno to *The Crave* or *Por Una Cabeza*.
  - **No row says either ask is met or waits for review** (`runs/compare-focus.txt`). The Latin track cannot be met past `latin.3` through the card until a groove there has a `yes` (Question 2).

Five things the reviewer should hear first:

- **`usable()` is the single filter, and the jam slot already goes through it.** The brief's premise was that the jam slot picks from a lesson's options directly. It does not: `jam` filters by `usable(ctx, item, 'any')` (`session.ts`, the jam function). So one line in `usable` covers the `runs`, `done` and `measure` offers, the ladder's `choose`, the exposure rule and the jam slot. `usable` serves no display-only path; every caller is card candidate selection (table below). The binding answer's deviation therefore did not arise, and no second call site was needed.
- **Pool and offer: what I found and what I did.** `if (pool.length === 0) continue` tests the pool, and I kept it that way. A want's `pool` is never chosen from. It is read only for whether the rung asks something (the `wants.length` tests in `warmup` and `fresh`) and for `fresh`'s `served()` ordering. Every row comes from `pick(want.offer, …)`, and `offer` passes `usable`.
  - A want whose offer is empty after admission produces no row. Its existence routes the slot to the fallback ladder and holds back the next lesson's asks. That is how the code already treats an unplayable candidate, and it is the brief's "the requirement stays unmet … the row falls to the next step of the fallback order".
  - Filtering the pool instead would drop the want. The warm-up would then go to the next lesson's ask under "The next lesson asks for it", a claim whose definition is "this one's asks of this kind are met". That is false. The `pool` mutant shows exactly this (`red/mutant-pool.txt`: the warm-up becomes `ex.next`, `asked`, rung `R2`), and the regressions' `claimsNext` check holds it out.
- **One reading, two askers.** `admittedForTeaching(item)` is `unapprovedMusic(item) === undefined`. `unapprovedMusic` stays the only reading of the promise fact and the teaching bit, and `eligibleFor` still uses it for the verdict with the stored bit. A new case shows the gate's `teaching-use-not-approved` and the admission refuse exactly the same items on the built catalogue, and both agree with the contract table, the oracle independent of the build. Another shows `session.ts` reads neither `facts.promise` nor `review.teaching`.
- **The per-path mutants split the 146 rows by path, with none left over.** Taking the admission off the want's offer brings back 44 rows. Off the ladder, 50. Off the jam slot, 52. Off exposure, none on the built catalogue for these learners, though every constructed card that falls to exposure goes red. Each path's own constructed case goes red under its own mutant, and a `false` read as approval turns every path's `false` iteration red.
- **Nothing learner-facing was added.** There is no "waiting for review" row and no new string (the binding answer). The swap sheet, `selectors.ts`, the gate's logic, the rung lists and the Library are untouched.

## The mechanism, and the test that told it apart

**Cause.** D3a put the teaching-use check inside `eligibleFor`, and every path that asks the gate refuses. The card's own rows never ask the gate for an item a rung lists: a rung's list is taken as the rung's authored ask. Those rows are the `runs`, `done` and `measure` offers, the ladder's rung and prerequisite steps, the jam slot and the exposure rule. They choose through `usable`, which checked playability, the card and reading rows, and nothing else.

**Alternative.** Some other path puts the grooves on the card, such as the repertoire claim or skill retention.

**Test.** The widened probe classifies each of the 146 rows by slot and claim: technique/asked 44, review/rung 50, jam/jam 52. The per-path mutants bring back exactly those counts. Every row is a `usable` path, and admission in `usable` turns every case green.

## Unverified, beside what passes

1. **Nothing heard, no decision made.** The replacements are unverified as music. That includes the arpeggio's level against the ostinato's, and the jam slot now holding a transposition page or an ear drill on a few rungs.
2. **The probe's learners are fresh**, placed at a rung with no runs. A learner with history reaches different slots (retention, counted items). The constructed cases, not the probe, cover those paths' logic.
3. **The phone look covers two rungs at two lengths** (`jam`, `holiday.5`; 30 and 60 minutes), read through the DOM and screenshots, not by a person on a phone. The "full page" pictures equal the viewport because the app scrolls inside its own container, so the 60-minute cards' last row is cut. The DOM JSON has every row.

## Not done

1. **No admission call at the reading slot, the daily read or skill retention.** They take reading rows only. A reading row is a runtime drill with no promise fact (D3a's build case), and the new built-catalogue case shows every item without a contract row admitted. A call there would be a second guard on a fact the build already holds, and a test for it would need a reading row that carries a music promise, which the build cannot make. **The mechanisms, and the hypotheses tested.**

*The object (items 1, 3, 4).* `tools/content/excerpts.py` cuts the parent's **built** file by printed position (`score.measures(from − 1, to, indicesNotNumbers=True)`, as `bisect_render.py` cuts), carries the clef, key, time and tempo in force into the first bar, keeps a pickup when the row starts at bar 1, severs a tie into the first bar to a plain note and drops one out of the last, neutralises a repeat sign at either edge, silences the unselected staff of a one-hand cut and lets `convert.normalise` drop it (one staff), and writes the normalised header: the excerpt's id as the work title, no credits, no encoding date, and the archive's inner entry named after the excerpt. That last was a found fault: the first cut's bytes depended on the output path, because music21 names the inner file after it; renaming the entry and its `container.xml` made two cuts of one definition byte-identical wherever written. The id is `excerpt.<parent id less "song.">.b<from>-<to>[.rh|.lh]`; the key is sha256 over `parentSha256|from|to|selection|cutVersion`; the cut file's sha256 is D2's identity and what a run writes as `material`. The step runs after the parents' files exist and before notation, demands and provenance, which read the cut as any file; a row the cutter refuses stops the build, named. A strict build refuses the cut where it refuses the parent, because the row carries the parent's `source` and licence tags (`TheLicence`, two mutants).

*Positions without cutting (item 5; the brief's second hypothesis).* The bridge (`demandsOfFiles.test.ts` through `demands.py`) now writes, beside each demand's count, its located places per printed bar and staff (each printed note once, however many passes the repeats make), cached in `build/positions-cache.json` on the counts' fingerprint and kept out of the catalogue. **Test:** the proposer's window counts against each cut's own measurement. **Result — the hypothesis fails for three kinds of detector, each named and handled:** `leftHandPattern` and `walkingBass` locate nothing unless every bar of the whole model qualifies, so their places cannot tell a window: the bridge asks each of them of every printed bar alone, the detector itself on a one-bar slice of the model (`everyBar`); `beyondPosition` widens a running span from the start of the piece, so its places do not compose: the bridge writes each hand's lowest and highest pitch per printed bar instead (`hands`); and the key-relative demands (`key.signature`, `pitch.chromatic`) in a window whose key differs from the piece's first key are judged against the first key, so the proposer scores such a window 0 and says only the cut can tell. And a count read in the parent's context can exceed the cut's at the edges: Hark! 25–28 had 7 syncopations by position and measures 5 on the cut, where the tie from bar 24 is severed. Both are above the window minimum; the build's measurement of the cut is what the catalogue carries.

*Phrase boundaries (the brief's first hypothesis).* **Test:** the top window of ten parents against the editions' own marks (double bars, repeat signs, rehearsal marks, slurs, fermatas, breath marks; `propose --edition-check`, `runs/edition-check-final.txt`). **Result:** 5 of 10 starts and 6 of 10 ends agree with a mark. The disagreements are of two kinds: an internal phrase the edition does not mark (Anh. 113's bar 17, after the long note of bar 16), and a phrase that starts on an upbeat in mid-bar (Für Elise's bar 16, Swan Lake's 20, Greensleeves' 9), which a cut of whole bars cannot start at. So the signals were changed before any weight was added: a mid-bar upbeat does not meet `phraseStart` (0.5, with the reason), a long note is a whole bar or the strictly longest note of at least half a bar, a long note or rest that opens a phrase the edition marks is not a phrase end (0.4), a bass change alone marks nothing in this repertoire (0.3), and a cadence is each tonic with its own dominant (C to D minor in F is deceptive). The top-scoring window of a parent may still leave a signal unmet (three of the ten above do): approval asks every signal, not the top score. Each change has its case and its mutant.

*The window rule (item 9).* `perBar` reached and at least `minInWindow` located, in place of the whole-piece `min`; two where the file states none. The values are spliced into `opportunity-density.json` beside each rule's `min`, each with `windowWhy` and `hypothesis: true`; the two every-bar rules keep `hypothesis: false` (their detector is already an every-bar rule). The build writes an excerpt's `measurement.window` — what the window rule establishes that the whole-piece rule does not — and the app's reading in `eligibility.test.ts` and the build rows' case in `test_measured_truth.py` both include it.

*The gate (item 7).* No excerpt branch in `eligibility.ts`: the whole Anh. 113 is refused at `classical.3` (sixteenths, taught at no rung, and triplets, 4.5) and its excerpt of bars 25–32 is eligible there, and eligible *for* `key.signature` (`eligibility.test.ts` › Q8, on the built catalogue; `test_measured_truth` › `test_q8_…`).

*The evidence (item 7).* The Score screen hashes the bytes it loaded for an excerpt (`cutIdentity`) and the run's `material` is that `{ kind: 'file', sha256 }`, carried through the observation into the evidence context beside `itemId` and `seed` and kept on the stored self-assessment; nobody reads it yet. A run is keyed by the excerpt's own id, so the parent is neither passed nor performed by it (`excerptItems.test.ts`).

**Found on the combined build and on the pictures, each fixed with its red first.** (1) The score checks read every excerpt as a truncated copy and an undeclared containment of its parent, and build 2 failed its gate: `score_checks.py` now reads `excerptOf` as it reads `variantOf`. (2) Every excerpt's `keySig` was empty, because `attach_excerpts` runs before `attach_notation`: the key is settled in the provenance pass, the parent's where the parent has one key and the cut prints that signature (a parent that changes key, like Wabash Blues and the Hark! lead sheet, gives none). (3) The Ode excerpt claimed seven concepts, every pattern the one detector answers for: a concept shared under one demand is not claimed. (4) The candidate-rungs report listed 3.6's alberti and blues.4's boogie for an oom-pah excerpt without saying why: the † mark. (5) Three of E0's cases encoded "no excerpt exists" (the tests table). (6) The excerpt view hid the bars before the cut (the judgement above): the page placement moved into `excerptPage.ts`, a pure function with its unit cases. (7) Two faults in my mutant harness, found when a mutant survived: a `FILE::OLD::NEW` separator that split wrongly when the old text ended in a colon, turning eight mutants into syntax errors (false reds), and a stale `.pyc` when a same-length mutation was written in the same second as the last restore, which let one mutant run the previous mutant's code (a false green). The separator is now `@@@`, each mutated run compiles into a cache of its own, and a mutant that then survived (`window-rule-reads-min`, alive under `TestExcerptLocalTruth` alone, whose leap fixture meets both minimums) got a table-driven case; all 25 are red for their reasons in the final run.

**The builder's calls.** The modules split as the brief allowed: `excerpts.py` (id, key, cutter, build step, provenance block, merge, candidate-rungs report, CLI) and `excerpt_proposer.py` (windows, signals, gates, candidates, the view's projection). Not the left hand alone: the proposer offers `both` and `right`; a left-hand cut is one staff in the bass clef, which the detectors read as treble (the clef assumption), so it would measure demands the passage does not have; the cutter and the definitions take `left`, and the proposer offers it once the detectors read the clef. The margin shown and played is two bars either side. A run keeps at most forty candidates, those meeting every signal first. `docs/04` has no microscope section, so the excerpt view is described where the item view is, in `docs/06` (a deviation from the file list, with this reason).

**Every reader of `item.type`, reviewed for its meaning** (the brief's table). `tsc -b` reported nothing when the union grew: the readers compare `type` with `===` and `!==`, which compile for any member, so the compiler was no census here; the readers were found by searching `app/src` for `.type` against the four values. Each reader whose treatment of an excerpt differs from its default has a case in `excerptItems.test.ts`.

| Reader | Song | Exercise / drill | Excerpt, and why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectors.ts` 206 (an option of the lesson, `excludeSongs`) | left out when songs are excluded | kept | left out with songs (`isPieceMaterial`): a passage of a piece is music, not technique |
| `selectors.ts` 231 (the tiers that search the whole catalogue) | offered unless excluded | offered | **never**: unplaced, teaching use undecided; it reaches a learner through a rung once F lists it |
| `session.ts` 674–675 (`usable`, the `songs` filter) | `none` refuses, `only` wants it | `none` keeps | `none` refuses it; `only` wants the piece, so refuses it too: the repertoire lifecycle keeps to songs (adversary 10) |
| `session.ts` 766 (the requirement pool) | never | the pool | never (`isExerciseKind`): a skill requirement is met by an exercise |
| `session.ts` 771 (the pool with songs left out) | removed | kept | removed with songs |

**The signals and weights** (`excerpt_proposer.WEIGHTS`; a signal is met at 0.6; a window's score is the weighted sum the view shows part by part; nothing reads a level, and the lowest-difficulty mutant is red):

| Signal | Weight | Reason | Readings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| opportunity | 3.0 | the reason the passage exists: the target at the window rule's density | met at the window rule (rising to 1.0 at twice the minimum); an every-bar detector 1.0 only when every bar holds |
| occurrences | 2.0 | practice needs the target to come back, in at least half the bars | the share of bars holding the target |
| phraseStart | 2.0 | a passage that begins mid-phrase is a fragment (adversary 3) | bar 1, a double bar, a repeat sign, a rehearsal mark 1.0; a new key or time, a fermata before, a rest before 0.9; a long note before, the melody resting into an upbeat 0.8; a slur starting on the first note 0.7; a mid-bar upbeat 0.5; a long note or rest opening an edition-marked phrase 0.4; a bass change alone 0.3; nothing 0 |
| ending | 2.0 | a passage that stops before its cadence is a fragment (adversary 4) | the piece's end, a double bar, a repeat, a fermata 1.0; a long note or rest over a cadence to the tonic 1.0, over the tonic 0.9, over the dominant 0.7 marked "leads onward", with no cadence read 0.7; a tie out or mid-motion 0 |
| pickup | 1.0 | an upbeat severed from its phrase is the commonest cut fault (adversary 5) | no upbeat before, or the piece's pickup included, 1.0; an upbeat in the bar before 0 (start there) |
| texture | 1.0 | the hands as the parent has them | the share of bars both hands sound; 0 for a window that begins on one hand's rest and ends on the other's, or a one-hand window silent at an edge |
| length | 1.0 | a phrase or two | 4 and 8 bars 1.0, 6 0.8, 5 and 7 0.7, others 0.6 |
| gates | — | refused whatever the score | untaught (the rung's ancestry, as `claims.py` reads it); forbidden (a generated parent's family contract); physical (D0's `physical_faults` over the window at the catalogue's tempo: an octave's span, a leap of up to two octaves with a fifth of a second, twelve notes a second; the edition's fingering is its editor's and not gated) |

The window minimums (`minInWindow`, each a hypothesis with its reason in the file): clef.bass 4, pitch.ledger 2, interval.step 4, interval.skip 3, interval.leap 3, rhythm.eighths 4, rhythm.shorter-than-quarter 4, rhythm.sixteenths 4, rhythm.dotted-quarter 2, rhythm.ties 2, rhythm.syncopation 3, rhythm.triplets 3, metre.compound 8, key.signature 4, pitch.chromatic 3, range.beyond-position 2, texture.hands-together 4, texture.left-hand-pattern 1 and texture.walking-bass 1 (the every-bar rule). Every window a rule or gate refuses is in the run's `refused` list with what refused it, which the view shows.

### Entry 104 — D3c: the rung page's automatic picks — *Start*, *Climb the ladder*, *Quick check* and the duet and blind tools' piece, named or the first song — each take the rung's next option that passes the one exported teaching-use admission, through one local helper, or are gone truthfully; Start's line calls its pick "the first thing on this rung" only when it is; the option rows keep every authored option; no second reading of the promise fact or the teaching bit (2026-09-28)

**Judgement.** The rung page no longer opens an unheard groove because a rung lists it first. I looked at `holiday.5` and `latin.3` on the phone at 342 × 740, before and after, from the DOM and from pictures, tapping each control. I checked every rung (109) through the real screen in a unit probe, and traced every place the page picks an item. Nothing was heard, and no teaching-use decision was made.

- **`holiday.5` before.** *Start*: "Opens “Ostinato over a pedal bass in A minor — broken minor triad”, the first thing on this rung", and it opened the ostinato. *Quick check* opened the ostinato too. There is no ladder, duet or blind tool on this rung.
- **`holiday.5` after.** *Start*: "Opens “E major arpeggio — 2 oct, both”." It opens the arpeggio, the rung's second listed exercise. *Quick check* opens the arpeggio. The ostinato is still the first row under *Exercise options*, with its ▶ (`pictures/after/rung-holiday.5.png`).
- **`latin.3` before.** *Start*: "Opens “Clave — son 2-3”, the first thing on this rung", and it opened the clave. *Quick check* opened the same clave. *Ways to play this* held *Play it as a duet*, which opened the son 3-2 clave over a quarter-note pulse, a groove.
- **`latin.3` after.** *Start*: "Opens “Cielito Lindo”." It opens the song, the rung's song ask. *Quick check* opens nothing and says "This lesson has no drill to check against yet." The duet button is gone, and with it the whole *Ways to play this* block. The duet names a groove, and a named item with no admission draws no button (no song is substituted). All five claves and the tresillo are still listed and tappable (`pictures/after/rung-latin.3.png`).
- **Across the curriculum.** On the committed code, **24 controls on 13 rungs** opened a music-promising generated item with no affirmative decision. That is *Start* and *Quick check* on the eleven rungs Entry 103 named (`latin.3`, `jazz.4`, `holiday.5`, `jam.5`, `jazz.6`, `blues.6`, `rock.6`, `jam.6`, `latin.6`, `blues.7`, `blues.8`), plus the duet on `latin` and on `latin.3`. After: **0**. Twenty of the 24 now open the rung's next admitted option. Four open nothing: the duets of `latin` and `latin.3`, and *Quick check* on `latin.3` and `latin.6`, whose every exercise is a groove. No *Start* is gone. Every one of the 1,021 option rows is still drawn (`runs/compare-probe.md`).
- **As music: unverified.** What a teacher would notice among the replacements:
  - A carol rung (`holiday.5`) now starts on a two-octave arpeggio, a level and a half above the ostinato.
  - `latin.6`'s *Start* opens a song titled *Tango La Cumparsita - Piano Solo (Tutorial Parte B)*.
  - `jam.5`'s *Quick check*, "a 2–3 minute measured test", now opens *Play the form with the chart*, a backing-track drill where nothing is judged (Follow-up 3).
  - Each is the rung's own authored option in the rung's own order.

Five things the reviewer should hear first:

- **One helper, four picks, one predicate.** `firstOffered(ids, valid)` in `LessonScreen.ts` walks the rung's options in order and returns the first that passes the control's own condition and `admittedForTeaching`. It is the only admission call on the page. Every pick goes through it: `startItem`, the ladder, *Quick check*, `scorePiece`'s named `tool.item` and `scorePiece`'s song fallback. `valid` is the control's existing question, asked of `openItem`'s helpers (`isPlayable`, `targetFor`) or read off the item (`drill || file`, `type === 'song'`). `openItem.ts` is untouched and holds no admission. A test holds both files to that.
- **Premise corrected: *Climb the ladder* changes nowhere.** Entry 103's Follow-up 1 said the ladder "does the same there and at `jazz.9` and `blues.9`". The ladder tool is on seven rungs only (`4.1`–`4.4`, `technique.4`, `.6`, `.7`; `ladderTool.test.ts`). None of them lists a refused exercise ahead of an admitted one, so no ladder control changes on the build. *Quick check*, which Entry 103 did not count, changes on the same eleven rungs as *Start*. The brief's "the eleven rungs' Start among them" for the controls that vanish is also corrected: every one of the eleven has an admitted next option, so none vanishes.
- **Start's line had to change with the pick.** "Opens “E major arpeggio”, the first thing on this rung" sits right above a list whose first row is the ostinato. That line is false. The line now keeps *the first thing on this rung* only when the pick is the rung's first listed option. Otherwise it reads *Opens “X”.* No new string and no "waiting for review" (the D3b ruling). On the build this changes exactly the eleven rungs' lines and no other (`runs/compare-probe.md`: the Start line changes only where Start moved).
- **The option rows are the learner's choice and are untouched.** Every refused groove is still listed with its ▶, and the tests say so literally: the refused row is drawn and tapping its ▶ opens it, while no automatic control resolves to it (the reviewer's constraint on the brief).
- **Written for E1a to broaden without reopening this.** No test or helper here says which kinds the predicate refuses.
  - The constructed refused item is a generated groove. Each case first asks the predicate what it says of it, and never infers it.
  - The sweep asks the predicate of whatever each control resolves to.
  - The "picked exactly as before" case uses a plain notated song (type `song`), not an excerpt.
  - The named list of gone controls is today's catalogue. No rung lists an excerpt, so E1a's extension changes nothing on the rung page today.

## The mechanism, and the test that told it apart

**Cause.** D3a put the teaching-use check in `eligibleFor`, and D3b put the same predicate into `session.usable` for the card's rows. The rung page asks neither. Its four controls pick from the rung's lists by position and by the item's shape (playable, opens as a score, has a drill or a file, is a song). An authored placement is not a teaching-use decision, so a groove the rung lists first is what Start and Quick check opened. The same goes for a groove a duet names.

**Alternative.** Some other path on the page opens the grooves, such as the option rows or the Simon tool. Or the grooves reach a control indirectly, for example Start through an import overlay.

**Test.** The rung-page probe, through the real screen on the built catalogue, lists all 24 offending controls: Start 11, Quick check 11, the named duet 2. Each changed pick's before-item is one the predicate refuses. None is explained any other way (the sweep's third case, and `compare_probe.py`'s check). The Simon tool opens only runtime drills with no promise fact (`runs/simon-check.txt`: three drills, none carrying one). The option rows are the learner's choice by the reviewer's ruling. With the admission in `firstOffered`, the count is 0. Each per-path mutant brings back its own path's red.

### Entry 105 — E1a: the one teaching-use admission covers excerpts — `unapprovedMusic`, the private reading behind the exported `admittedForTeaching` and `eligibleFor`, returns an excerpt's stored bit as it returns a music-promising generated item's, so an excerpt reaches no automatic offer (the gate's four wants, the card's rows, the swap sheet's tiers and last resort) until `provenance.review.teaching === true` on its cut's current identity; a `yes` on an earlier cut of the same definition admits nothing, because the build fills the bit only from a decision on the cut file's current sha256; the Library and exploration stay open; E1's rule that an unplaced excerpt is in no whole-catalogue tier stays and stops being the only guard (2026-09-28)

**Judgement.** Nothing a learner sees changes today, and nothing was heard or decided. The five excerpts are on no rung, and before this change none reached an automatic offer: on the committed code, with the sweeps' oracle extended to excerpts, no tier of any rung's swap sheet offered one to a learner who copes with everything, and no card row offered one to a fresh learner at any rung, every track on, at 15, 30, 60 and 120 minutes. Both sweeps were green before and after (`red/red-app-committed-code.txt`, `runs/vitest-three-final.txt`). What changes is what the contract guarantees for an excerpt a rung lists:

- **Before, on the committed code, a rung listing an excerpt offered it at once.** I placed each built excerpt as the one song of the first rung that teaches what it was cut for. A fresh learner on the core path and that rung's track got the cut as the card's new row on four of the five placements (`runs/probe-placed-committed-code.txt`):
  - Wabash Blues 1–4 at 3.1: "This lesson asks for it — not counted yet".
  - Anh. 113 25–32 at 3.1: "This lesson asks for it — not counted yet".
  - I Got Rhythm 15–18 at `blues.5`: "Blues & boogie asks for it — not counted yet".
  - Hark! 25–28 at `latin.3`: "Latin asks for it — not counted yet".
  - Ode to Joy 9–12 at 3.6 asks for exercises only, so no row took it.
  - The swap sheet's lesson tier offered the cut for the rung's other options.
  - Nobody had approved any of them for teaching use: the reviewer's finding, reproduced.
- **After, the same placements.** No card row and no swap-sheet tier offers any of the five while undecided (`runs/probe-placed-after.txt` and the built-catalogue case). The rung's songs ask stays unmet, and the card fills the row from what the slot's rules already admit. At 3.1 that is a second exercise under the rung's exercises ask, "This lesson asks for it — not counted yet". That claim is true, because the exercises ask is unmet too. ## The predicate: what each kind of item needs to be admitted to an automatic offer

`admittedForTeaching(item)`, and the teaching-use check in `eligibleFor` for the `skill`, `requirement`, `demand` and `equivalent` wants. Admission is necessary, never sufficient: the gate's two questions (can the learner cope, is the opportunity established) and each consumer's own rules still apply. `exploration` is exempt, and the Library never asks.

| Kind of item | Needs, to be admitted | Identity the bit is filled against | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A drill (a generated family whose promise for the recipe is `drill`, or an authored or runtime drill) | nothing: its promise is its contract; admitted whatever its bit | — | D3a (unchanged) |
| A music-promising generated item (promise `music`: the studies, grooves, the 12/8 blues) | `provenance.review.teaching === true`; `null` (undecided) or `false` (a `no` or `fix`) refused as `teaching-use-not-approved` with the bit kept | the generator triple, recipe and tempo | D3a (gate), D3b (card) |
| A notated song (PDMX, kern, MuseTrainer, authored) | nothing: its notes are its truth; admitted whatever its bit | — | D3a (unchanged) |
| A runtime reading row (a drill made when it opens, no file, no promise fact) | nothing | — | D3a (unchanged) |
| An excerpt (`type: 'excerpt'`) | `provenance.review.teaching === true`; `null`, `false` or no provenance refused as `teaching-use-not-approved` with the bit kept | the cut file's sha256; a decision on an earlier cut is stale | **E1a** |

Placement is a separate question: an unplaced excerpt is in no tier that searches the whole catalogue at any bit (E1, `selectors.ts`, kept), and on no card row, since the card's candidates are what reached rungs list.

## The mechanism, and the test that told it apart

**Cause.** `admittedForTeaching` and `eligibleFor` read one private function, and it asked only whether `facts.promise.value === 'music'`. A cut carries no promise fact (the build writes one only for generated items), so every excerpt was admitted whatever its bit. The only thing keeping the five off the glass was that no rung lists one, together with E1's whole-catalogue skip for unplaced excerpts.

**Alternative.** Some consumer admits excerpts by a path that does not read the predicate, so fixing the predicate would leave a door open.

**Test.** The reds on the committed code split by path: the gate's verdicts, the card (`session.usable`), the swap sheet's lesson tier and last resort (the gate), and the built placement. One change in the predicate turns every one green and touches no consumer. The direct-consumer mutant, which bypasses the predicate at `usable()` for excerpts, turns only the card's two cases red.
