The only candidates in the build are the twelve transfer roles and the five excerpts: shifting position has six scales (pentatonic and blues, in A, D and E; drills, admitted) and one study; reading by interval, subdivision, syncopation, six-eight and playing hands together have one study each; every study promises music with no teaching-use `yes`, so the one gate refuses it; the five excerpts are undecided and on no rung. So **only shifting position can be offered today**, and only the scales. Sight-reading, reading ahead, the bass clef, ledger lines, dotted quarters, ties, triplets, key signatures, accidentals and hand independence have no candidate of either form.

## The identity table: what each source's `material` is, and how equality is decided

| Source of the run | `material` | Written by | Equal when (`material.sameMaterial`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A generated catalogue item (scales, studies, grooves, the pentatonic items) | `{kind: 'generator', family, version, seed, recipe, tempoBpm}` — the build's `provenance.identity` (`review.current_identity`: `drill.generator`, `drill.params` with the hands, `tempoBpm`) | `build.attach_provenance`; the run copies it (`material.runFacts`) | family, version, seed, recipe (deep, key order free) and tempo all equal — D2's `sameIdentity` |
| A notated item (PDMX, kern, MuseTrainer, authored) | `{kind: 'file', sha256}` of the built file | the build | the sha256 |
| An excerpt | `{kind: 'file', sha256}` of the **cut**, never the parent — E1's field, generalised, not renamed | the build (E1's Score screen hashed the loaded bytes; the build hashes the same file, and the app no longer recomputes it) | the sha256 |
| A sight-reading phrase (runtime) | `{kind: 'generator', family: 'sight-reading', version, seed, recipe, tempoBpm}`: the phrase's `generator` (D1a), **the generator options it was written from** — the row's params with the reader's moves and the rung's hold (`readingOptions`) — seed and version apart, and the tempo written into it | the Score screen (`material.phraseMaterial`) | as a generator: reopening the same version, seed and recipe is equal; another seed, version, move or hold is not (`materialIdentity.test.ts`) |
| A drill made when it opens (the drill screen's runs) | `{kind: 'none', why: 'made when it opens: no file the build keys'}` | the drill screen (`runFacts`) | never — contact by id alone |
| An import | `{kind: 'none', why: 'an imported score: no build identity'}` | the Score screen | never — by id alone |
| A placeholder | `none` (`no notation is bundled`) on the row; never played | — | never |
| A legacy run (before D4), a paper run | absent | — | by id alone: `met-by-id` |

**The deviation, and why.** The brief and the reviewer name "the exact `ReadingRecipe`" as the phrase's recipe. The `ReadingRecipe` (`{row, moved, easy}`) does not determine the phrase: the row's params and the judging rung's hold also do — which is why `evidenceJob.candidatePhrases` has to try three option sets to write a stored run's phrase again. So the recipe is the options the phrase was written from, which is exactly what D2's identity holds for a generated catalogue item (`drill.params`: the generator's input). The row id and `easy` are left out on purpose: two rows whose options are equal write the same phrase from the same seed, and calling those two materials would be a false first contact. **Tempo stays in D2's type**: it is the options' `bpm` or the version's default, so it is determined by the recipe and adds no discrimination; no second identity structure exists (`Identity` is `review/record.ts`'s, reused by `types.ts` through `import type`).

## The contact cases (`progressStore.contactIn`, over every stored row; `contactNovelty.test.ts`)

| Rows on record | Candidate | Contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a run with the same file identity, same id | that file | `met`, `metById: true`, `metAs: [id]` |
| the same identity under a renamed or duplicate id | the new id | `met`, `metById: false`, `metAs: [old ids]` (the lookup crosses ids; `sessionsForItem` could not) |
| only a legacy run of the id (no material) | any material | `met-by-id` — never `unmet`, never offered |
| a run of the id whose material is `none` | any material | `met-by-id` |
| a legacy run and a run of other known material, same id | new material | `met-by-id` (the legacy run may have been this one) |
| a run of the id under version 1 (or seed 1) | version 2 (or seed 2) | `unmet`, `metById: true` |
| nothing of either kind | anything | `unmet`, `metById: false` |
| a phrase of version 2, seed 7, recipe R | the same | `met`; version 1 seed 7 → `unmet` with `metById`; the recipe moved → `unmet` |
| the whole piece's file | its excerpt's cut | `unmet` as material (the relationship records the composition) — `met` only once the cut itself was played |
| a candidate with no material (`none`, or absent) | — | by id alone, `materialUnknown: true`; `none` never meets `none` |

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**The identity (item 1).** *Hypothesis:* the build already computes the identity every review decision binds to, so writing it on the row is one call. *Alternative:* the sha256 costs the attach step more than it can bear (the brief's deviation clause). *Test:* the identity from `review.identities` after `review.fill_reviewed`, held by `TestTheMaterialIdentity` against an oracle independent of `review.py` (the triple off `drill.generator`, the recipe off `drill.params`, `hashlib` over the built file) and against D2's record's own current identity. Red on the committed build (`KeyError: 'identity'`, 2,090 rows), green on build 1; the build line reads as before, and the catalogue differs from the committed build's in `provenance.identity`, `provenance.transferOf` and its fact alone (`runs/compare-catalogues.txt`: 0 items differ otherwise; `curriculum.json` byte-identical); the catalogue text is about 7 % larger (every generated item's recipe copied into its identity). Kinds: 1,200 generator, 811 file, 79 none (71 made when they open, 8 placeholders).

**Contact from identities (item 3).** *Hypothesis:* the rows the rung state already holds in memory (`rungRows`, every run without its per-step detail) are enough to scan by identity. *Alternative:* a `byMaterial` index. A scan was chosen: the value is nested and discriminated, so an index needs a computed key and a schema version, and every derivation already reads these rows. `sessionsForItem` alone cannot see a renamed id — the `lookup-by-id-only` mutant (identity compared only among the id's rows) turns the renamed-id cases red.

**What established the skill, asked of the ladder (item 5).** `ladder.ts` is untouched and its `shownOn` is private, so re-deriving it would be a second reading of its rules. Instead `transfer.establishedOn` asks the ladder: a probe — a supporting full-standard first contact on an item, dated after the history — turns `transfer` on exactly when the item is not in `shownOn`; the records are those on the ladder's items up to the reading that last reached proficiency (the ladder over each prefix). A reset below proficiency is invisible to both questions, so a record before one can be included: more material, never less, which makes a candidate less likely to differ. The `shown-on-not-the-ladders` mutant (every supporting record) survived the first cases — a later read on *another* item was excluded by the item filter anyway — and was caught once a later read of the *same* row was added (`runs/mutants.txt`, then `runs/mutants-final.txt`).

**The offer's place (item 4).** *Hypothesis:* "after the rung's own new material" means after a strand rung's own asks, before the next lesson's preview. *Alternative:* after every asked claim, the next lesson's included. *Test:* the alternative measured on the three learners' diaries (`scripts/probe_offer_after_next.py`, `runs/probe-offer-after-next.txt`, `session.ts` restored by sha256): **0 offers in 90 mornings**, against 5 with the chosen place. The guard is "no strand's rung asks anything this slot serves, offered or not": an ask whose only candidate is refused (D3b's pool-not-offer case) still keeps the offer out — the `displaces-the-rungs-ask` mutant survived until that case was added, and `offer-before-the-rungs-ask` is caught by the first.

## What the facts say (the brief's first hypothesis): the pentatonic for shifting position, and an excerpt

- **The seeded learner's offer** (`pictures/after-run-row.json`): shown on two phrases of 2.5's right-hand row (materials known). Declared: family and rhythm differ from `position_shift`, the thumb passing under unmeasured. Measured against the phrases: **family differs** (pentatonic, sight-reading); generated both; key signature the same (0: A minor has none, the phrases were in C); hands the same (right); texture the same (none); **rhythm the same** (eighths on both). `differsOn`: family, rhythm — rhythm by the declaration only.
- **The intermediate's day 5** (`diaries-after/relationship-facts.txt`): its establishing reads are **legacy** (the diaries' harness records runs without the Score screen, so without material) — two unknown historical references carrying the row's id; family read from the item by id (sight-reading), key unknown, hands both (the harness's header), rhythm the same. `differsOn`: family, hands, rhythm (declared).
- **An excerpt** (Anh. 113, bars 25–32, for reading by interval; `transferRelationship.test.ts`): family (its composition), generated → notated, key (−1 against 0), hands (both against right), texture (hands together against none) and rhythm all differ; nothing declared; the composition recorded with the items of it the learner has runs of.
- **So:** the declaration is written against the contract's `from` family (`position_shift`), which is not what establishes a skill in the app — the reading rows do — and against those the declared rhythm difference does not hold. The dimension a teacher would name for this pair, **how the hand moves** (a thumb passing under against a hand lifting to a new position), is in neither: the contract says so in `notMeasured`, which the relationship carries as such. Register, fingering and the size of the shift are not dimensions either. The facts can say "another family, another key, generated → authentic"; they cannot say whether the difference matters for the skill — that stays the post-E policy's, with a musician's reading where it needs one.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **The slot and frequency**: the `new` slot, before the next lesson's preview (above); one a card, and none on a day a stored run already came from an offer. The reviewer's answer rules out `review` (retention's meaning).
- **The copy**: `SLOT_TEXT.somethingNew`, `feelDifferent` — "Shifting position: something new, for a skill you have shown — it should feel different": the skill first, where the line is cut, like skill retention's lines.
- **Which measured dimensions count**: family, generated or notated, key signature, hands, texture demands, rhythm and metre demands — presence on both sides (the candidate's measured `demands`; a reference's located in the notation its run played, from its stored evidence's per-demand entries), so a difference means one side has none of what the other has. The family is a generator's family or a notated item's composition, so a cut of a piece that established a skill is "the same family".
- **The candidate pool**: a transfer role anywhere in the catalogue (the contract's selection intent; the gate judges coping with the learner's rung, as the swap sheet's tiers do); an excerpt only where a reached rung lists it — E1's placement rule, which the reviewer kept after E1a.
- **Order among candidates**: the vocabulary's skills, then the nearest level to the learner's rung band, Shuffle taking the next — an order, never a filter; the ranking is E2's.
- **No rung judges the offer's run**: it is no rung's ask, so Today opens it with `?intent=transfer&skill=` and no `?rung=` (which would otherwise have credited 2.5 or 3.1 by listing).
- **The run's relationship** is computed when the Score screen opens (the stored runs and the catalogue, the same pure function), so it records what the offer was made on.
- **The identity type** is reused from `review/record.ts` (`import type`), not moved: one type, one import.

## Unverified, beside what passes

1. **Unverified as music**: the blues and pentatonic scales offered, every study that could be, and every excerpt; whether "it should feel different" is apt; whether a thumb-under scale exercises what reading a position shift at sight does. Nothing heard.
2. **Nothing is claimed about transfer**: the offer's run produces no evidence the ladder reads (the scales' skills are not in force), and v0's rule still reads a first read of another reading row. The relationship facts are for the post-E policy; nothing here tests them against learning.
3. **The seeded learner's two reads are constructed rows**, not played phrases; the three diaries' learners record runs through the test harness, without the Score screen, so their establishing reads are legacy references (no material). A real learner's reads after D4 carry their phrase's material; that path is proven by the unit cases and the browser run's read-back, not by a month of real use.
4. **The phone look is one learner at one rung**, read from the DOM and the pictures, not by a person on a phone. At 342 px the offer's reason line shows "Shifting position: something n…".
5. **The relationship on the run is loaded when the Score screen opens**, asynchronously; a run finished before it resolves (it reads rows already in memory and the cached catalogue) would carry the intent without the relationship. Not observed; not tested.
6. **CI has not run this tree.**

## Not done

1. **Paper runs carry no `material`**: a shelf piece is the learner's own book, with no file and no build identity; `PaperScreen.ts` is untouched, and its runs read as legacy (by id).
2. **Imports get `none`**, not a hash of the stored score: the build keys no identity for them and the brief's identity is the build's; an import is never a transfer candidate.
3. **No store index**: contact reads the in-memory rows (above), by choice.
4. **The swap sheet's tiers are unchanged**, as decided; the offer's row swaps like any row, and a swap drops the claim and the intent.
5. **No excerpt is placed or approved, and no study decided**: the positive excerpt and study cases use constructed rows from built items with `teaching: true`, as the reviewer allowed.

## Follow-ups (recorded, not fixed)

1. **P2 — contact facts can be pruned.** `holdsEvidence` keeps rows with evidence or a `lessonId`; a transfer-intended run has neither (its skills are not in force, no rung judges it), so past the cap (25,000 rows plus slack, beyond the 90-day window) the run that made an item `met` can be deleted and the item offered again as unmet. Whether `material` or `intent` should keep a row is a retention decision (C7's rule).
2. **P2 — the same offer comes back every morning until played** (the intermediate, four days running): one a day holds, and it reads as a standing invitation; whether an unplayed offer should step aside for a while is the chooser's (E2).
3. **P3 — the offer's line is cut at phone width** to its skill and "something n…", as every row's is; a shorter head would say more there.
4. **P3 — `excerpt.cutIdentity` is no longer called by the app** (the run reads the build's identity); kept because E1's case pins it; remove it with that case, or reuse it if imports get a file identity.
5. **P1 (the post-E task's) — the declaration is written against the contract's `from` family**, not against what establishes a skill in the app (the reading rows); on the seeded learner the declared rhythm difference does not hold measured. The policy that reads these facts should weigh declared and measured apart, and how the hand moves is measured by nothing.

## Questions

1. **The offer's place in the new slot.** It takes the slot after the strand rungs' own asks and **before the next lesson's first ask** — the preview *"Next lesson — this one waits for your reads"* — because that ask is not an unmet requirement of the learner's rung. Placed after it instead, the three learners are offered nothing in 90 mornings (measured). The reviewer's "never displace an unmet rung requirement" could be read to include the next rung's; if so, the offer becomes near-invisible until the chooser (E2) makes room for it. A product choice; I chose, and the alternative is one line.

### Entry 107 — E2: the chooser's material layer — one candidate contract over bundled, generated, runtime, excerpt, imported, PDF and external material; material requirements as data with the experience contract (`automatic` or `chosen`) the reviewer asked to be told apart; validity per source kind read before the gate's questions, an unknown forbidden demand refusing an automatic experience and leaving a chosen one open; the gate over requirements as a sibling of `eligibleFor` (the brief's deviation clause: the reviewer's rule moves one verdict, and nothing else moves); the import's store side — the converter owning its version, the command-line converter stamping its own, an import's inferred tempo marked as the build marks a bundled row's, every stored import measured once on the next launch through the store, and the assign sheet reading the measured truth; the seed list of teaching repertoire as a proposal source (2026-09-29)

**Judgement.** Nothing was heard. What I looked at: the assign sheet for one imported MIDI at 342 × 740, as the app's converter split it and after a hand correction saved through `importStore.correctImportHands` (`docs/prompts/pictures/e2/`, with the text the sheet showed and the stored rows in `assign-pictures.json`); the new browser case's sheet on the built app; the gate's verdicts as the tests print them; the code. The brief in this worktree is the committed one, which lacks the reviewer's required change; I built from the amended brief in the main checkout (`docs/prompts/tasks/E2-chooser-material-layer.md`, uncommitted there, read only) — item 3's rule and adversary 13 are its.

- **The import on the sheet, before its correction** (a one-track MIDI of one melody, E4 D4 C4 B3 | A3 B3 C4 D4 | E4 F4 G4 E4 | C4, hand-written for the picture). The converter split the one line at its dip: the right hand plays E4 D4 and rests; the left hand, on the bass staff, takes C4 B3, then A3 B3 C4 in bar 2 while the right hand rests until D4 on beat 4, and the closing C4 (`probe-one-line-split.txt`). The sheet says so in its conversion note ("The hands were split by the shape of the lines … check those bars") and, in the new line under it, **"Measured in the notes: the bass-staff notes, steps, skips and the syncopation."** Level "≈ 1.3". The syncopation is the detectors' reading of the split, not of the tune — inferred: the right hand's bar 2 opens on a rest and enters on the fourth beat, T37's clause for a bar whose melody opens on a rest (the reading E1 recorded on the Lemoine étude); nothing in the melody is syncopated.
- **After the correction** (the line in the right hand, the left hand resting). **"Measured in the notes: the ledger-line notes, steps, skips and the notes beyond the hand position."** Level "≈ 1.17". Each is true of the melody as written: B3 and A3 sit on ledger lines below the treble staff, and A3 to G4 is wider than a five-finger position. The bass staff and the syncopation are gone. The stored row's provenance says the hands are the learner's and the demands were measured on the corrected score. What a teacher would notice: the conversion note above still says the converter split the hands and to check those bars — it is the visit's note about the import moment, kept in memory (T29), and after a correction it describes a decision the learner has already undone (a follow-up for X3's import experience, which builds on this).
- **An import stored before E0**, on the next launch (the browser case, desktop Chromium on the production build): the row's measurement and provenance taken off, the page reloaded; the launch measured it in the background, and the sheet's line then named the bass-staff notes and both hands together for the two-track fixture (what the case asserts). The full line jsdom's detectors give the same file is "Measured in the notes: the bass-staff notes, steps, skips, leaps, the notes beyond the hand position and both hands together" (`probe-two-hands.json`); the browser's full line was not captured.

**What the gate now says, as observations against the rules** (the requirements object's `experience` tells the two contracts apart; the verdicts are the tests'):

- **An external recommendation** (a rag a teacher named for its syncopation, estimates at high confidence): for **discovery** (a chosen experience, no target) it is *eligible for exploration*, with the missing fact said as "an external recommendation's demands are estimates, never measured (…)"; for a **project claim** of syncopation reading it is *exploration only*; for an **automatic** offer to a learner prepared only for steps and skips it is *ineligible, `unknown-forbidden`*, naming the seventeen demands that learner is not prepared for, because an estimate rules none of them out; for an automatic offer to a learner prepared for everything it is *exploration only* — never eligible by estimate. The seed list's works read the same way.
- **A PDF** under an automatic constrained requirement: *ineligible, `unknown-forbidden`*, the unprepared demands named and "a PDF: the app reads no notes from it"; under an explicitly chosen project: *exploration only*, the same missing fact; under plain exploration: *eligible for exploration*, the missing fact kept. No verdict it receives carries a `practises`: never a competence claim (L24's grammar decides evidence).
- **An unmeasured bundled row or a score imported before E0** is the one existing case whose verdict moves (below, Questions 1).
- **A known forbidden demand** is refused under either contract (`untaught`): the asymmetry the reviewer asked for — an unknown is not an observed absence; an observed unpreparedness is.

Four things the reviewer should hear first:

- **The overload is a sibling, by the brief's own deviation clause.** The reviewer's rule cannot keep every existing `Want` verdict byte-identical: an unmeasured candidate asked for a skill, a requirement, a demand or an equivalent, by a learner who is not prepared for every demand, was `{verdict: 'exploration-only', missing}` and is `{verdict: 'ineligible', why: 'unknown-forbidden', demands, missing}` under the material gate. So `eligibleFor` is untouched (not one line of `eligibility.ts` changed), no caller changes, and `eligibleForMaterial` stands beside it. Every other verdict is `eligibleFor`'s own: the material gate asks it the two questions and adds only what a requirement adds. Proved two ways: over the built catalogue and a constructed set, five learners and every want kind (`materialLayer.test.ts`, the moved set exactly the rule's case); and over **every** `eligibleFor` call the gate's own test files make (a one-off instrumented run, `probe-every-gate-call.jsonl`): 1,021,608 calls across `eligibility`, `gateAtTheConsumers`, `excerptItems`, `lessonPagePicksPassTheAdmission` and `importOverlay`; 1,021,587 byte-identical, 21 moved, every one the rule's case (seven in `eligibility.test.ts`'s adversary 8, fourteen in `gateAtTheConsumers.test.ts`: its unmeasured option and the eight import-only bundled rows), none unexpected. Consumers read only `eligible()`, and both verdicts refuse, so adopting the sibling would change no offer — only the reason a future line could say.
- **Item 4(d)'s premise is wrong at the lines, and the import path had a gap `docs/03` §4a said it did not.** The brief says an import is "`exploration-only` while a tempo-sensitive demand rests on an inferred tempo (E0's `untrusted`)". E0's `untrusted` is *eligible, with the list carried* (`eligibility.ts`, `withTrust`; `eligibility.test.ts` › *marks tempo-sensitive demands untrusted*), and the import path never wrote the list at all, so an import whose file states no tempo was the one notated candidate whose inferred tempo the gate could not see. I fixed the mechanism — the import path writes the build's rule (`importProvenance`, `correctImportHands`, the migration) — and kept E0's verdict for every source. Making an untrusted tempo-sensitive target `exploration-only` for imports alone would make an import unlike other candidates (4(d)'s first clause); for every source it would move bundled verdicts. Questions 2.
- **The migration is idempotent by a stamp, not by the converter version.** A converter bump cannot re-convert a stored score — the MIDI bytes are not kept — so the row must go on naming the converter that wrote its notes, and a rule "converter older than current" alone would re-measure it on every launch. Each measurement now writes `facts.measuredUnder` (the converter version in force when the notes were measured, an unmeasurable verdict included; absent reads as 1). A PDF is never handed to the detectors, and its verdict is written with the version, so it is not retried until the version moves (the reviewer's constraint). Each row is written in one transaction onto the row as it is then, and only if its score is still the one measured: a correction or an assignment saved while the measurement runs is never overwritten (both held by cases, both mutants red).
- **The seed list reaches the proposer, and reaches the finder's prompts only when the build passes a concept.** `finder.generate` takes `concepts`; `build.py`'s two call sites do not pass them, and `build.py` is D4's this wave. The built curriculum's prompts are therefore unchanged today (a case holds `generate` without a concept byte-identical). Not done, with the two-line change named.

## The mechanisms, and the tests that told them apart

**The material gate over the one gate (items 2, 3).** *Hypothesis:* the requirements object can be the `Want` plus fields, the gate `eligibleFor`'s two questions plus a validity pre-check and the fields' checks, so every existing verdict survives by construction. *Alternative:* the translation drifts — a field read differently, an order changed — and verdicts move silently. *Test:* the sweep and the probe above; the naive version of the gate (every requirement asked as its `Want` and nothing else, `scripts/naive_gate.py`) as the red: 24 of 36 cases red — the reviewer's rule, the validity table, the requirements beyond a want, adversaries 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13 and the seed reader's automatic refusal. *Result:* the hypothesis holds everywhere but one case, which the reviewer's rule moves on purpose.

**Validity per source kind (item 3).** One function over a candidate's facts, never over its origin's name: a notated song, an excerpt and an import measured by the same detectors all answer demands `{answers: true, by: 'measured'}` (adversary 3 holds a corrected import's entries equal to a bundled score's); a generated family with a stated density answers its opportunity by `contract`; a runtime reading row by `runtime`; a PDF and a placeholder with no notation answer nothing about notes; an external recommendation answers nothing but its described wholeness and its estimated level. The gate reads it once, before the questions.

**The import that could not be measured (E25).** *Cause:* rows imported before E0 carry no measurement, and nothing measures them later (Entry 92's Not done). *Mechanism of the fix:* a job like the evidence job, started once per open after the first screen, one row per idle slice, through the store. *The race the job could introduce*, found by writing its case before trusting it: a learner saving the assign sheet (a rung) or a correction while a row is being measured — the job's first draft wrote the row it had read, which would have erased the assignment. The job now writes onto the row as it is when it writes, only if the stored score is unchanged; `sameData` compares a PDF's bytes by content, because a PDF comes back from the store as a new `ArrayBuffer` each read — the first run of the fixture store failed on exactly that (`import-truth-first-green-attempt.txt`: the PDFs never written), my fault, fixed before the green.

**The command-line converter's version (E26).** MusicXML has a place for it: `<software>` in `<encoding>` may repeat, so the converter adds `tools/midi-cleanup/midi_to_musicxml.py v.1` beside music21's own through `Metadata.add('software', …)` — no comment needed. The app reads it back (`converterStampOf`) and names the converter in `provenance.converter` (the block's shape unchanged). Read off a file the converter wrote (`fixtures/imports/stamped-by-the-converter.musicxml`, from `two-hands.mid` at v.1), so the two sides of the format are held by one artefact.

## The builder's calls, each with its reason

- **Source kinds** are seven, not the brief's five words: `runtime` (a drill the app writes when it opens) and `pdf` are kinds of their own because their validity differs from `generated` and `import` in every fact that matters. A bundled placeholder with no notation is `notated` with nothing measured: its validity says so.
- **The requirements' fields and how the gate reads each.** `forbidden`, `allowed`, `range: 'within-position'` and `hands: 'one'` forbid demands, so an unknown under an automatic experience refuses (they join the learner's unprepared set in `unknown-forbidden`); `supporting`, `hands: 'both'`, `completeness`, `duration` and `novelty` ask for something present, so an unknown leaves the claim `exploration-only` with the missing fact named. `range` is read from the measured `range.beyond-position` (no catalogue row carries a pitch range). `physical: 'd0-limits'` asks D0's limits of a source that checked them — generated items (D0's physical gate on every item the build writes); every notated source is honestly unknown, so under an automatic experience it refuses (`unknown-physical`). **No built row carries a duration** (0 of 2,090; the render step never ran on them), so a duration requirement leaves every catalogue candidate for exploration only; the case says so.
- **Completeness** is a fact, not a verdict: an excerpt is a `phrase` (its boundary by the rules), a notated song `whole`, a generated drill `isolation`, a music-promising generated item `phrase` (D3's grammar; unheard), a reading row `phrase`, an import `whole`, a PDF unknown, an external recommendation `whole` (a named work). Only a completeness requirement reads it; ranking will (layer 7).
- **Novelty** reads `MaterialLearner.contact(identity)`, a fixture until D4's reading lands; the identity is the item id. A reading row is first contact by construction (C4's unseen seeds). Entry 106 is in the main checkout and not in this tree; by the dispatch instruction the adapt clause does not apply (Follow-ups: the names to wire at the merge).
- **An automatic experience with no target** asks the gate's first question only — the `equivalent` want's question set — so a first-contact read (adversary 11) names no source and no opportunity.
- **A score imported before E0** gets, from the migration, the provenance its stored file shows, with no `hands` or `key` fact unless a converter's stamp says whose they are: a converted MIDI file is stored as MusicXML too, and the door it came through is not on the row, so "the file's staves, authored" would be a guess stated as a fact.
- **A MusicXML file the command-line converter wrote** gets `hands` and `key` `inferred` (the MusicXML door otherwise says `authored`): the staves and the key are that converter's decisions, and the file does not say whether it kept the tracks or split one line.
- **The assign sheet's line** uses the swap sheet's demand words (`help.DEMAND_WORDS`), names "notes shorter than a quarter" only where neither eighths nor sixteenths are named (the words table calls it "the eighth notes", which would be false of a piece in sixteenths), and leaves out a reading the build marks misread on the file, saying so — a line that said "the ledger-line notes" of a one-staff bass-clef part would teach wrong (red first: `red-sheet-misread-said-as-measured.txt`).
- **The seed list** names sixteen works whose teaching reputation I am confident of, each with the curriculum concepts it is known for; Kabalevsky, named in E28's row, is left out: his works are in copyright (he died in 1987). The public-domain check is the composer's death year against life plus seventy. The proposer offers the catalogue's editions of a seeded work first within each pass (the windows meeting every signal, then the rest) and adds, removes or rescores nothing; each candidate row says why (`seed`), and a run lists its seeded parents.
- **The TS seed reader** estimates a demand only from a concept that is a vocabulary skill whose opportunity is that one demand — the rule `claims.concepts_naming` reads — so *The Happy Farmer*'s "hand independence" estimates no demand (which of two it means is not in the concept). No level is estimated.

## Follow-ups

1. **P1, the merge with D4.** Back `MaterialLearner.contact` with D4's `progressStore.contactIn` and `contactIdentity` with D4's `provenance.identity` / `material` (D4's `met-by-id` reads as `met`); a generated item's identity is its generator triple there, not its id.

4. **P3, the conversion note after a correction** keeps describing the converter's split (in memory for the visit): X3's import experience should say the hands are the learner's now.

6. **P2, the detectors read a split melody as syncopated** (T37's clause on a bar opening on a rest, seen in the picture): the detectors' owner's (E22), recorded beside E1's note on the same clause.

## Questions

1. **Adopt the sibling, or keep both?** The reviewer's rule moves exactly one existing verdict: an unmeasured candidate under an automatic want, for a learner not prepared for every demand, from `exploration-only` to `unknown-forbidden` (21 of 1,021,608 calls in the gate's own tests; on the build, the eight import-only rows and any import from before E0 until the launch measures it). No offer changes either way (consumers read `eligible()`). If adopted, `eligibility.test.ts`'s adversary 8 and `gateAtTheConsumers.test.ts`'s unmeasured-option expectations are revised to the new verdict, and `eligibleFor` becomes `eligibleForMaterial(requirementsFromWant(want), candidateOf(item), learner)`.
2. **The untrusted tempo: E0's rule or the brief's?** I kept E0's (eligible, the list carried) for every source, the import path now writing the list. The brief's `exploration-only` for an import's untrusted tempo-sensitive target would make an import unlike other candidates; for every source it would move the bundled rows at a converter-supplied tempo (E0 counted 236) out of the automatic offers for those demands. Which is the rule?

## Validity, per source kind (`validityOf`)

`answers` by what, or the missing fact. The gate reads `demands` before its questions (an unknown under an automatic experience: `unknown-forbidden`), and the other facts only where a requirement asks.

### Entry 110 — D5: the microscope tells the truth it already has — the study gate's verdict on the musical line with the evaluator's contract version and whether it was carried or recomputed, "requires but the notes lack" from the rules the recipe selects, every provenance fact with its value (G55, G56, G60; 2026-09-29)

**Judgement.** I looked at the microscope the way a reviewer meets it: the three lines at one study, one groove and one drill, on the built data, drawn by the built app in headless Chromium at 342 × 740 and 1280 × 800, before (the committed screen) and after. The pictures are in `docs/prompts/pictures/d5/` and the lines' text in `before-lines.md` and `after-lines.md`. **Nothing was heard.** Every study stays **unverified as music**. The verdict now printed is a notation score of phrase shape, not a hearing, and the screen says so beside it.

On the built catalogue, the old warning named at least one requirement the recipe does not ask for on 189 generated items in nine families:

- accompaniment 15, comping 36, interval_reading 8, meter 2, rhythm 18
- scale 72, study 24, syncopation 2, walking_bass 12

Under the selected rule, no built generated item is warned. These are catalogue counts from a scratch probe over the projection, not timings.

As a reader of the words (not as a musician):
- At 342 wide the study's line runs to five lines, and it reads in one pass.
- The groove's line says "unheard" twice: once as the gate's own closing word, once in the sentence the brief asks for beside it.
- The gate's "(D3)" and "(D2)" show on this builder-only route.

**Carried or recomputed, and the cost.**
- **Recomputed, all 24 of 24 studies.** No build step persists the gate's verdict. `confirm_musical` either raises or passes. `drill.study` holds the realiser's `chosen.score` and the form, not the gate's verdict.
- **How.** The projection runs the same gate (`family_contracts.musical_gate`) on the exact built `.mxl`.
- **Agreement.** On every study, the recomputed total equals the realiser's `chosen.score` to three places (held by the projection test).
- **The carried path.** It exists (`drill.study.verdict`, with the version it was written under). Only a test fixture exercises it; nothing writes it.
- **Cost.**
  - The recomputation is well under a hundredth of the offline build's time.
  - It is smaller than the gap between this session's two offline builds of the same catalogue (the baseline and the final build). Another builder's content build ran on the same machine at the time.
  - So its cost is **within the noise**.
  - In process, the verdicts are about half of the projection step. The step itself is a small fraction of the build.
- **The "when to deviate" clause** was not taken: the pass covers only the 24 studies, and its cost is within the noise.

### Done

1. **The musical line (G55).**
   - *Mechanism:* the screen composed the line from the promise alone, as a fixed sentence written before D3. The projection carried no verdict.
   - *Change:*
     - `review.musical_verdict` puts `musical` on every generated item: the gate's own answer for a drill (`applies: false`) and for a music family without an evaluator (the contract's words).
     - For the study, the evaluator's verdict (`passes`, `total`, `floor`, `wrong`, `parts`, the gate's `why`), plus `evaluator`, `version` and `source` (`carried` | `recomputed`).
     - With neither a carried verdict nor the built notes, it gives "evaluated at build: verdict not carried".
     - `musical_evaluator.VERSION = 1` is the contract version, with the rule for bumping it (the floor stays the row's and travels beside the verdict).
     - The data has a top-level `evaluator` (name, current version). The screen says so when a carried verdict was written under another version.
     - The screen's `musicalLines` prints all of this and computes nothing.
   - *Technical:* green on the built data (below). *Pedagogical:* unverified as music.
2. **The contract warning (G56).**
   - *Mechanism:* the screen filtered `family.requires` without a rule's `when`.
   - *Change:* `review.contract_warning` puts `requires` (the rules `family_contracts.selected` picks for the recipe) and `missing` (those the measured demands lack) on every generated item. The screen prints `missing` and reads no rule.
   - Forbidden verdicts and secondary targets were already selected by the projection (`demand_verdicts`, `target_skills`). They are now guarded by a test that two mutants turn red.
   - The screen prints no overconcentration warning, so there was nothing to select there.
3. **The provenance facts (G60).**
   - *Mechanism:* the list printed kind, `via` and `why`, and dropped `value`.
   - *Change:* `provenanceLines` prints each fact's value as the record holds it: `music` or `drill`; `yes`, `no` or `fix`, never reworded into a conclusion. A reviewed fact adds its basis, date and event. A review dimension with no current decision reads "no decision". Each dimension has its own line.
   - The projection carries nothing for G60 (the screen reads the catalogue's provenance), so its tests are the unit file and the browser case.
4. **Tests:** the table below. **The product look:** before and after, above.

### Doc rows

**`docs/03-content-pipeline.md` §4b.** After the paragraph ending "… and exits 1 only for a fault in the record.":

> **What the microscope prints of the gate and the contract** (D5, 2026-09-29; G55, G56, G60). `review.microscope_data` carries, per generated item, the musical gate's answer (`musical`, from `review.musical_verdict`). A drill has `applies: false`. A music family whose row names no evaluator gets the gate's "not evaluated" words. The study gets the evaluator's verdict — `passes`, `total`, `floor`, `wrong`, `parts` and the gate's `why` — with `evaluator`, the evaluator's contract `version` and a `source`. The version is `musical_evaluator.VERSION`, bumped in the same change as anything that can move a total or a wrong cadence; it is provenance for the displayed assessment, never part of the material identity and never a hearing. The `source` is `carried` when the item holds a verdict the build persisted (`drill.study.verdict`; no build step writes one yet) and `recomputed` when the projection ran the same gate on the built file, which is every study today, at a cost within the build's noise. The data's top-level `evaluator` names the version the projection recomputes with, and the screen says so when a carried verdict was written under another. Each generated item also carries `requires` (the rules `family_contracts.selected` picks for its recipe) and `missing` (those its measured demands lack). The screen prints `missing` as "Contract requires but the notes lack" and reads no rule's `when` itself. The screen's provenance list prints each fact's `value` beside its kind and `via`, as the record holds it (a promise's `music` or `drill`; a decision's `yes`, `no` or `fix`, with its basis, date and event), and "no decision" for a review dimension nobody has decided, each on its own line. The browser computes no verdict, and "unheard" follows every musical promise.

### Entry 109 — D4a: the transfer offer's relationship written before a transfer-intended run can start — Today keeps the offer it showed, bound to the card by a token the route carries, and navigates only once it is kept; the Score screen reads it before play, pending meaning nothing starts and nothing is stored; the run stores that exact relationship beside the intent, or, where the snapshot does not name the route's offer, opens as practice, says so, and stores neither; `runFacts` unable to make an intent-only fact; `cutIdentity` removed with its case (fix-forward on Entry 106, `docs/prompts/entry-106.md`; the reviewer's required change `docs/review/responses/9193261.md`, the brief's approval `responses/1cbc38a.md`; 2026-09-29)

**Judgement.** Nothing was heard: the offered material (*A blues scale — one octave, thumb under*) is **unverified as music**, as in Entry 106, and D4a claims nothing about it. What I looked at: the stored rows the browser left (`pictures/d4a/*.json`), the Score screen at 342 × 740 with the fallback line (`pictures/d4a/*.png`), and the stored rows the unit harness captured from the real Score screen and Today code (engraver and session stubbed). Against D4's contract — a transfer-intended run records the relationship the offer was made on:

- **After a quick run** (browser, `quick-run-row.json`): opened from the card and played as soon as ▶ was enabled (the input and Wait for me chosen first), through to the summary. The route carried the card's token (`…&offer=<token>`, equal to the card's); the stored row has `intent: 'transfer'` and a `relationship` whose JSON is byte-identical to the card's claim captured before opening (`sameBytes: true`), `role: transfer`, the row's material, no rung. In the unit harness, with the snapshot read held pending, ▶ is disabled, pressing it starts nothing, and a finish forced through the session's callback stores **no row at all**; on D4's code the same forced finish stored a row with `intent: 'transfer'` and no relationship — the race the reviewer named, now a red line.
- **After a run with the history changed** (unit harness only; not observed in the browser): the snapshot written over two proficient reads; two misread reads of the establishing row stored before the opening, so that `relationshipOf` over the stored runs now gives another relationship (asserted in the case; in a probe of the same history the ladder fell below proficient and `shownOn` emptied). The stored run's relationship is the snapshot's, byte for byte, and differs from the recomputation; on D4's code it was the recomputation.
- **After a same-day recomposition** (browser, `stale-route-row.json`, `score-stale-route-342x740.png`): the offer opened (token A), back to Today (the card composed again, token B, the kept offer cleared), the old link opened again. Under the header: *This offer is no longer on today's card; opened as practice.* — two lines, inside the phone's width, not cut (`score-offer-gone-facts.json`), in the header that folds away when the run starts. The run stored with its material and role and **neither `intent` nor `relationship`**.
- **As observations against the rules:** a partial transfer record can no longer be written by application code (the type, the function and the screen each refuse it); a pending read is never a practice run; the fallback is said, in plain words, before anything is played. What it costs the learner: two short lines of header above the music until the run starts, only on a link whose offer is gone. The stricter reading of "recomposed" (every composition is a new offer, not only a different one) means a stale link to an identical offer is also refused, out loud; tapping the card again opens it as the offer.
- **Adjacent, not D4a's:** on the in-app path from Today the two-bar scale is drawn as one small system with most of the stage empty — in D4's merged picture too (`pictures/d4/merged-score-opened-342x740.png`); opened by a link after a load it fills two systems. Recorded below, not investigated.

## The mechanism

**The fault.** D4 set `transferRelationship` from an unawaited `Promise.all([rungRows(), catalogIndex()])` after the score loaded, while ▶ was already live, and passed `intent` to `runFacts` whether or not it had resolved (`ScoreScreen.ts`, D4's 4289–4292 and 3192–3196); `runFacts` wrote the intent alone when the relationship was undefined. So a quick run stored the intent without a relationship, and any run stored a relationship recomputed at opening, not the card's.

**The discriminating tests** (red on D4's code, green now): the pending read with a forced finish (a row with the intent and no relationship → none); the history changed between offer and opening (the recomputation → the snapshot's bytes); the happy path (the relationship stored ≠ the snapshot's → equal).

**The change, on the mechanism:**

1. **Today keeps the offer as shown** (`TodayScreen.open`): the session's own claim — item, skill, the item's material, `relationship`, `contact`, the card's day (`dayKey(now)`) — with the card's offer token, written by `offerSnapshot.writeOfferSnapshot` to one `settings` row (`pianopath.transferOffer`); the route opens only when the write has settled, as `?intent=transfer&skill=…&offer=<token>`. A second tap is ignored.
2. **Bound to the exact offer instance**: a token minted each time the card is composed (and again when the offer's row is swapped away), and every composition or swap clears the kept row (`supersedeOffer`), except after the tap (`leaving`), so a composition already in flight cannot undo the tap's own snapshot.
3. **The read before play** (`ScoreScreen`): started as the screen is built (`loadOffer`), awaited in the load flow before the keys are attached and the bar shown; while it is out the screen is still "Loading…", ▶ is disabled (`render`), `startRun` — the one gate every start passes — starts nothing, and a finish would build no run. `kept` needs the route's token, this item, this skill and today; anything else is a named refusal (`missing`, `superseded`, `other-item`, `other-skill`, `other-day`, `corrupt`, `unreadable`) and the screen shows the line and records practice.
4. **The pair as one fact** (`material.ts`): `RunFacts = MaterialFacts & (TransferFact | NoTransferFact)`, and `runFacts`'s argument the same union; an intent handed in without its relationship (only a cast can) gives no transfer fact at all.

**The builder's calls, each with its reason.** The `settings` store, not `plan`: a key-value row, as the daily read's days are kept; the `plan` store is keyed by `PlanRow.id` and a snapshot is not a plan row. Every recomposition supersedes (the reviewer: "recomposed … or its row swapped away"): a recomposed card is a new decision even on the same item, and the cost is one refused stale link. Two variants of the line, one shown per case: *no longer on today's card* is untrue where the stored value could not be read, so `corrupt`/`unreadable` say *This offer could not be read back; opened as practice.* The line has its own element under the header (`#score-offer-note`, a CSS rule of its own): the header's status line is cut at phone width. The snapshot stores the material and does not match on it (the brief's four conditions). A failed write still opens the route, where the Score screen finds no snapshot and says so.

## Done

1. **The snapshot** (item 1): `app/src/data/offerSnapshot.ts`, one `settings` row, no store and no `DB_VERSION` change; the token minted per composition and per swap of the offer's row, carried by the route, required exactly. Technical: done. Pedagogical: none claimed.
2. **The read before play** (item 2): pending, kept, refused as above; the unawaited `Promise.all` gone, with `rungRows`, `catalogIndex` and `relationshipOf` out of the Score screen's imports.
3. **The regressions and mutants** (item 3): (a)–(f) as the six rows above; the brief's five mutants and three more (`RunFacts-type-widened`, `supersede-skipped`, `leaving-guard-dropped`), all caught on the final tree, each file restored by sha256 (`mutants-final.txt`).
4. **`cutIdentity` removed** (item 4): the function, its comment and the now unused `Identity` import in `excerpt.ts`; its assertion and import in `excerptItems.test.ts`. The import search (`app/src`, `app/tests`, `tools`) found nothing else.
5. **Record** (item 5): the doc rows below, for `docs/04` §2 and `docs/08`.

## Not done

1. **The history-changed case in a browser.** Its evidence is the unit harness on the real Score screen code; a browser version needs misread reads with stored evidence constructed in the page. Not done because the unit case already distinguishes the recomputation from the snapshot on the same code path; a browser run would add the real store and engraver around it.
2. **The pending state in a browser.** A snapshot read that never answers cannot be arranged from a spec without a hook into the store; unit only.
3. **The e2e red is weak**: on D4's app the new case stops at "Today exposes no card to read" (`red/red-e2e-transfer-committed-consumers.txt`), before the route or the row; the discriminating reds are the unit ones.

## Follow-ups (recorded, not fixed)

1. **P2 — rows D4 wrote may carry the intent without the relationship** (the race, between D4's landing and this). `RunHeader` keeps two optionals (`db.ts`, not mine); the day rule reads `intent` alone, which is right; any later reader of `relationship` (G2, the post-E policy) must treat such a row as a transfer-intended run whose relationship is unknown, never as evidence.
2. **P3 — a failed snapshot write says "no longer on today's card"**: Today still opens the route and the Score screen finds nothing; the words are imprecise in that case.
3. **P3 — the snapshot's material is stored, not matched**: an app update between the tap and the opening (same day, same token, no recomposition) would pair the new build's material with the relationship the old build computed.
4. **P? (unclassified) — the Score screen on the in-app path from Today draws the two-bar scale as one small system** with most of the stage empty (D4's merged picture as well as mine); opened by a link after a load it fills two systems. Unverified whether it is a real fit fault or the capture's timing (taken as soon as the SVG draws). Tier 1 if real (biggest undistorted music); for the render owner.

## Questions

None that changes a decision. The stricter supersede (every composition, not only a different offer) is my call per the reviewer's wording; the alternative (supersede only when the offer differs) is a comparison in `supersedeOffer`.

## The mechanism

**What was wrong.** The report measured each rung's claims, and nothing tied the curriculum to it. A rung could name a measurable concept that none of its options practises, and the build warned and went on. The first marker the brief proposed was a lesson's word that a promise is "not yet kept", read only by the validator. The reviewer's objection (`responses/12af708.md`): `taughtAt` is derived from `concepts`, and the gate reads `taughtAt`, so such a marker lets the report pass while the learner's gate still treats the demand as taught.

**The structural marker.** `introduces` sits beside `concepts` in the stage files, and its semantics are fixed across the derivation and every consumer:

- `claims.teaching_rungs` reads `concepts` alone, so an introduced concept never makes its rung a teaching rung.
- `claims.introduced_of` lists it in the report as *introduced*, which is no claim.
- `validate.taught_at_findings` refuses a listed rung that only introduces the demand, even where a `taughtAtNote` reads it by hand.
- The evidence gate's requirement check reads `targetSkills`, so an introduced skill meets no requirement.
- The app reads `taughtAt` and never a lesson's lists.

**The rule the validator holds** (`validate.concept_claim_findings`, over the report's one reading of "establishes"):

- It **fails** where a rung's `concepts` name a measurable skill or demand that no checkable option establishes, where a concept sits in both lists, and where a deferral no longer describes the build.
- It **warns** for each deferral, with its reason, and where an option establishes a concept the rung only introduces: it belongs in `concepts`.
- The 467 claims no detector can measure stay a warning (`rung_claims_warning`).
- This proves the rungs agree with the report, not that either is true (Part 10's permanent rule).

**Discriminating tests.**

- A fixture rung naming a demand its option lacks fails; the same concept under `introduces` passes; the same with an establishing option passes, and under `introduces` it is warned back.
- A fixture path where the earlier rung only introduces a walk leaves a later option untaught; the same rung naming it in `concepts` teaches it. This is checked through the build's derivation and `untaught_on`, and in the app through `taughtAtRung` and the swap sheet.
- A `taughtAt` listing an introducing rung fails even with a hand-reading note.
- A required skill that the rung only introduces, with no declaring option, fails the evidence gate as it did before.
- On the shipped data: `blues.5` is untaught for the walk and `blues.6` taught (red on the committed vocabulary).
- Per claim, the per-bar reading tells a whole-piece artefact from a real absence: blues.5's exercise walks in 0 of 12 bars (no right hand), where blues.6's walks in 11 of 12.

**Placement rule applied, in one line** (the brief's goal: "no option is added to any rung without a current teaching-use decision on its identity"; the dispatch: nothing placed without a current `yes`).

- An option whose notes its rung has not taught was **moved only by leaving that rung**, where a later rung on the same track already lists it and teaches everything it carries.
- The report's other destinations are named per row as proposals (code A in the table) and question 3.
- The practice floor lists items the Stage 1 core rungs already list, none of which D3a's admission holds for a decision: a generated five-finger drill, two runtime drills and the authored steps-and-skips study. D21's three-exercise minimum made a replacement for Hanon necessary.

   - Pedagogically: the two changed lessons say what the rung does. `blues.5` introduces the line hands separately and the next rung puts it under a right hand, which is a common order of teaching a walking bass. That ordering is the curriculum's, read from the notation, and unverified as music.

## Follow-ups

- **P1, curriculum data (L109's data half):** the practice rungs carry no `prerequisites`, so the ancestry model opens each after Stage 0. The floor's steps therefore read as untaught on `practice.1` and `practice.2`, and every Stage 1 practice rung's steps are untaught in the report.
- **P1, detectors (E22 with the density owner):** the walking-bass and left-hand-pattern rules demand every bar of a whole piece, and the walking-bass rule refuses a bar that returns to a pitch. That refuses the root–third–fifth–approach walk the app generates, and a rag's introduction fails the oom-pah. Reading these two demands on a whole piece as a share of bars (as E1's cut rule already reads a passage) would settle question 2 without a curriculum change, and would expose the deferrals as stale.
- **P1, vocabulary (L101):** sixteenths are taught at no rung, so 193 option rows stay untaught wherever they are listed, Hanon among them.
- **P2, an app consumer of `concepts` that `introduces` bypasses:** `rungState.carriedExposures` (`app/src/evidence/rungState.ts`) turns a carried-over rung's `concepts` into exposure events. An exposure is an introduction, exactly what `introduces` means. A learner who carried `blues.5` over from before C5 therefore no longer gets a walking-bass exposure, nor `technique.5`'s syncopation or `latin`'s walking bass (the last two correctly, since those lessons never taught them). The fix is to read `introduces` there too; it is the app's code, not F2's, and it changes no requirement or evidence. `assignSheet`'s default concepts read `concepts` alone as well.
- **P2, the Library sheet (no ids on screen):** the rock placeholders print "What it trains: import-only" and "Tracks: film-game".
- **P2, wording outside my files:** `docs/03` line 72 ("the rock-module and *Beautiful* wish-list songs", E2's file) and `app/src/curriculum/session.ts` line 1562 ("A rock-module song you have not imported") still use the old frame.
- **P2, placement proposals:** the 80 code-A rows are the report's own destinations, ready for a teaching-use decision; `practice.3`–`practice.5` as above.
- **P3:** `theory.9`'s "the only way sight-reading can be practised at all" is an absolute for F3's voice pass. On `practice.1`'s page the rhythm drill's row reads "Hands together" (the runtime drill's `hands` field).

### Entry 113 — Q47: CI fetches the three MAESTRO performances through a verified, cached step, so the converter's real-recording class runs as a gate rather than a skip; a committed one-track fixture puts the hand split under parity on every run; the technique-units test finds the build from its own file (with Q46, 2026-09-29)

**Judgement.** What newly runs in CI once this is pushed, and what it said here:

1. **The converter harness's real-recording class, nine tests** (`TestRealRecordings`, among them *no note is lost or invented between the file and the score*). It skipped on every CI run. Here, on the three performances as the new step extracts them, all nine pass under `CI=1` (`final-harness-ci.txt`). For each of the three recordings the harness observed: notes in the second track; nothing lost, every bar adding up, two parts; the file's own Note-On count equal to the score's struck notes; the independent byte counter agreeing with the reader; not called swung; one braced grand staff; left hand below the right. With the recordings absent the class now **fails under `CI` set** (nine failures, each naming `fetch_maestro.py` and the step "Fetch the MAESTRO test recordings"). On a developer's checkout without them it still **skips** (`red-harness-ci-no-recordings.txt`, `run-harness-no-ci-no-recordings.txt`).
2. **The port's parity on four more references.** `parity_reference.py` now writes eight references: the three recordings, the four committed ones, and the new fixture. `midiParity.test.ts` goes from 38 passed and 4 skipped to 78 passed and 4 skipped. That is 40 newly running cases, ten per new reference. The case *splits the hands the same way* runs and passes on the three recordings and on `one-track-two-hands`. It still skips, by design, on the four references that hold no split (`run-midiParity-eight-references.txt`). Without the recordings the split case still runs, on the fixture alone: `✓ … > one-track-two-hands > splits the hands the same way`. In the before state it ran on nothing (`run-midiParity-fixture-without-recordings.txt` against `before-midiParity-no-recordings-no-fixture.txt`).
3. **The gates around them.** A cache hit is validated, never trusted. Under `CI`, a missing recording now fails the reference writer after it has written the rest; before, the writer exited 0 under `CI=1` with three "skipped, missing" lines (`before-parity-reference-ci.txt`). The writer also refuses the fixture's reference if it holds no split, and removes any earlier reference for it. 27 new tests in the harness step hold these rules, and 17 mutants each turned one red (`red-mutants.txt`).

**The reviewer's worry was real.** The archive's own metadata lists **two** 2011 performances of BWV 885, both titled "Prelude and Fugue in G Minor, WTC II, BWV 885" apart from a double space. A match on composer, title and year alone therefore finds two. Each alias is mapped by member path instead, checked against its metadata row and pinned to the member's SHA256. Those pinned bytes are the main checkout's `build/midi-real/` files: each of the three is byte-identical to its member (`run-compare-with-main-checkout.txt`). So CI will run the harness on exactly the bytes it was built against. Which part of BWV 885 the 45-second performance holds (the metadata's duration; the alias says "prelude") is unverified as music: nothing was heard.

Nothing here reaches a learner's screen. This is tooling, so there is no pedagogical verdict to give. **The CI run itself is unverified until the orchestrator pushes.** That covers the cache miss, then the hit on a second run, and the runner's download.

#### The mapping, as written (`fetch_maestro.PERFORMANCES`; the step's comment lists the same)

| Alias (`build/midi-real/`) | Archive member | Metadata row (composer, title, year) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bach-bwv885-prelude-2011.mid` | `maestro-v3.0.0/2011/MIDI-Unprocessed_22_R1_2011_MID--AUDIO_R1-D8_12_Track12_wav.midi` | Johann Sebastian Bach, "Prelude and Fugue in G Minor, WTC II, BWV 885", 2011 (one of two such rows: the count is in `run-fetch-maestro-real-archive.txt`; the other row's member, `…_20_R1_2011_…_Track02_wav.midi`, was read off the metadata in this session and not captured) |
| `grieg-op38-7-waltz-2014.mid` | `maestro-v3.0.0/2014/MIDI-UNPROCESSED_21-22_R1_2014_MID--AUDIO_21_R1_2014_wav--2.midi` | Edvard Grieg, "Lyric Piece in E Minor, “Waltz,” Op. 38 No. 7", 2014 (unique) |
| `scarlatti-k525-2008.mid` | `maestro-v3.0.0/2008/MIDI-Unprocessed_09_R3_2008_01-07_ORIG_MID--AUDIO_09_R3_2008_wav--2.midi` | Domenico Scarlatti, "Sonata K. 525", 2008 (unique) |

The archive: `maestro-v3.0.0-midi.zip`, SHA256 `70470ee2…dde12c`. That is the publisher's figure, re-read on the dataset's page today. Both fetch runs here verified the downloaded zip against it (exit 0). The archive carries its metadata CSV and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 `LICENSE`.

#### Done

- **The fetch** (`tools/midi-cleanup/tests/fetch_maestro.py`, new; standard library only). It verifies the archive's SHA256 before opening it. Each alias must match exactly one metadata row by member path, and that row must name the expected composer, work and year. A member listed zero or several times, absent from the archive, empty, or with other bytes than the pinned SHA256 fails, and nothing is written. Only then are exactly three files and `SOURCE.md` written. `SOURCE.md` carries the members and aliases, the version, the archive's checksum, the licence sentence verbatim with the page's URL and the licence's, the citation the dataset asks for with the version, and the date. `--cache-hit true` validates and never downloads: the three files present, non-empty and with the pinned bytes, and `SOURCE.md` naming each alias, member and the checksum. The script's own download path was run once here too (`run-fetch-maestro-download.txt`). It and the `--archive` run both passed the pinned member checksums, so they wrote the same bytes. The zip was then deleted, and only the three files and `SOURCE.md` are kept in the worktree's `build/midi-real/`.
- **The workflow** (`ci.yml`), before "MIDI converter harness", has three steps:
  - "Restore the MAESTRO test recordings": `actions/cache/restore@v4`, keyed by the archive's SHA256 plus a hash of `fetch_maestro.py`.
  - "Fetch the MAESTRO test recordings": runs the script with the restore's `cache-hit`.
  - "Save the MAESTRO test recordings": `actions/cache/save@v4`, only after a fetch that passed.

  The comment carries the licence quoted, the citation and version, and the three member paths. The harness step's comment and the parity step's comment now say what they do. **Deviation 1:** restore, fetch and save as three steps rather than one `actions/cache` step. Two reasons: the combined action saves at the job's end, so a later red step would send the next run back to the download; and the only `actions/cache@` step stays unique, which `test_ci_order` asserts. **Deviation 2:** the key carries the script's hash as well as the checksum, so a changed mapping or check fetches afresh instead of failing validation on an older cache.
- **The skip site** (`test_converter.py`). The class decorator became a `setUp` that skips when `CI` is unset and fails when it is set. The developer behaviour is the same; the rule is read at run time so `TestTheRealRecordingsGate` can hold it with the files made absent. The reason drops "not redistributable" and "no CI step fetches them", and now names the script, the step and the licence. The module docstring's paragraph on real input is brought level.
- **The reference writer** (`parity_reference.py`). `APP_FIXTURES` became (path from the root, must split). The new fixture lives outside `app/tests/fixtures/imports`, so `fixtureFrom` is derived from each path, and `midiParity.test.ts` needed no code change. What now fails:
  - A missing committed fixture, anywhere. **Deviation 3:** the brief spoke of real inputs only, but a missing fixture would silently skip the split assertion; this is Q24's committed-input rule.
  - A missing recording under `CI`, after the rest is written.
  - A must-split fixture whose reference holds none. Any earlier reference for it is removed, so the parity test cannot read a stale one.

  Developers still see "skipped, missing" for a recording, now naming the script.
- **The fixture** (`tools/midi-cleanup/tests/fixtures/make-one-track-two-hands-midi.py` and its `one-track-two-hands.mid`). A conductor track and one note track. Four bars in C, I–IV–V–I, at 90 bpm. The right hand plays half notes above a left-hand line that climbs through middle C to D4. Two runs wrote identical bytes (`fixture-sha-first.txt`, `fixture-sha-second.txt`, `cmp` exit 0). The Python split puts all 8 right-hand and all 14 left-hand notes where the script's table puts them. Its boundary moves from 56 to 68, so a fixed middle-C boundary would have given the left hand's C4 and D4 to the right (`probe-fixture-split.txt`). The port agrees on all ten cases for it. That the texture is idiomatic is unverified as music: nothing was heard.
- **The path** (`test_technique_units.py`). The test reads `common.BUILD_DIR`. From `tools/content/tests/` it was red on the committed code (4 failed, naming `…\tools\content\tests\build\catalog.generated.json`) and is green now. Without the catalogue it fails naming the repository's `build\` path.
- **`test_ci_order.py`** (outside the brief's file list; no other builder owns it). It is the file that holds the step names the gated messages cite, so `CITED` gains the fetch step. A new test holds restore → fetch → save, and fetch before the harness and before the parity reference.
- **`midiParity.test.ts`, two comments only.** They said no committed fixture is split and that the tests skip without the reference; this change made the first false, and Q24 had already made the second false.
- **`docs/00-overview.md`**: D27, beside D23. It records the licence quoted, the citation with the version, the test-only use and where it lives, and that any use beyond testing is a new decision. The licence's own sentence names its publisher and is quoted verbatim, as the brief requires. No AI model or assistant vendor is named anywhere.

### Entry 112 — G1: one factual encounter model — what this learner met, as small durable rows beside the runs (`encounters`: viewed once a visit, heard, demonstrated; `DB_VERSION` 8, no other store touched), the runs staying the record of runs and every run the sessions cap deletes folded first into a durable, evidence-free summary per material (`contacts`), one query over the three (`encounterStore.familiarity`: per facet the most recent time or null, passage by passage, an excerpt's bars in its parent's, the composition beside), sight-reading's first contact derived from that history and a visit id instead of a per-visit flag, the same fact written on every notated, excerpt and import run, an import its stored bytes, D4's contact saying how it was met (2026-09-29)

**Judgement.** Nothing was heard: the phrases read here are generated sight-reading phrases, **unverified as music**, and G1 claims nothing about them. What I looked at: the Progress history line and the summary sheet at 342 × 740 after today's phrase was played to the learner at noon and read in the evening (`pictures/g1/progress-history-342x740.png`, `summary-heard-at-noon-342x740.png`, the DOM and stored rows in `pictures/g1/facts.json`), the stored rows of the unit harness, and the code.

- **What the history line says after a phrase was heard earlier** (observed, the probe on G1's app): the row reads *Sight-reading generator, level 1 · 2026-09-29 23:00 · Keep tempo* over **100% at 70% · not first sight · 0 min**, the meta line whole inside its row (`metaFitsTheRow: true`: its `scrollWidth` within its `clientWidth`). The sheet over the run: **Run finished**, then *Sight-reading counts only on music you have not heard — this run is kept as practice.*, and under *Not judged*, *Sight-reading — it counts only on music you have not seen or heard*. The store: one run, `unseen: false`; three encounters — the noon visit's `viewed` and `demonstrated`, the evening visit's `viewed`, each with its visit id and its source (`today`, `daily-read`, rung 1.5).
- **Heard the day before** gives the same line and the same stored fact: first contact compares visits, never days (the harness's *heard, left, returned later* case stores `unseen: false` and the history helper prints *not first sight*). The browser case and the picture use noon and evening of one day because a day later Today's card carries the next day's phrase, and the brief's adversary is that one.
- **Before G1** (HEAD's app, the red of the new browser case): the same evening run was stored `unseen: true` — a first reading of a phrase heard at noon — so by `historyDetail`'s rule its line carried no flag, the reading was evidence, and the day's read was ticked by it (inferred from the stored flag and the code; HEAD's line was not captured as a picture).
- **As observations against the rules:** the record now says what happened; a perfect reading of music already heard does not count as sight-reading and the learner is told why, once, on the sheet, and again on the history line. What it costs: **today's phrase opened and left, or reloaded, before it was played can no longer be the day's read** — the rule the brief and the reviewer set (a viewing on another visit is prior contact) — and Today's card still offers it as unread, because the card reads runs only (Follow-ups 1; X's L32 recheck). The sheet says why and offers *New phrase*.
- **Adjacent, not G1's:** the history's time label is the UTC hour — *23:00* for a run at 19:00 local — because `ProgressScreen.drawHistory` prints `session.at` sliced as text (Follow-ups 2).

## The mechanism

**The fault.** The Score screen remembered a hearing for the visit only (`phraseHeard`) and stored nothing; `unseen` was decided per visit from the seeds on record and that flag; a notated piece or an import carried no first-contact fact; the only "seen" in the store was the flag on generated runs. And the sessions cap could delete the run that was the only proof an item was met (G63; the reviewer's constraint on D4).

**The discriminating tests** (red on the committed code, green now): a phrase demonstrated on one visit and read on the next is stored `unseen: false` (was `true`: the e2e red, and the unit harness's 14 of 15 cases red with HEAD's Score screen); a practised passage pruned by the real cap is still practised, and contact still `met` (the `prune-folds-nothing` mutant turns it red); a piece played again stays passed and meets its rung (red with HEAD's rung state).

**The change, on the mechanism:**

1. **The store** (`db.ts`): `DB_VERSION` 8 creates `encounters` (keyPath `id` = `<visit>:<n>`, indexed `byKey` on the material's key and `byItem`) and `contacts` (keyPath the material's key); the upgrade touches no other store (the version-7 fixture's every store, rows and keys, deep-equal before and after). Both stores are in `STORE_NAMES`, so the backup carries them; a merge restore puts encounters by id (restoring twice adds nothing) and joins summaries.
2. **The summary before deletion** (`progressStore.pruneSessions`): the one transaction now spans `sessions` and `contacts`; each run the cap deletes is folded (`foldRun`) into its material's summary (`mergeSummaries`, a join: first the earlier, last the later, ids and sources as sets), keyed by the material or, for a run that knew none, by the id with `byId: true`. Only the projection is kept: material or id, item ids, and per span `practised` or `performed`, the printed bars, first, last, sources — never evidence, accuracy or a verdict.
3. **The query** (`encounterStore.ts`): `familiarityIn(target, history, { visit })` and `familiarity(target)` over the store — facts from encounter rows, live runs (`rungRows`) and summaries; matched by material (D4's `sameMaterial`; `materialKey` agrees with it), by id where the row knew no material and the target's id names its material (never for a runtime phrase), or through the catalogue's hierarchy (an excerpt's bars normalised into its parent's by `fromBar`); covered → the facet, touched only → `partly`; the composition facet over every item of `provenance.composition`.
4. **The Score screen** (`ScoreScreen.ts`): a visit id minted as the screen opens; the material a run plays computed once (`material.playedMaterial`: the phrase's identity, an import's loaded bytes, the row's); the history read beside the engraving and awaited before play; a viewing written where the notation is first drawn (never in Blind); a playback written by the learner's action; `unseen` derived at the summary (phrase whole; anything else over the bars the run covered) and read again before storing (`confirmFirstContact`), which only ever turns a first contact into none and, for a reading, says so on the sheet.
5. **The first-contact fact on every run, and its readers scoped** (`db.isPhraseRun`): see Questions 1.

## The query's table (`familiarityIn`; `encounterModel.test.ts`)

| History | Asked | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing | the piece | every facet null, `byId: false`, `partly` null, `composition` null facets |
| a viewing (another visit) | the piece | `viewed` at, the rest null — viewed, not practised |
| *Play it to me* | the piece | `heard` at, `demonstrated` null |
| *Hear it* | the piece | `heard` and `demonstrated` at (heard is the superset, explicitly) |
| a run (no evidence, or not measured and answered, or `unseen: false`) | the piece | `attempted`, `practised` at |
| a performance take | the piece | `attempted`, `performed` at; `practised` null |
| a run over bars 1–8 | bars 1–8 / 3–5 | `practised` at |
| a run over bars 1–8 | bars 25–32 | null, `partly` null |
| a run over bars 1–8 | bars 5–12 / the whole | `practised` null, `partly.practised` at |
| a bar held down (bar 3) | bar 3 | `demonstrated` at |
| the whole piece played | its excerpt bars 25–32 | `practised` at |
| excerpt A (bars 1–8) played | excerpt B (25–32) | nothing, `partly` nothing |
| excerpt A played | the whole piece / bars 2–6 | `partly.practised` / `practised` at |
| excerpt C (5–12) | beside A | `partly.practised` |
| bars 2–3 of excerpt B's own score | the parent's 26–27 / 25–26 | `practised` at / null |
| the piece practised over 25–32 | excerpt B / excerpt A | `practised` at / nothing |
| another arrangement heard (same `provenance.composition`) | this arrangement | notation facets null, `viewed` null; `composition.heard` at |
| the same, target naming no composition, or no catalogue | — | `composition: null` (unknown, never manufactured) |
| a run with no material (legacy) or `none`, same id | the piece | `attempted`, `practised`, `byId: true` |
| a run of other known material, same id | the piece | nothing, `byId: false` |
| a legacy run of a reading row | a phrase of it | nothing — a row id names a recipe, every seed other material |
| a viewing of this visit | asked by this visit / another | null / at |
| a pruned run's summary over bars 1–8 | bars 1–8 / 25–32 | `attempted`, `practised` at / null |
